lines.en: Did she mention anything about her plans?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Comentó que quería quedarse allí varios años.
lines.en: She mentioned that she wanted to stay there for several years.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y admitió que echaba de menos esta ciudad?
lines.en: And did she admit that she missed this city?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, al final lo admitió, un poco triste.
lines.en: Yes, in the end she admitted it, a bit sadly.

days.title: Una historia de vida
days.objective: The learner can narrate a whole invented life across the four past tenses, the way a biography naturally moves between habits, single events, background and earlier facts.
days.paretoFocus: A biography forces every past tense to work together in one coherent text, which is exactly the skill this block has been building toward.
drills: Read the biography aloud and mark which past tense each verb uses.
Write three sentences about your own life using the four past tenses.
Retell the biography from memory in your own words.

items: Recall the connectors de pequeño and cuando tenía... años.
Recall the absolute superlative with -ísimo.
Recall the relative pronoun que in a restrictive clause.

activities.title: La vida de Lucía Fernández
activities.intro: This invented biography moves through all four past tenses: the indefinido for the single events of a life, the imperfecto for childhood habits and background, the pluscuamperfecto for what had already happened, and the perfecto for what connects to now.

items.hr: Lucía Fernández Ortiz nació en Salamanca en 1985.
items.en: Lucía Fernández Ortiz was born in Salamanca in 1985.
items.note: indefinido: a single, dated event

items.hr: De pequeña, siempre dibujaba en cualquier papel que encontraba.
items.en: As a child, she always used to draw on any paper she could find.
items.note: imperfecto: a childhood habit

items.hr: Cuando tenía dieciocho años, se mudó a Bilbao para estudiar Bellas Artes.
items.en: When she was eighteen, she moved to Bilbao to study Fine Arts.
items.note: imperfecto for the age, indefinido for the single event of moving

items.hr: Ya había terminado la carrera cuando consiguió su primer trabajo en un estudio de diseño.
items.en: She had already finished her degree when she got her first job at a design studio.
items.note: pluscuamperfecto: earlier than the indefinido event consiguió

items.hr: Esta semana ha inaugurado su tercera exposición en la ciudad.
items.en: This week she has opened her third exhibition in the city.
items.note: perfecto: connects to the present through esta semana

activities.title: La biografía de Lucía
activities.intro: Practise choosing the right past tense across a whole narrated life.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase describe correctamente un hábito de la infancia de Lucía?
options: De pequeña, siempre dibujaba en cualquier papel.
De pequeña, siempre dibujó en cualquier papel.
De pequeña, siempre ha dibujado en cualquier papel.
De pequeña, siempre había dibujado en cualquier papel.
questions.answer: De pequeña, siempre dibujaba en cualquier papel.
questions.explanation: The imperfecto dibujaba is the tense for a repeated childhood habit, not a single event or something connected to now.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase indica correctamente que algo ya había pasado antes de otro momento?
options: Ya había terminado la carrera cuando consiguió el trabajo.
Ya terminó la carrera cuando consiguió el trabajo.
Ya terminaba la carrera cuando consiguió el trabajo.
Ya ha terminado la carrera cuando consiguió el trabajo.
questions.answer: Ya había terminado la carrera cuando consiguió el trabajo.
questions.explanation: había terminado (pluscuamperfecto) marks finishing her degree as earlier than consiguió, the reference point in the past.

questions.prompt: Completa: Lucía Fernández Ortiz ______ en Salamanca en 1985. (nacer, indefinido)
questions.explanation: nació is the indefinido, the single dated event of her birth.

questions.prompt: Completa: Esta semana ______ su tercera exposición. (inaugurar, ella, perfecto)
questions.explanation: ha inaugurado (perfecto) connects the event to the present through esta semana.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'When she was eighteen, she moved to Bilbao to study Fine Arts.'
questions.explanation: tenía (imperfecto) gives her age, and se mudó (indefinido) is the single event of moving.

activities.title: Hablando de la exposición
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends discuss the invented artist's new exhibition and what they know of her life.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has visto la nueva exposición de Lucía Fernández?
lines.en: Have you seen Lucía Fernández's new exhibition?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Todavía no, pero he leído que la ha inaugurado esta semana.
lines.en: Not yet, but I've read that she has opened it this week.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Sabías que de pequeña ya dibujaba todo el tiempo?
lines.en: Did you know that as a child she already used to draw all the time?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No lo sabía. ¿Y estudió Bellas Artes aquí?
lines.en: I didn't know that. And did she study Fine Arts here?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No, se mudó a Bilbao cuando tenía dieciocho años.
lines.en: No, she moved to Bilbao when she was eighteen.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Qué interesante. ¿Y ya había terminado la carrera cuando empezó a trabajar?
lines.en: How interesting. And had she already finished her degree when she started working?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sí, consiguió su primer trabajo justo después.
lines.en: Yes, she got her first job right after.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pues quiero ir a ver la exposición este fin de semana.
lines.en: Well, I want to go see the exhibition this weekend.

days.title: Noticias y sucesos
days.objective: The learner can read and produce a short news item in its own register, using the perfecto for fresh news, the pluscuamperfecto for background and reported speech for what an official said.
days.paretoFocus: News writing has its own grammar habits: fresh facts in the perfecto, older context in the pluscuamperfecto and officials always reported with que, and recognising this pattern makes real news readable.
drills: Read the news item aloud and mark the perfecto, pluscuamperfecto and reported clauses.
Write two sentences of invented local news using the perfecto.
Report one official statement using dijo que + the correct tense shift.

items: Recall the impersonal se in a rule or sign.
Recall the connector según for citing a source.
Recall the future of probability for a guess.

activities.title: El Diario de Puentenuevo informa
activities.intro: News register mixes tenses on purpose: perfecto covers what just broke, pluscuamperfecto fills in older background, and reported speech carries whatever a source or official is quoted as saying. From this level onward, the course's reading material may also show American Spanish, always paired here with its peninsular counterpart.

items.hr: Esta mañana el ayuntamiento de Puentenuevo ha anunciado el cierre temporal del puente principal.
items.en: This morning Puentenuevo's town council announced the temporary closure of the main bridge.
items.note: perfecto: fresh news, connected to today

items.hr: El puente, que ya había sufrido daños en una tormenta anterior, necesita reparaciones urgentes.
items.en: The bridge, which had already suffered damage in an earlier storm, needs urgent repairs.
items.note: pluscuamperfecto: older background information

items.hr: El alcalde declaró que las obras terminarían en dos semanas.
items.en: The mayor stated that the works would finish in two weeks.
items.note: reported speech: futuro shifts to condicional

items.hr: Según Radio Puentenuevo, cientos de vecinos ya han firmado una petición pidiendo más información.
items.en: According to Radio Puentenuevo, hundreds of residents have already signed a petition asking for more information.
items.note: según introduces the source of the information

items.hr: La noticia preocupa también a los turistas: muchos ya habían comprado el boleto de tren, que en España se llama el billete, para pasar por la zona esta semana.
items.en: The news also worries tourists: many had already bought their train ticket, called billete in Spain, to pass through the area this week.
items.note: boleto is the American form, paired here with the peninsular billete

activities.title: Leyendo la noticia
activities.intro: Practise the news register: perfecto for fresh facts, pluscuamperfecto for background, reported speech for officials.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase da correctamente el contexto anterior de una noticia?
options: El puente ya había sufrido daños antes.
El puente ya sufre daños antes.
El puente ya ha sufrido daños antes.
El puente ya sufriría daños antes.
questions.answer: El puente ya había sufrido daños antes.
questions.explanation: The pluscuamperfecto había sufrido gives background from before the main reported event, the classic use of this tense in news writing.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase reporta correctamente la declaración del alcalde?
options: Declaró que las obras terminarían en dos semanas.
Declaró que las obras terminar en dos semanas.
Declaró que las obras terminaban en dos semanas.
Declaró que las obras terminaron en dos semanas ya.
questions.answer: Declaró que las obras terminarían en dos semanas.
questions.explanation: The mayor's original future (terminarán) shifts to the conditional terminarían because the reporting verb declaró is in the past; the other options use an ungrammatical bare infinitive, the imperfecto, or an odd indefinido-plus-ya combination.

questions.prompt: Completa: Esta mañana el ayuntamiento ______ el cierre del puente. (anunciar, perfecto)
questions.explanation: ha anunciado (perfecto) is the tense for fresh news connected to esta mañana.

questions.prompt: Completa: ______ Radio Puentenuevo, cientos de vecinos han firmado la petición. (according to)
questions.explanation: Según introduces the source a news item is citing.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The mayor stated that the works would finish in two weeks.'
questions.explanation: declaró que introduces the reported clause, and terminarían is the conditional shift of the mayor's original future.

activities.title: Comentando la noticia
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two neighbours discuss the bridge closure reported in the local news.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has leído la noticia del puente en el diario?
lines.en: Have you read the bridge news in the paper?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, dicen que ya había sufrido daños antes de esta tormenta.
lines.en: Yes, they say it had already suffered damage before this storm.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cuánto tiempo van a tardar en arreglarlo?
lines.en: And how long are they going to take to fix it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: El alcalde declaró que las obras terminarían en dos semanas.
lines.en: The mayor stated that the works would finish in two weeks.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Eso espero de verdad, lo necesitamos para ir al trabajo.
lines.en: I really hope so, we need it to get to work.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Según la radio, mucha gente ya ha firmado una petición.
lines.en: According to the radio, a lot of people have already signed a petition.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo también la firmaré esta tarde.
lines.en: I'll sign it too this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Buena idea, seguro que mucha gente más la firmará.
lines.en: Good idea, I'm sure a lot more people will sign it.

days.title: Consolidación: narrar y reportar
days.objective: The learner can move between the four past tenses and reported speech, with its tense shift, in one connected piece of narration, with no new grammar in this lesson.
days.paretoFocus: Putting narration and reported speech together under pressure is what actually locks in a block this dense; a mixed review does more here than a new rule would.
drills: Retell a short story mixing direct and reported speech.
Report three statements from the block using three different verbs of saying.
Correct three deliberately wrong sentences from this block.

items: Recall the tense shift table: presente to imperfecto, perfecto/indefinido to pluscuamperfecto, futuro to condicional.
Recall preguntó si versus preguntó plus a question word.
Recall the variety of reporting verbs: contar, explicar, comentar, añadir and admitir.

activities.title: Repaso: narrar y reportar
activities.intro: No new grammar here. This lesson pulls together the pluscuamperfecto, the full past system and reported speech, in both statements and questions, from this whole block.

items.hr: Cuando la llamé, ya había salido de casa, así que quedamos para el día siguiente.
items.en: When I called her, she had already left home, so we arranged to meet the next day.
items.note: pluscuamperfecto plus indefinido, ordering two past events

items.hr: Me dijo que estaba muy ocupada esa semana.
items.en: She told me she was very busy that week.
items.note: presente shifted to imperfecto

items.hr: Añadió que había terminado el proyecto el día anterior.
items.en: She added that she had finished the project the day before.
items.note: indefinido shifted to pluscuamperfecto

items.hr: Preguntó si podríamos vernos el sábado en vez del viernes.
items.en: She asked if we could meet on Saturday instead of Friday.
items.note: reported yes/no question with si

items.hr: Comentó que vendría con su hermana, si consigue el billete a tiempo.
items.en: She mentioned that she would come with her sister, if she gets the ticket in time.
items.note: futuro shifted to condicional; the si clause keeps the present because the condition is still open when the report is made

activities.title: Repaso de narración y reportaje
activities.intro: A mixed review across the whole block: the past system and reported speech.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase ordena correctamente dos sucesos del pasado?
options: Cuando la llamé, ya había salido de casa.
Cuando la llamé, ya salía de casa.
Cuando la llamé, ya sale de casa.
Cuando la llamé, ya ha salido de casa.
questions.answer: Cuando la llamé, ya había salido de casa.
questions.explanation: había salido (pluscuamperfecto) places her leaving before the indefinido llamé, the reference point in the past.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase reporta correctamente una pregunta de sí o no?
options: Preguntó si podríamos vernos el sábado.
Preguntó que podríamos vernos el sábado.
Preguntó si podría vernos el sábado.
questions.answer: Preguntó si podríamos vernos el sábado.
questions.explanation: si introduces a reported yes/no question, and podríamos is the conditional shift of the original future podremos; que and a missing si are both wrong, and podría wrongly drops the plural nosotros ending needed for vernos (we could see each other).

questions.prompt: Completa: Me ______ que estaba muy ocupada esa semana. (decir, ella, indefinido)
questions.explanation: dijo is the indefinido of decir, the ordinary verb for reporting a single statement.

questions.prompt: Completa: Añadió que ______ el proyecto el día anterior. (terminar, ella, pluscuamperfecto)
questions.explanation: había terminado (pluscuamperfecto) reports a finished action, shifted back from the original indefinido or perfecto.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'She mentioned that she would come with her sister.'
questions.explanation: Comentó que introduces the reported clause, and vendría is the conditional shift of the original future vendré.

activities.title: Repasando la semana
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends recap a busy week of messages and plans, mixing narration and reported speech.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Al final hablaste con Elena sobre el sábado?
lines.en: Did you end up talking to Elena about Saturday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, cuando la llamé, ya había salido de casa, pero hablamos un rato.
lines.en: Yes, when I called her, she had already left home, but we talked for a bit.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y qué te dijo?
lines.en: And what did she tell you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me dijo que estaba muy ocupada esa semana con el trabajo.
lines.en: She told me she was very busy that week with work.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Preguntó algo sobre el plan?
lines.en: Did she ask anything about the plan?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, preguntó si podríamos vernos el sábado en vez del viernes.
lines.en: Yes, she asked if we could meet on Saturday instead of Friday.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y vendrá con alguien más?
lines.en: And will she come with anyone else?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Comentó que vendría con su hermana, si consigue el billete a tiempo.
lines.en: She mentioned she would come with her sister, if she gets the ticket in time.

days.title: El subjuntivo presente: la forma
days.objective: The learner can build the present subjunctive of regular verbs from the yo-form of the present, and recognises that the usted imperative already known from A2 was this form all along.
days.paretoFocus: Learning the form on its own, before any of its uses, means the uses that start soon will only need new rules, not a new set of endings to memorise as well.
drills: Turn five yo-present forms into their subjunctive equivalent out loud.
Say the usted and ustedes commands you already know and name which verb they come from.
Write the full subjunctive paradigm of hablar, comer and vivir.

items: Recall the usted and ustedes imperative forms from A2.
Recall the irregular participle escrito.
Recall the peninsular perfecto marker todavía no.

activities.title: Cómo se forma el subjuntivo presente
activities.intro: This lesson covers only the shape of the present subjunctive for regular verbs; its uses start a few lessons from now. The trick: start from yo, in the present tense, strip the final -o, and add the opposite vowel's endings. -ar verbs take e-type endings, -er and -ir verbs take a-type endings.

items.hr: El truco es quitar la -o de la forma yo del presente y añadir la vocal contraria: hablo se convierte en hable, como se convierte en coma, vivo se convierte en viva.
items.en: The trick is to take the -o off the yo-form of the present and add the opposite vowel: hablo becomes hable, como becomes coma, vivo becomes viva.

items.hr: Hable usted más despacio, por favor.
items.en: Speak more slowly, please.
items.note: hable is exactly the usted command you already know from A2

items.hr: Coma usted algo antes de salir de casa.
items.en: Eat something before you leave home.
items.note: -er and -ir verbs take the endings normally associated with -ar verbs, the opposite-vowel swap: coma, viva

items.hr: Escriban ustedes su nombre en la primera línea, por favor.
items.en: Write your name on the first line, please.
items.note: ustedes: the same subjunctive stem, with the plural ending -an

items.hr: Por eso el imperativo de usted que aprendiste en el nivel anterior era, en realidad, el subjuntivo presente.
items.en: That's why the usted imperative you learned in the previous level was, in fact, the present subjunctive.

activities.title: Formando el subjuntivo presente
activities.intro: Strip the final -o from the yo-form and add the subjunctive's opposite-vowel ending.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta del subjuntivo presente de 'hablar' para 'yo'?
questions.explanation: The subjunctive is built from the yo-form hablo: drop the -o and add the opposite-vowel ending -e.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase es un mandato formal de 'usted', construido con la misma forma que el subjuntivo?
options: Coma usted algo antes de salir.
Come usted algo antes de salir.
Comió usted algo antes de salir.
Comía usted algo antes de salir.
questions.answer: Coma usted algo antes de salir.
questions.explanation: coma is built from como minus -o plus -a, the same process that builds the present subjunctive; the other options are present, indefinido and imperfecto, not the subjunctive-based command.

questions.prompt: Completa la transformación: vivo -> ______ (subjuntivo presente, yo)
questions.explanation: vivo drops its -o and adds -a, the ending -ir verbs share with -er verbs in the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa el mandato formal: ______ ustedes su nombre aquí, por favor. (escribir, subjuntivo, ustedes)
questions.explanation: escribo drops its -o and adds -an for the ustedes form, the same stem used as the ustedes imperative.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Speak more slowly, please.'
questions.explanation: Hable is the usted command, built exactly like the present subjunctive from hablo.

activities.title: En la consulta del médico
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A patient realises, mid-checkup, that the usted commands the doctor uses are actually the present subjunctive.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Respire hondo, por favor.
lines.en: Breathe deeply, please.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¿Así, doctor?
lines.en: Like this, doctor?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sí, muy bien. Ahora abra la boca un momento.
lines.en: Yes, very good. Now open your mouth for a moment.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale. Oiga, 'abra' es del verbo abrir, ¿verdad?
lines.en: Okay. Hey, 'abra' is from the verb abrir, right?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Exacto. Y es la misma forma que el subjuntivo presente.
lines.en: Exactly. And it's the same form as the present subjunctive.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ah, ¡por eso me suena tan parecido a lo que aprendí antes!
lines.en: Ah, that's why it sounds so similar to what I learned before!

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Claro, usted ya conocía esta forma sin saberlo.
lines.en: Of course, you already knew this form without realizing it.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Qué curioso. Muchas gracias, doctor.
lines.en: How curious. Thank you very much, doctor.

days.title: El subjuntivo: los cambios heredados del indicativo
days.objective: The learner can form the present subjunctive of stem-changing verbs, including the extra nosotros/vosotros change in -ir verbs.
days.paretoFocus: Almost every high-frequency verb the learner already knows is either stem-changing or has an irregular yo-form ending in -go, so these two patterns govern most subjunctive sentences from here on.
drills: Write the six present subjunctive forms of cerrar, pedir and dormir.
Say aloud three wishes using ojalá with a stem-changing verb.
Write one sentence with durmamos and one with pidáis.
Write the six present subjunctive forms of tener and salir.

items: Recall the opposite-vowel rule for building the present subjunctive from the yo-form.
Remember why the usted imperative was secretly a subjunctive all along.
Recall the six subjunctive endings for an -ar verb.

activities.title: Cambios heredados
activities.intro: Verbs that change their stem in the present indicative keep the same change in the present subjunctive. -ir verbs with an e-ie, e-i or o-ue change also get a change in nosotros and vosotros, taken from the gerund stem: e becomes i (pidamos, sintamos) and o becomes u (durmamos). And every irregular yo-form is inherited too, not just stem changes: the g-verbs (tengo, salgo, hago, pongo, digo, vengo, oigo) build their whole subjunctive on that same irregular stem.

items.hr: Espero que cierres la puerta.
items.en: I hope you close the door.
items.note: cerrar (e-ie): cierro -> cierre, cierres, cierre, cerremos, cerréis, cierren

items.hr: Quiero que pidas la cuenta.
items.en: I want you to ask for the bill.
items.note: pedir (e-i) changes in every single form: pido -> pida, pidas, pida, pidamos, pidáis, pidan

items.hr: Es mejor que durmamos temprano esta noche.
items.en: It's better that we sleep early tonight.
items.note: dormir (o-ue) has a second change in nosotros: duermo -> duerma, but dormimos -> durmamos

items.hr: Ojalá que os divirtáis en la fiesta.
items.en: I hope you all have fun at the party.
items.note: ojalá (I hope, if only) always triggers the subjunctive; divertirse (e-ie) shifts to i in nosotros/vosotros: os divertís -> os divirtáis

items.hr: No creo que vuelvas a tiempo.
items.en: I don't think you'll be back on time.
items.note: volver (o-ue): vuelvo -> vuelva, vuelvas, vuelva, volvamos, volváis, vuelvan

items.hr: Muchos verbos con la yo-forma irregular en -go mantienen esa misma irregularidad en el subjuntivo: tengo se convierte en tenga, salgo en salga, hago en haga, pongo en ponga, digo en diga, vengo en venga y oigo en oiga.
items.en: Many verbs with an irregular yo-form ending in -go keep that same irregularity in the subjunctive: tengo becomes tenga, salgo becomes salga, hago becomes haga, pongo becomes ponga, digo becomes diga, vengo becomes venga, and oigo becomes oiga.
items.note: same trick as always: drop the -o and add the opposite-vowel ending to the irregular stem

items.hr: Espero que tengas tiempo de venir a la fiesta.
items.en: I hope you have time to come to the party.
items.note: tener: tengo -> tenga, tengas, tenga, tengamos, tengáis, tengan

items.hr: Ojalá que salga todo bien esta noche.
items.en: I hope everything goes well tonight.
items.note: salir: salgo -> salga, salgas, salga, salgamos, salgáis, salgan

activities.title: Practicando los cambios
activities.intro: Practise the stem changes a present subjunctive verb inherits from the indicative.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma de nosotros del verbo dormir en presente de subjuntivo?
questions.explanation: dormir takes its secondary change from the gerund stem in nosotros/vosotros, o to u, unlike the simple o-ue of the other persons.

questions.prompt: Elige la forma correcta: Quiero que tú te ______ antes de salir. (vestirse)
questions.explanation: vestirse (e-i) changes in every person of the present subjunctive, not just in nosotros/vosotros.

questions.prompt: Completa: Espero que ellos ______ (pedir) ayuda si la necesitan.
questions.explanation: pedir changes e to i in every form of the present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ojalá que nosotros nos ______ (sentir) mejor mañana.
questions.explanation: sentir shows e to i in nosotros/vosotros of the subjunctive, unlike the e-ie of the other persons.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I want us to sleep early.'
questions.explanation: dormir's nosotros subjunctive form takes u, not the ue of dormir's other persons.

questions.prompt: Completa: Espero que (tú) ______ (tener) tiempo mañana.
questions.explanation: tener keeps its irregular yo-stem teng- in the subjunctive, the same way any other yo-form irregularity is inherited.

activities.title: Cerrando la tienda
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two coworkers close up a shop and decide what to do next, using stem-changing subjunctives.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿A qué hora prefieres que cerremos la tienda hoy?
lines.en: What time do you prefer we close the shop today?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Prefiero que la cerremos a las ocho, no antes.
lines.en: I prefer we close it at eight, not earlier.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vale. ¿Quieres que pida algo de comer para los dos?
lines.en: Okay. Do you want me to order some food for both of us?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, quiero que pidas ensalada para mí, por favor.
lines.en: Yes, I want you to order me a salad, please.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Es necesario que durmamos aquí esta noche?
lines.en: Is it necessary that we sleep here tonight?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No creo que durmamos aquí, mejor volvemos a casa.
lines.en: I don't think we'll sleep here, better we go home.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Entonces espero que vuelvas pronto mañana.
lines.en: Then I hope you're back soon tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ojalá que todo salga bien y podamos descansar.
lines.en: I hope everything goes well and we can rest.

days.title: Los seis irregulares del subjuntivo
days.objective: The learner can produce the six genuinely irregular present subjunctives: ser, estar, ir, dar, saber, haber.
days.paretoFocus: These six verbs cannot be derived from any rule, and several of them (ser, estar, ir) appear in almost every subjunctive sentence a learner will ever build.
drills: Write the full conjugation of sea, esté, vaya, dé, sepa and haya.
Say aloud one wish using ojalá with each of the six irregulars.
Write a sentence contrasting dé with the preposition de.

items: Recall the opposite-vowel rule for building the subjunctive, from two lessons ago.
Remember how dormir and pedir change in the present subjunctive.
Recall one wish using ojalá que.

activities.title: Los seis irregulares
activities.intro: Six verbs skip the opposite-vowel rule entirely and simply have to be learned by heart: haber, saber, ir, dar, ser and estar. Note the written accents that mark esté, dé and the difference from the ordinary word de.

items.hr: Espero que seas puntual.
items.en: I hope you're punctual.
items.note: ser -> sea, seas, sea, seamos, seáis, sean, unrelated to soy

items.hr: Quiero que estés cómodo en el piso nuevo.
items.en: I want you to be comfortable in the new flat.
items.note: estar keeps a written accent throughout: esté, estés, esté, estemos, estéis, estén

items.hr: Prefiero que vayas al médico hoy.
items.en: I prefer that you go to the doctor today.
items.note: ir -> vaya, vayas, vaya, vayamos, vayáis, vayan

items.hr: Ojalá que me dé tiempo a llegar.
items.en: I hope I have time to arrive.
items.note: dar carries an accent, dé, to tell it apart from the preposition de

items.hr: No creo que haya nadie en casa, pero espero que lo sepas seguro.
items.en: I don't think there's anyone home, but I hope you know for sure.
items.note: haber -> haya (the subjunctive of hay); saber -> sepa, sepas, sepa, sepamos, sepáis, sepan

activities.title: Los seis de memoria
activities.intro: Practise the six irregular present subjunctives.

questions.prompt: Es importante que ______ temprano al aeropuerto. (ir)
questions.explanation: es importante que always needs the subjunctive; vas is indicative, irás and ibas are other tenses that don't fit here.

questions.prompt: Ojalá que ______ suficientes entradas para el concierto. (haber)
questions.explanation: ojalá always requires the subjunctive; hay is indicative, había and hubo are past indicative forms.

questions.prompt: Completa: Espero que tú ______ (ser) sincero conmigo.
questions.explanation: ser is one of the six real irregulars and must be memorised: sea, seas, sea, seamos, seáis, sean.

questions.prompt: Completa: No creo que me ______ (dar) tiempo a terminarlo hoy.
questions.explanation: dar keeps its written accent in the subjunctive, dé, to distinguish it from the preposition de.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I hope you know the answer.'
questions.explanation: saber is one of the six irregulars: sepa, sepas, sepa, sepamos, sepáis, sepan.

activities.title: Antes de la cita
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend is worried about arriving on time for an appointment, using the six irregular subjunctives.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Espero que sepas dónde está la consulta del médico.
lines.en: I hope you know where the doctor's office is.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, lo sé, pero ojalá que me dé tiempo a llegar.
lines.en: Yes, I know it, but I hope I have time to arrive.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Quiero que estés tranquilo, todavía es temprano.
lines.en: I want you to be calm, it's still early.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Prefiero que vayamos ya, por si hay tráfico.
lines.en: I prefer that we go now, in case there's traffic.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No creo que haya mucho tráfico a esta hora.
lines.en: I don't think there'll be much traffic at this hour.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Espero que estés en lo cierto.
lines.en: I hope you're right about that.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ojalá que todo vaya bien en la consulta.
lines.en: I hope everything goes well at the appointment.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Gracias, quiero que estés tranquilo tú también.
lines.en: Thanks, I want you to be calm too.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bueno, sea como sea, ya casi llegamos.
lines.en: Well, be that as it may, we're almost there.

days.title: Los cambios ortográficos del subjuntivo
days.objective: The learner can produce the spelling changes that keep a verb's sound the same across the present subjunctive: -car, -gar, -zar, -ger/-gir and -guir verbs.
days.paretoFocus: These spelling changes look like irregularities but are entirely predictable from the sound of the verb, so once the rule is understood it applies to hundreds of verbs.
drills: Write the yo-form indicative and the whole subjunctive of buscar, llegar and empezar.
Say aloud one sentence with coja and one with siga.
Explain out loud why llegue keeps the hard g sound of llegar.

items: Recall the six irregular subjunctives from the last lesson.
Remember why dé carries a written accent.
Recall how durmamos differs from duerma.

activities.title: Cambios de ortografía
activities.intro: Some verbs change a letter in the present subjunctive purely to keep the same sound: -car becomes -que, -gar becomes -gue, -zar becomes -ce, -ger/-gir becomes -ja, and -guir becomes -ga.

items.hr: Espero que busques trabajo pronto.
items.en: I hope you find work soon.
items.note: buscar (c-qu): busco -> busque, busques, busque, busquemos, busquéis, busquen

items.hr: Ojalá que llegues a tiempo.
items.en: I hope you arrive on time.
items.note: llegar (g-gu): llego -> llegue, llegues, llegue, lleguemos, lleguéis, lleguen

items.hr: Es mejor que empecemos temprano.
items.en: It's better that we start early.
items.note: empezar (z-c): empiezo -> empiece, empieces, empiece, empecemos, empecéis, empiecen

items.hr: Prefiero que cojas el autobús en vez del coche.
items.en: I prefer that you take the bus instead of the car.
items.note: coger (g-j): cojo -> coja, cojas, coja, cojamos, cojáis, cojan

items.hr: Espero que sigas mis consejos.
items.en: I hope you follow my advice.
items.note: seguir (gu-g): sigo -> siga, sigas, siga, sigamos, sigáis, sigan

activities.title: El sonido correcto
activities.intro: Practise swapping c, g and z for the letter that keeps each verb sounding the same before an e.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta? Espero que ______ trabajo pronto. (buscar, tú)
questions.explanation: buscar changes c to qu before e to keep the hard c sound: busque, busques...

questions.prompt: Elige la frase correcta sobre llegar a tiempo.
questions.explanation: ojalá always takes the subjunctive; llegar keeps its hard g by adding a u before e.

questions.prompt: Completa: Es mejor que ______ (empezar, nosotros) temprano.
questions.explanation: empezar changes z to c before e: empiece, empieces, empiece, empecemos, empecéis, empiecen.

questions.prompt: Completa: Prefiero que ______ (coger, tú) el autobús en vez del coche.
questions.explanation: coger changes g to j before a to keep the same soft sound: coja, cojas, coja...

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I hope you follow my advice.'
questions.explanation: seguir changes gu to g before a: siga, sigas, siga, sigamos, sigáis, sigan.

activities.title: Buscando trabajo
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend is job hunting and getting advice, using the spelling-change subjunctives.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Espero que busques trabajo en algo que te guste.
lines.en: I hope you look for work in something you like.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, aunque es difícil. Ojalá que llegue pronto una buena oferta.
lines.en: Yes, though it's hard. I hope a good offer arrives soon.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Es mejor que empecemos a mirar las páginas de empleo juntos.
lines.en: It's better that we start looking at the job listings together.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale. Espero que sigas ayudándome esta semana.
lines.en: Okay. I hope you keep helping me this week.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Claro. ¿Prefieres que cojamos el coche o el metro para la entrevista?
lines.en: Of course. Do you prefer we take the car or the metro for the interview?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Prefiero que cojamos el metro, es más rápido a esa hora.
lines.en: I prefer we take the metro, it's faster at that hour.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ojalá que llegues muy tranquilo a la entrevista.
lines.en: I hope you arrive very calm at the interview.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Gracias, espero que salga todo bien.
lines.en: Thanks, I hope everything goes well.

days.title: Deseos: ojalá y que
days.objective: The learner can express a wish using ojalá (que) and the short que + subjunctive formula for everyday good wishes.
days.paretoFocus: Wishing someone well happens constantly, and ojalá is the one high-frequency word in Spanish that takes the subjunctive with no main clause at all.
drills: Say aloud three wishes for a friend using ojalá.
Write two short wishes using que + subjunctive with no ojalá.
Practise a vosotros wish for a group of friends.

items: Recall the spelling changes from the last lesson.
Remember one of the six irregular subjunctives.
Recall a stem-changing subjunctive verb.

activities.title: Ojalá y que
activities.intro: Ojalá always takes the subjunctive, with or without que. A short wish can also be built with just que plus the subjunctive, with no ojalá at all, for everyday expressions like getting well or having a nice weekend.

items.hr: Ojalá tengas un buen viaje.
items.en: I hope you have a good trip.
items.note: ojalá can be followed by que or not, the meaning doesn't change

items.hr: Ojalá que apruebes el examen.
items.en: I hope you pass the exam.
items.note: aprobar (o-ue): apruebe, apruebes, apruebe, aprobemos, aprobéis, aprueben

items.hr: ¡Que te mejores pronto!
items.en: Get well soon!
items.note: a short wish with just que, no ojalá needed

items.hr: ¡Que tengáis un buen fin de semana!
items.en: Have a good weekend, everyone!
items.note: the vosotros form of a que + subjunctive wish

items.hr: ¡Que aproveche!
items.en: Enjoy your meal!
items.note: a fixed wish said before eating: aprovechar -> aproveche

activities.title: Buenos deseos
activities.intro: Practise everyday wishes with ojalá and que.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta para desear buena suerte a un amigo?
questions.explanation: ojalá always takes the subjunctive, with or without que.

questions.prompt: Elige el deseo correcto para un grupo de amigos.
options: ¡Que tengáis un buen fin de semana!
¡Que tenéis un buen fin de semana!
¡Que tendréis un buen fin de semana!
¡Que teníais un buen fin de semana!
questions.answer: ¡Que tengáis un buen fin de semana!
questions.explanation: a wish with que always takes the subjunctive; the vosotros form here is tengáis.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¡Que ______ (dormir, tú) bien!
questions.explanation: dormir keeps its o-ue change in a que + subjunctive wish.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ojalá ______ (aprobar, tú) el examen.
questions.explanation: aprobar changes o to ue in the present subjunctive: apruebe, apruebes, apruebe...

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Get well soon!'
questions.explanation: a short everyday wish uses just que plus the subjunctive, no ojalá needed.

activities.title: Antes de un viaje
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends say goodbye before a trip, exchanging wishes.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Me voy mañana temprano al aeropuerto.
lines.en: I'm leaving early tomorrow for the airport.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ojalá tengas un buen viaje y no haya retrasos.
lines.en: I hope you have a good trip and there are no delays.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Gracias. Y tú, ¿no tenías un examen la semana que viene?
lines.en: Thanks. And you, didn't you have an exam next week?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, ojalá que apruebe sin problemas.
lines.en: Yes, I hope I pass without problems.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Que tengas mucha suerte con eso!
lines.en: Good luck with that!

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Gracias. ¡Que tengáis todos un buen fin de semana también!
lines.en: Thanks. Have a good weekend, all of you too!

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Nos vemos a la vuelta. ¡Que te vaya bien!
lines.en: See you when I'm back. Take care!

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¡Que disfrutes del viaje, hasta pronto!
lines.en: Enjoy the trip, see you soon!

days.title: La duda en oraciones independientes
days.objective: The learner can express varying degrees of doubt with quizá, tal vez, a lo mejor and posiblemente, choosing the mood that matches the intended certainty.
days.paretoFocus: Speculating about the future or the unknown is constant in daily speech, and the mood choice after these words carries real meaning that a learner needs to control, not just recognise.
drills: Say the same idea twice with quizá, once with the subjunctive and once with the indicative.
Write one sentence with a lo mejor, always in the indicative.
Write one sentence with posiblemente and the subjunctive.

items: Recall a wish with ojalá from the last lesson.
Remember why buscar becomes busque in the subjunctive.
Recall the six irregular subjunctives.

activities.title: Quizá, tal vez, a lo mejor
activities.intro: Quizá and tal vez can take either mood, and the choice is meaningful: the subjunctive signals more doubt, the indicative signals more confidence. A lo mejor means much the same but always takes the indicative, which simply has to be learned rather than reasoned out.

items.hr: Quizá venga a la fiesta.
items.en: Maybe he'll come to the party.
items.note: quizá + subjunctive signals more doubt

items.hr: Quizá viene a la fiesta, pero llega tarde.
items.en: Maybe he's coming to the party, but he's arriving late.
items.note: quizá + indicative signals more confidence; both sentences are correct Spanish

items.hr: Tal vez tengamos suerte hoy.
items.en: Maybe we'll be lucky today.
items.note: tal vez behaves exactly like quizá, either mood, meaning shifts

items.hr: A lo mejor llueve esta tarde.
items.en: Maybe it will rain this afternoon.
items.note: a lo mejor always takes the indicative, unlike quizá and tal vez

items.hr: Posiblemente lleguemos tarde a la reunión.
items.en: We'll possibly arrive late to the meeting.
items.note: posiblemente is regularly followed by the subjunctive too

activities.title: ¿Cuánta duda?
activities.intro: Practise choosing the right word and mood for different degrees of doubt.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué expresión va siempre con el indicativo, nunca con el subjuntivo?
questions.explanation: a lo mejor always takes the indicative even though it means much the same as quizá or tal vez, which can take either mood.

questions.prompt: Completa: A lo mejor ______ antes que nosotros. (llegar)
questions.explanation: a lo mejor is always followed by the indicative; llegue is the wrong mood, llegó and llegaba are the wrong tense here.

questions.prompt: Completa: A lo mejor no ______ (tener) razón esta vez.
questions.explanation: a lo mejor never takes the subjunctive, only the indicative.

questions.prompt: Completa: Posiblemente nosotros ______ (llegar) tarde a la reunión.
questions.explanation: posiblemente is regularly followed by the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Maybe we'll have luck today.'
questions.explanation: tal vez behaves exactly like quizá and can take the subjunctive to signal more doubt.

activities.title: Planes inciertos
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends make weekend plans full of uncertainty.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué planes tienes para el sábado?
lines.en: What plans do you have for Saturday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No sé todavía. Quizá vaya a la montaña, si hace buen tiempo.
lines.en: I don't know yet. Maybe I'll go to the mountains, if the weather's good.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: A lo mejor llueve, según la previsión.
lines.en: Maybe it'll rain, according to the forecast.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es verdad, tal vez sea mejor quedarnos en la ciudad.
lines.en: True, maybe it's better to stay in the city.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Posiblemente organicemos algo con más gente entonces.
lines.en: We'll possibly organize something with more people then.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Buena idea. Quizá vengan también Marta y Pablo.
lines.en: Good idea. Maybe Marta and Pablo will come too.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: A lo mejor tienen otros planes, pero les pregunto.
lines.en: Maybe they have other plans, but I'll ask them.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, tal vez decidamos todo esta noche.
lines.en: Okay, maybe we'll decide everything tonight.

days.title: Oraciones sustantivas: querer que
days.objective: The learner can express wants and preferences directed at someone else using querer que, preferir que and necesitar que plus the subjunctive.
days.paretoFocus: Wanting another person to do something is the reason most speakers reach for the subjunctive in the first place, so this is the use that makes the whole mood feel motivated rather than arbitrary.
drills: Write three sentences about what you want other people to do, using querer que.
Say aloud the difference between quiero ir and quiero que vayas.
Write one sentence with necesitar que about something at home.

items: Recall the difference between quizá plus indicative and quizá plus subjunctive.
Remember why a lo mejor never takes the subjunctive.
Recall a wish using que plus subjunctive.

activities.title: Querer que
activities.intro: Verbs of wanting like querer, preferir and necesitar take que plus the subjunctive whenever the person doing the wanting is different from the person who has to act. When both are the same person, an infinitive is used instead, with no que at all.

items.hr: Quiero que vengas a mi cumpleaños.
items.en: I want you to come to my birthday.
items.note: querer que + subjunctive, two different subjects

items.hr: Prefiero que hagas los deberes antes de cenar.
items.en: I prefer that you do your homework before dinner.
items.note: preferir que + subjunctive

items.hr: Necesito que me ayudes con esto.
items.en: I need you to help me with this.
items.note: necesitar que + subjunctive

items.hr: Quiero ir contigo.
items.en: I want to go with you.
items.note: same subject for both verbs, so the infinitive is used, no que

items.hr: Mis padres quieren que estudie medicina.
items.en: My parents want me to study medicine.
items.note: querer que with a third-person subject: quieren que estudie

activities.title: Lo que quiero de ti
activities.intro: Practise choosing querer que, preferir que or necesitar que, then supplying the right subjunctive form after it.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? Mis padres quieren que yo ______ medicina. (estudiar)
questions.explanation: querer que with a different subject takes the subjunctive; the other options are indicative tenses that don't fit here.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase es correcta cuando el sujeto es el mismo?
questions.explanation: with one subject only the infinitive is possible; que plus a conjugated verb is ungrammatical here.

questions.prompt: Completa: Necesito que tú me ______ (ayudar) con la mudanza.
questions.explanation: necesitar que with a different subject takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa: Prefiero que los niños se ______ (acostarse) antes de las nueve.
questions.explanation: acostarse (o-ue) in the subjunctive: se acueste, te acuestes, se acuesten, and the reflexive pronoun still goes before the verb.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I want you to come to my birthday.'
questions.explanation: querer que with a different subject takes the subjunctive: quiero que vengas.

activities.title: La fiesta de cumpleaños
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend is organizing a birthday party and negotiating who wants what.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Quiero que vengas a mi cumpleaños el sábado.
lines.en: I want you to come to my birthday on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro que sí. ¿Necesitas que traiga algo?
lines.en: Of course. Do you need me to bring something?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sí, necesito que traigas hielo y algunas bebidas.
lines.en: Yes, I need you to bring ice and some drinks.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, sin problema. ¿Prefieres que llegue temprano para ayudar?
lines.en: Okay, no problem. Do you prefer I arrive early to help?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sí, prefiero que llegues una hora antes.
lines.en: Yes, I prefer that you arrive an hour earlier.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfecto, quiero ayudarte con todo lo que pueda.
lines.en: Perfect, I want to help you with whatever I can.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Gracias. Mis padres también quieren que la fiesta salga bien.
lines.en: Thanks. My parents also want the party to go well.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Seguro que sí, todos queremos que te diviertas.
lines.en: Sure it will, we all want you to have fun.

days.title: Oraciones sustantivas: emoción y reacción
days.objective: The learner can react to news or situations using emotion verbs like alegrarse de, molestar, sorprender and sentir plus the subjunctive.
days.paretoFocus: Reacting emotionally to what someone else says is a core part of natural conversation, and every one of these verbs forces the subjunctive in the clause that follows.
drills: Write three reactions to imaginary news using me alegro de que, me sorprende que and siento que.
Say aloud one sentence with me molesta que about a daily annoyance.
Write one vosotros sentence with nos encanta que.

items: Recall the difference between quiero ir and quiero que vayas.
Remember one of the six irregular present subjunctives.
Recall a sentence using necesitar que.

activities.title: Reaccionar con emoción
activities.intro: This group of verbs describes an emotional reaction rather than a fact, so whatever follows que has to be in the subjunctive: sentir, sorprender, molestar and alegrarse de are the four to know here.

items.hr: Me alegro de que estés aquí.
items.en: I'm glad you're here.
items.note: alegrarse de que + subjunctive

items.hr: Me molesta que llegues tarde siempre.
items.en: It bothers me that you're always late.
items.note: molestar que + subjunctive, like gustar in structure

items.hr: Me sorprende que no sepas la noticia.
items.en: It surprises me that you don't know the news.
items.note: sorprender que + subjunctive; saber -> sepas

items.hr: Siento que no puedas venir.
items.en: I'm sorry you can't come.
items.note: sentir que + subjunctive; poder -> puedas

items.hr: Nos encanta que vengáis a vernos.
items.en: We love that you all come to see us.
items.note: encantar que + subjunctive, vosotros form vengáis

activities.title: Reacciones
activities.intro: Practise reacting to news with emotion verbs and the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? Me sorprende que no ______ la noticia. (saber)
questions.explanation: sorprender que always takes the subjunctive; the other options are indicative tenses.

questions.prompt: Elige la reacción correcta cuando alguien llega.
options: Me alegro de que estés aquí.
Me alegro de que estás aquí.
Me alegro de que estarás aquí.
Me alegro de que estabas aquí.
questions.answer: Me alegro de que estés aquí.
questions.explanation: emotion verbs like alegrarse de que always require the subjunctive in the clause that follows.

questions.prompt: Completa: Siento que no ______ (poder) venir a la boda.
questions.explanation: sentir que takes the subjunctive; poder changes o to ue: pueda, puedas, pueda...

questions.prompt: Completa: Nos encanta que ______ (venir, vosotros) a vernos.
questions.explanation: encantar que takes the subjunctive; venir is irregular in the subjunctive: venga, vengas, vengáis...

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'It bothers me that you always arrive late.'
questions.explanation: molestar que, like gustar, always takes the subjunctive in the clause it introduces.

activities.title: Noticias inesperadas
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend shares some unexpected news and both react emotionally.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Me han ofrecido un trabajo en otra ciudad.
lines.en: They've offered me a job in another city.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¡Vaya! Me sorprende que me lo cuentes tan tarde.
lines.en: Wow! It surprises me that you're only telling me this so late.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Lo sé, lo siento. Me alegro de que lo entiendas.
lines.en: I know, I'm sorry. I'm glad you understand.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro que lo entiendo. Siento que tengamos que separarnos.
lines.en: Of course I understand. I'm sorry we have to separate.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: A mí también me molesta que sea tan lejos.
lines.en: It also bothers me that it's so far.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pero nos encanta que tengas esta oportunidad.
lines.en: But we're delighted that you have this opportunity.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Gracias. Espero que vengáis a visitarme pronto.
lines.en: Thanks. I hope you all come to visit me soon.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Seguro que sí, nos alegra que empieces algo nuevo.
lines.en: For sure, we're happy that you're starting something new.

days.title: Oraciones sustantivas: juicios de valor
days.objective: The learner can express value judgements with es bueno que, es importante que, es necesario que and está bien que plus the subjunctive.
days.paretoFocus: Impersonal value judgements are the natural way to give advice or state an opinion indirectly in Spanish, and they are extremely common in both speech and writing.
drills: Write three pieces of general advice using es importante que and es necesario que.
Say aloud one sentence with está bien que about a decision someone made.
Write one sentence with es una pena que about a missed opportunity.

items: Recall a reaction sentence using me alegro de que.
Remember why molestar que behaves like gustar.
Recall the subjunctive form of poder.

activities.title: Juicios de valor
activities.intro: An impersonal opinion, saying something está bien, es necesario, es importante or es bueno, still needs the subjunctive in the que-clause that follows, because these judge an action rather than report it as settled fact.

items.hr: Es bueno que hagas ejercicio.
items.en: It's good that you exercise.
items.note: es bueno que + subjunctive

items.hr: Es importante que estudies para el examen.
items.en: It's important that you study for the exam.
items.note: es importante que + subjunctive

items.hr: Es necesario que todos participen.
items.en: It's necessary that everyone participates.
items.note: es necesario que + subjunctive

items.hr: Está bien que digas siempre la verdad.
items.en: It's good that you always tell the truth.
items.note: está bien que + subjunctive

items.hr: Es una pena que no podáis quedaros más tiempo.
items.en: It's a shame that you all can't stay longer.
items.note: es una pena que + subjunctive, vosotros form podáis

activities.title: Opiniones y valores
activities.intro: Practise value judgements followed by the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? Es importante que ______ todos los días. (estudiar)
questions.explanation: es importante que always takes the subjunctive when there is a subject in the clause that follows.

questions.prompt: Elige el juicio de valor correcto.
questions.explanation: es necesario que with a subject takes the subjunctive, not the indicative.

questions.prompt: Completa: Está bien que ______ (decir, tú) siempre la verdad.
questions.explanation: está bien que takes the subjunctive; decir is irregular: diga, digas, diga...

questions.prompt: Completa: Es una pena que no ______ (poder, vosotros) quedaros más tiempo.
questions.explanation: es una pena que takes the subjunctive; poder changes o to ue: pueda, puedas, podáis, puedan.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'It's good that you exercise.'
questions.explanation: es bueno que, a value judgement, takes the subjunctive: hagas.

activities.title: Consejos para una vida sana
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend gives lifestyle advice using value judgements.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Es bueno que hagas ejercicio cada semana.
lines.en: It's good that you exercise every week.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, es importante que cuidemos la salud.
lines.en: Yes, it's important that we take care of our health.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: También es necesario que descanses lo suficiente.
lines.en: It's also necessary that you rest enough.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Está bien que me lo recuerdes, últimamente duermo poco.
lines.en: It's good that you remind me, lately I sleep little.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Es una pena que no tengas más tiempo libre.
lines.en: It's a shame you don't have more free time.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es cierto, pero es importante que organicemos mejor el día.
lines.en: That's true, but it's important that we organize the day better.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Estoy de acuerdo, es bueno que empieces poco a poco.
lines.en: I agree, it's good that you start little by little.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Gracias por los consejos, es necesario que te escuche más.
lines.en: Thanks for the advice, it's necessary that I listen to you more.

days.title: Duda y negación frente a certeza
days.objective: The learner can distinguish creo que from no creo que, and use dudar que and no es verdad que, choosing indicative or subjunctive based on whether the following clause is being asserted as fact.
days.paretoFocus: This single idea, that the subjunctive marks a clause not asserted as true, quietly explains almost every subjunctive trigger in this whole block rather than requiring six separate lists.
drills: Say the same fact twice, once with creo que and once with no creo que.
Write one sentence with dudo que about something you genuinely doubt.
Write a pair of sentences about the same topic, one starting dudo que and the other starting no dudo que.

items: Recall a value judgement sentence using es importante que.
Remember the subjunctive of decir.
Recall a reaction sentence using me sorprende que.

activities.title: Lo que se afirma y lo que no
activities.intro: The subjunctive appears in a noun clause whenever what follows is not being asserted as a fact: doubt, denial and negated certainty all trigger it, while creer, es verdad and other statements of certainty keep the indicative. Learn this one idea and the whole block becomes one rule instead of six.

items.hr: Creo que Ana tiene razón.
items.en: I think Ana is right.
items.note: creer que asserts something as true, so it keeps the indicative

items.hr: No creo que Ana tenga razón.
items.en: I don't think Ana is right.
items.note: negating creer removes the assertion, so the subjunctive appears

items.hr: Dudo que sea verdad.
items.en: I doubt it's true.
items.note: dudar que always expresses doubt, so it always takes the subjunctive

items.hr: No dudo que tienes razón.
items.en: I don't doubt that you're right.
items.note: no dudar que mirrors no creer que in reverse: removing the doubt restores the assertion, so it takes the indicative, not the subjunctive

items.hr: Es verdad que llueve mucho aquí en invierno.
items.en: It's true that it rains a lot here in winter.
items.note: es verdad que asserts a fact, so it keeps the indicative

items.hr: No es verdad que llueva mucho aquí en verano.
items.en: It's not true that it rains a lot here in summer.
items.note: denying the fact removes the assertion, so the subjunctive appears

activities.title: ¿Se afirma o se duda?
activities.intro: Decide whether the statement that follows is presented as settled or merely doubted, then pick indicative or subjunctive to match.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? No creo que Ana ______ razón. (tener)
questions.explanation: no creo que removes the assertion of certainty, so the subjunctive is required.

questions.prompt: Elige la expresión de duda correcta.
questions.explanation: dudar always expresses doubt, so it always takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa: Es verdad que ______ (llover) mucho aquí en invierno.
questions.explanation: es verdad que asserts a fact, so it keeps the indicative.

questions.prompt: Completa: No es verdad que ______ (llover) mucho aquí en verano.
questions.explanation: denying the truth of a statement removes the assertion, so the subjunctive appears.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I don't think Ana is right.'
questions.explanation: no creo que removes the assertion of certainty, requiring the subjunctive: tenga.

activities.title: Una discusión de sobremesa
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends disagree about a rumour, contrasting creer with no creer.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has oído que van a cerrar la fábrica del barrio?
lines.en: Have you heard they're going to close the factory in the neighbourhood?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No creo que sea verdad, nadie me ha dicho nada.
lines.en: I don't think that's true, nobody has told me anything.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Pues yo creo que es cierto, lo dijo un vecino.
lines.en: Well I think it's true, a neighbour said it.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Dudo que un vecino lo sepa mejor que la propia empresa.
lines.en: I doubt a neighbour knows it better than the company itself.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Es verdad que la fábrica lleva meses con problemas.
lines.en: It's true that the factory has had problems for months.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Eso sí lo creo, pero no es verdad que vaya a cerrar ya.
lines.en: That I do believe, but it's not true that it's going to close already.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ojalá tengas razón y todo siga igual.
lines.en: I hope you're right and everything stays the same.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Yo también lo espero, no creo que sea tan grave.
lines.en: I hope so too, I don't think it's that serious.

days.title: Un sujeto o dos
days.objective: The learner can choose correctly between an infinitive and que plus the subjunctive, based on whether the subject of both verbs is the same person or two different people.
days.paretoFocus: This is the single most common overgeneralisation error at this level, using que plus the subjunctive with only one subject, so making the rule explicit prevents a mistake that would otherwise repeat in every future lesson.
drills: Write one pair of sentences, same subject and different subject, with querer.
Say aloud why 'Quiero que yo vaya' is wrong.
Write one pair of sentences with necesitar, same subject and different subject.

items: Recall the difference between creo que and no creo que.
Remember why dudar always takes the subjunctive.
Recall a value judgement using es necesario que.

activities.title: Infinitivo o que + subjuntivo
activities.intro: With one subject, Spanish uses the infinitive and que is ungrammatical: 'Quiero ir', never 'Quiero que yo vaya'. With two different subjects, que plus the subjunctive is required instead. Learners overgeneralise the subjunctive here constantly, so it is worth stating as its own rule.

items.hr: Quiero ir a la playa este verano.
items.en: I want to go to the beach this summer.
items.note: same subject, so the infinitive is used; 'Quiero que yo vaya' would be ungrammatical

items.hr: Quiero que vayas a la playa conmigo.
items.en: I want you to go to the beach with me.
items.note: two different subjects, so que plus the subjunctive is required

items.hr: Prefiero descansar esta tarde.
items.en: I prefer to rest this afternoon.
items.note: same subject, infinitive, no que

items.hr: Prefiero que descanses esta tarde.
items.en: I prefer that you rest this afternoon.
items.note: different subjects, que plus the subjunctive

items.hr: Espero llegar a tiempo, pero también espero que tú llegues antes que yo.
items.en: I hope to arrive on time, but I also hope you arrive before me.
items.note: both patterns in one sentence, same subject then different subjects

activities.title: Mismo sujeto o distinto
activities.intro: Decide whether both verbs share one subject or belong to two different people, then pick the infinitive or a que-clause accordingly.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'I want to go home' con un solo sujeto?
questions.explanation: with one subject only the infinitive is possible; que plus a conjugated verb is ungrammatical here.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'I want you to go home' con dos sujetos distintos?
questions.explanation: two different subjects require que plus the subjunctive; the infinitive alone would wrongly suggest the speaker is going.

questions.prompt: Completa (mismo sujeto): Necesito ______ (descansar) un poco.
questions.explanation: with the same subject, an infinitive follows necesitar, with no que.

questions.prompt: Completa (sujetos distintos): Necesito que tú ______ (descansar) un poco.
questions.explanation: with two different subjects, que plus the subjunctive follows necesitar.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I prefer that you decide.'
questions.explanation: a different subject requires que plus the subjunctive: decidas.

activities.title: Compañeros de piso
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two flatmates negotiate chores, mixing same-subject and different-subject sentences.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Quiero limpiar la cocina esta tarde, ¿te parece bien?
lines.en: I want to clean the kitchen this afternoon, is that okay with you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, y prefiero que hagamos también el salón.
lines.en: Yes, and I prefer that we also do the living room.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vale. Necesito comprar productos de limpieza antes.
lines.en: Okay. I need to buy cleaning products first.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Necesito que compres también bolsas de basura.
lines.en: I need you to also buy trash bags.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: De acuerdo. Prefiero descansar un rato antes de empezar.
lines.en: Agreed. I prefer to rest a bit before starting.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Prefiero que empecemos ya, así terminamos antes.
lines.en: I prefer that we start now, so we finish sooner.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vale, tienes razón. Quiero que quede todo perfecto.
lines.en: Okay, you're right. I want everything to end up perfect.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Yo también quiero terminar pronto y descansar.
lines.en: I also want to finish soon and rest.

days.title: Contar órdenes y peticiones
days.objective: The learner can report a request or order using decir que and pedir que plus the subjunctive, keeping the main verb in the present.
days.paretoFocus: Relaying what someone wants another person to do is extremely common in daily life, whether at work, at home or between friends.
drills: Write one sentence reporting an order with dice que.
Write one sentence reporting a request with pide que.
Say aloud the difference between dice que trabaja and dice que trabajes.

items: Recall the difference between quiero ir and quiero que vayas.
Remember the subjunctive of ir.
Recall a sentence with prefiero que.

activities.title: Dice que, pide que
activities.intro: Decir and pedir report a command or request with que plus the subjunctive. Throughout this course, the verb that introduces the request stays in the present tense, so it comes out as 'Me pide que espere', never with a past-tense frame, which would need a form beyond this course.

items.hr: Dice que vengas a la reunión.
items.en: She says you should come to the meeting.
items.note: decir que + subjunctive, reporting an order

items.hr: Dice que la reunión empieza a las nueve.
items.en: She says the meeting starts at nine.
items.note: decir que + indicative, reporting a plain fact, contrast with the previous line

items.hr: Me pide que espere un momento.
items.en: She asks me to wait a moment.
items.note: pedir que + subjunctive, present main verb

items.hr: Te digo que tengas cuidado con el hielo.
items.en: I'm telling you to be careful with the ice.
items.note: decir que + subjunctive, a warning

items.hr: Nos piden que llamemos antes de las ocho.
items.en: They ask us to call before eight.
items.note: pedir que + subjunctive, third person plural

activities.title: Órdenes y hechos
activities.intro: Practise the difference between reporting an order and reporting a plain fact.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase transmite una orden, no un hecho?
options: Dice que vengas a la reunión.
Dice que la reunión empieza a las nueve.
questions.answer: Dice que vengas a la reunión.
questions.explanation: decir que plus the subjunctive transmits an order or request; decir que plus the indicative transmits a fact.

questions.prompt: Completa: Cada vez que llego, me ______ que espere un momento. (pedir)
questions.explanation: the habitual frame cada vez que llego needs a present main verb, pide, paired with the present subjunctive espere; the other options clash with that frame or are not conjugated.

questions.prompt: Completa: Te ______ (decir) que tengas cuidado.
questions.explanation: the main verb stays in the present, paired with the subjunctive tengas.

questions.prompt: Completa: Nos ______ (pedir) que llamemos antes de las ocho.
questions.explanation: pedir que with a plural subject takes the subjunctive in the clause it introduces.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'She says the meeting starts at nine.'
questions.explanation: decir que reporting a plain fact keeps the indicative: empieza.

activities.title: El mensaje del jefe
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A coworker relays instructions from the boss.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: El jefe dice que vengas a su despacho.
lines.en: The boss says you should come to his office.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¿Ahora mismo? ¿Dice para qué?
lines.en: Right now? Does he say what for?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Dice que la reunión de hoy empieza antes de lo previsto.
lines.en: He says today's meeting starts earlier than planned.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, voy enseguida. ¿Te pide algo a ti también?
lines.en: Okay, I'm going right away. Does he ask you for anything too?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sí, me pide que prepare los documentos.
lines.en: Yes, he asks me to prepare the documents.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Nos pide siempre que lleguemos con todo listo.
lines.en: He always asks us to arrive with everything ready.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Es verdad. Te digo que te des prisa, es tarde.
lines.en: True. I'm telling you to hurry, it's late.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Voy corriendo, gracias por avisarme.
lines.en: I'm going right now, thanks for letting me know.

days.title: Pedir, aconsejar y prohibir
days.objective: The learner can give advice, make recommendations, and state permissions or prohibitions using aconsejar, recomendar, sugerir, prohibir and permitir plus que and the subjunctive.
days.paretoFocus: These verbs cover the everyday acts of advising and setting rules, at work, at home and between friends, all of which the subjunctive now lets the learner express naturally.
drills: Write one piece of advice using te aconsejo que.
Write one rule using prohíben que and one using permiten que.
Say aloud a recommendation using os recomiendo que.

items: Recall the difference between decir que plus indicative and decir que plus subjunctive.
Remember the present subjunctive of empezar.
Recall a sentence reporting a request with pedir que.

activities.title: Consejos y normas
activities.intro: Verbs that give advice, grant permission or forbid something, like permitir, prohibir, sugerir, recomendar and aconsejar, all take que plus the subjunctive whenever the action falls on someone other than the speaker.

items.hr: Te aconsejo que descanses más.
items.en: I advise you to rest more.
items.note: aconsejar que + subjunctive

items.hr: Os recomiendo que probéis el restaurante nuevo.
items.en: I recommend you all try the new restaurant.
items.note: recomendar que + subjunctive, vosotros form probéis

items.hr: Sugiero que empecemos cuanto antes.
items.en: I suggest we start as soon as possible.
items.note: sugerir que + subjunctive

items.hr: Mis padres me prohíben que salga entre semana.
items.en: My parents forbid me from going out on weekdays.
items.note: prohibir que + subjunctive; prohíben is the indicative of the main verb

items.hr: El profesor nos permite que usemos el diccionario en el examen.
items.en: The teacher allows us to use the dictionary in the exam.
items.note: permitir que + subjunctive

activities.title: Consejos, permisos y prohibiciones
activities.intro: Practise advising, recommending, forbidding and allowing.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? Te aconsejo que ______ más. (descansar)
questions.explanation: aconsejar que always takes the subjunctive in the clause that follows.

questions.prompt: Elige la prohibición correcta.
options: Mis padres me prohíben que salga entre semana.
Mis padres me prohíben que salgo entre semana.
Mis padres me prohíben que saldré entre semana.
Mis padres me prohíben que salía entre semana.
questions.answer: Mis padres me prohíben que salga entre semana.
questions.explanation: prohibir que always takes the subjunctive in the clause it introduces.

questions.prompt: Completa: Sugiero que ______ (empezar, nosotros) cuanto antes.
questions.explanation: sugerir que takes the subjunctive; empezar changes z to c before e.

questions.prompt: Completa: El profesor nos permite que ______ (usar) el diccionario.
questions.explanation: permitir que takes the subjunctive in the clause that follows.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I recommend you all try the new restaurant.'
questions.explanation: recomendar que with vosotros as the addressee takes probéis in the subjunctive.

activities.title: Normas de la oficina
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two coworkers discuss office rules and advice for a new colleague.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: El jefe prohíbe que comamos en las mesas de trabajo.
lines.en: The boss forbids us from eating at our desks.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ya lo sabía. En cambio, sí permite que trabajemos desde casa.
lines.en: I already knew that. On the other hand, he does allow us to work from home.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Es verdad. Te aconsejo que se lo pidas para los viernes.
lines.en: True. I advise you to ask him for it on Fridays.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Buena idea. ¿Qué le recomiendas a la nueva compañera?
lines.en: Good idea. What do you recommend to the new colleague?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Le recomiendo que hable con el jefe pronto, es fácil de tratar.
lines.en: I recommend she talk to the boss soon, he's easy to deal with.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sugiero que empecemos por presentarle a todo el equipo.
lines.en: I suggest we start by introducing her to the whole team.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Me parece bien. ¿Te prohíben algo más en tu departamento?
lines.en: Sounds good. Do they forbid you anything else in your department?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Solo nos prohíben que usemos el móvil en las reuniones.
lines.en: They only forbid us from using our phones in meetings.

days.title: Esperanza, miedo y sorpresa
days.objective: The learner can express hope, fear and worry using esperar que, temer que and tener miedo de que plus the subjunctive.
days.paretoFocus: Hoping for a good outcome and fearing a bad one are among the most natural things to say about an uncertain future, and both require the subjunctive automatically.
drills: Write one sentence hoping something goes well with espero que.
Write one sentence fearing something with temo que.
Say aloud a sentence using tener miedo de que about travel.

items: Recall a sentence using te aconsejo que.
Remember the subjunctive of permitir.
Recall the difference between prohibir que and permitir que.

activities.title: Esperar y temer
activities.intro: Verbs of hope and fear, like tener miedo de que, temer que and esperar que, take the subjunctive because they express an emotional stance toward an outcome that is not yet certain.

items.hr: Espero que todo salga bien.
items.en: I hope everything goes well.
items.note: esperar que + subjunctive

items.hr: Temo que perdamos el tren.
items.en: I'm afraid we'll miss the train.
items.note: temer que + subjunctive

items.hr: Tengo miedo de que se enfade conmigo.
items.en: I'm afraid he'll get angry with me.
items.note: tener miedo de que + subjunctive

items.hr: Esperamos que hagáis buen viaje.
items.en: We hope you all have a good trip.
items.note: esperar que + subjunctive, vosotros form hagáis

items.hr: Tienen miedo de que el vuelo se retrase.
items.en: They're afraid the flight will be delayed.
items.note: tener miedo de que + subjunctive

activities.title: Esperanzas y temores
activities.intro: Practise expressing hope and fear with the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? Espero que todo ______ bien. (salir)
questions.explanation: esperar que always takes the subjunctive in the clause that follows.

questions.prompt: Elige la expresión de temor correcta.
questions.explanation: temer que expresses fear about an uncertain outcome and always takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa: Tengo miedo de que se ______ (enfadar) conmigo.
questions.explanation: tener miedo de que takes the subjunctive: enfade, enfades, enfade...

questions.prompt: Completa: Esperamos que ______ (hacer, vosotros) buen viaje.
questions.explanation: esperar que with vosotros as the subject takes the subjunctive hagáis.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'They're afraid the flight will be delayed.'
questions.explanation: tener miedo de que takes the subjunctive: retrase.

activities.title: En el aeropuerto
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two travellers worry about their connecting flight.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tengo miedo de que perdamos la conexión.
lines.en: I'm afraid we'll miss the connection.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Espero que no, todavía tenemos una hora.
lines.en: I hope not, we still have an hour.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Temo que el vuelo se retrase con esta lluvia.
lines.en: I'm afraid the flight will be delayed with this rain.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ojalá que no sea así, pero está lloviendo mucho.
lines.en: I hope that's not the case, but it's raining a lot.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Esperemos que el piloto pueda despegar sin problemas.
lines.en: Let's hope the pilot can take off without problems.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, esperamos que todo salga bien al final.
lines.en: Yes, we hope everything goes well in the end.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: También tengo miedo de que perdamos las maletas.
lines.en: I'm also afraid we'll lose our bags.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No pienses en eso, espero que lleguen con nosotros.
lines.en: Don't think about that, I hope they arrive with us.

days.title: Consolidación: indicativo o subjuntivo
days.objective: The learner can apply one clear decision procedure to choose indicative or subjunctive across every kind of noun clause studied so far.
days.paretoFocus: Consolidating these separate lists into a single decision procedure is what turns scattered rules into a skill the learner can use in real time.
drills: Say the decision procedure aloud in your own words.
Write one sentence for each of the four categories: will, emotion, value, doubt.
Correct an incorrect sentence a classmate might write, out loud.

items: Recall a sentence using espero que.
Remember why temer que always takes the subjunctive.
Recall a sentence using tener miedo de que.

activities.title: Un solo procedimiento
