activities.intro: No new grammar here, just one procedure that covers every case seen so far: with a verb of will, emotion, value or doubt, use que plus the subjunctive if the subject changes and the infinitive if it stays the same; with a verb of certainty in the affirmative, keep the indicative, and only switch to the subjunctive if that certainty is denied.

items.hr: Quiero que aprendas español.
items.en: I want you to learn Spanish.
items.note: voluntad, sujeto distinto: subjuntivo

items.hr: Quiero aprender español.
items.en: I want to learn Spanish.
items.note: voluntad, mismo sujeto: infinitivo

items.hr: Creo que hablas muy bien.
items.en: I think you speak very well.
items.note: certeza afirmativa: indicativo

items.hr: No creo que hables tan mal como dices.
items.en: I don't think you speak as badly as you say.
items.note: certeza negada: subjuntivo

items.hr: Es importante que practiques cada día.
items.en: It's important that you practise every day.
items.note: juicio de valor con sujeto: subjuntivo

activities.title: El procedimiento en acción
activities.intro: Practise applying one decision procedure across different kinds of noun clauses.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? No creo que ______ tan difícil. (ser)
questions.explanation: no creo que denies the certainty, so the subjunctive is required.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? Creo que ______ muy bien español. (hablar, tú)
questions.explanation: creo que asserts certainty, so it keeps the indicative; only its negation would take the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa: Es importante que ______ (practicar, tú) cada día.
questions.explanation: a value judgement with a subject takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa: Quiero ______ (aprender) español, no quiero que otra persona lo haga por mí.
questions.explanation: with the same subject as querer, the infinitive is used, with no que.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I don't believe that it's true.'
questions.explanation: no creo que denies the certainty, so the subjunctive sea is required.

activities.title: Opiniones mezcladas
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends discuss a shared project, moving between wants, opinions, emotions and doubts.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Quiero que terminemos el proyecto esta semana.
lines.en: I want us to finish the project this week.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Creo que es posible si nos organizamos bien.
lines.en: I think it's possible if we organize well.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No creo que sea tan fácil, todavía falta mucho.
lines.en: I don't think it's that easy, there's still a lot left.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es verdad, pero es importante que lo intentemos.
lines.en: True, but it's important that we try.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Me alegro de que pienses así, necesitamos energía.
lines.en: I'm glad you think that way, we need energy.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Espero que los demás también se animen a esforzarse.
lines.en: I hope the others also feel encouraged to make an effort.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Dudo que todos tengan el mismo tiempo libre que nosotros.
lines.en: I doubt everyone has the same free time as us.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es cierto, pero quiero intentarlo de todas formas.
lines.en: That's true, but I want to try anyway.

days.title: Opiniones y reacciones en diálogo
days.objective: The learner can use a wider set of everyday reaction phrases, like me parece que, qué bien que, qué pena que and no está de más que, all with the subjunctive.
days.paretoFocus: These fixed reaction phrases appear constantly in casual conversation and give the learner natural-sounding ways to react to what someone else has just said.
drills: Write one reaction using me parece genial que about good news.
Say aloud qué pena que about something you're sorry about.
Write one sentence of mild advice using the it-wouldn't-hurt-to phrase from this lesson.

items: Recall the decision procedure from the last lesson.
Remember the subjunctive form of venir.
Recall a sentence using es importante que.

activities.title: Más formas de reaccionar
activities.intro: Everyday Spanish keeps piling up fixed reaction phrases beyond alegrarse and sorprender. Some state an opinion (me parece bien, mal or genial), others react with surprise or regret (qué bien..., qué pena...), and one softens advice (no está de más...); every one of them still pulls the subjunctive into what follows.

items.hr: Me parece genial que vengas a la boda.
items.en: I think it's great that you're coming to the wedding.
items.note: me parece + adjective + que + subjunctive

items.hr: ¡Qué bien que vengas a la fiesta!
items.en: How great that you're coming to the party!
items.note: qué bien que + subjunctive

items.hr: ¡Qué pena que no puedas quedarte!
items.en: What a shame you can't stay!
items.note: qué pena que + subjunctive

items.hr: No está de más que preguntes antes de firmar.
items.en: It doesn't hurt to ask before signing.
items.note: no está de más que + subjunctive, mild advice

items.hr: Me parece mal que la gente no recicle.
items.en: I think it's wrong that people don't recycle.
items.note: me parece mal que + subjunctive

activities.title: Reaccionando de verdad
activities.intro: Match each opinion or reaction cue to the subjunctive clause that has to follow it.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? Me parece genial que ______ a la boda. (venir, tú)
questions.explanation: me parece + adjective + que always takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Elige la reacción correcta con qué pena que.
questions.explanation: qué pena que always takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa: No está de más que ______ (preguntar, tú) antes de firmar.
questions.explanation: no está de más que takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa: Me parece mal que la gente no ______ (reciclar).
questions.explanation: me parece mal que takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'It seems great to me that you're coming to the party.'
questions.explanation: me parece + adjective + que takes the subjunctive: vengas.

activities.title: Charlando sobre planes
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends catch up, reacting to each other's news and opinions.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Al final voy a poder ir a tu boda.
lines.en: In the end I'll be able to go to your wedding.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¡Qué bien que vengas! Me parece genial que puedas venir.
lines.en: How great that you're coming! I think it's wonderful you can come.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Pero solo podré quedarme un día.
lines.en: But I'll only be able to stay one day.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¡Qué pena que no puedas quedarte más tiempo!
lines.en: What a shame you can't stay longer!

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Lo sé, tengo mucho trabajo estos días.
lines.en: I know, I have a lot of work these days.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bueno, no está de más que descanses un poco también.
lines.en: Well, it doesn't hurt for you to rest a bit too.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tienes razón. Me parece mal que trabaje tanto sin parar.
lines.en: You're right. I think it's wrong that I work so much without stopping.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exacto, me alegro de que por fin lo reconozcas.
lines.en: Exactly, I'm glad you finally admit it.

days.title: El imperativo negativo
days.objective: The learner can form the negative imperative for every person, recognising it as exactly the present subjunctive, with the pronoun moving before the verb.
days.paretoFocus: Telling someone not to do something is as common as telling them to do it, and the negative imperative is entirely built from a form the learner already has.
drills: Write the negative imperative of hablar, comer and escribir for tú.
Say aloud no lo hagas and no te vayas.
Write one sentence with a double pronoun in a negative command, like no se lo digas.

items: Recall a reaction phrase using qué pena que.
Remember the subjunctive of decir.
Recall the affirmative imperative of decir and its pronoun position.

activities.title: No lo hagas
activities.intro: Unlike the affirmative imperative learned at A2, which is not the subjunctive except in the usted/ustedes forms, the negative command form, across every person without exception, is exactly the present subjunctive. Pronouns that attach after the affirmative verb move to before the verb in the negative form.

items.hr: No te vayas todavía.
items.en: Don't leave yet.
items.note: irse negative imperative = present subjunctive vayas, reflexive pronoun moves before the verb

items.hr: No lo hagas así.
items.en: Don't do it that way.
items.note: hacer negative imperative = hagas, direct object pronoun before the verb

items.hr: No me esperes, llegaré tarde.
items.en: Don't wait for me, I'll be late.
items.note: esperar negative imperative = esperes, pronoun before the verb

items.hr: No habléis tan alto.
items.en: Don't speak so loud, all of you.
items.note: vosotros negative imperative = habléis, no pronoun here

items.hr: No se lo digas a nadie.
items.en: Don't tell it to anyone.
items.note: decir negative imperative with a double pronoun, se lo, both before the verb

activities.title: Órdenes negativas
activities.intro: Practise forming the negative imperative for different persons and pronoun combinations.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la negación correcta de '¡Dilo!'?
questions.explanation: the pronoun moves before the verb in the negative imperative, and the verb form is the present subjunctive, not the indicative.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'Don't wait for me' a un amigo?
questions.explanation: the pronoun me goes before the negative imperative, and the verb is the present subjunctive esperes.

questions.prompt: Completa: No ______ (hacer, tú) eso otra vez.
questions.explanation: the negative imperative of hacer is exactly the present subjunctive: hagas.

questions.prompt: Completa: No os ______ (ir) sin despediros.
questions.explanation: the vosotros negative imperative of irse is the present subjunctive: vayáis.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Don't tell it to anyone.'
questions.explanation: both pronouns, se lo, move before the negative imperative digas.

activities.title: Consejos de un padre
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A parent warns a teenager before a night out, using negative imperatives.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No vuelvas muy tarde esta noche, por favor.
lines.en: Don't come back too late tonight, please.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, no te preocupes tanto por mí.
lines.en: Okay, don't worry so much about me.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No hables con desconocidos si sales sola.
lines.en: Don't talk to strangers if you go out alone.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo sé, no lo hago nunca.
lines.en: I know, I never do.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No se lo digas a tu hermano, pero te dejo el coche.
lines.en: Don't tell your brother, but I'm letting you have the car.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¡Gracias! No se lo diré, te lo prometo.
lines.en: Thanks! I won't tell him, I promise.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Y no os quedéis sin gasolina, por favor.
lines.en: And don't run out of gas, please.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No te preocupes, llenaré el depósito antes.
lines.en: Don't worry, I'll fill the tank first.

days.title: Imperativo afirmativo y negativo juntos
days.objective: The learner can switch fluently between the affirmative and negative imperative, moving the pronoun position correctly each time.
days.paretoFocus: Giving and correcting instructions in the same breath is an everyday pattern, and getting the pronoun position wrong is the single most common imperative mistake.
drills: Write three sentences that give an affirmative command and then correct it with a negative one.
Say aloud dímelo and no me lo digas back to back.
Write one vosotros pair, affirmative then negative, with a reflexive verb.

items: Recall the negative imperative of hacer.
Remember why se lo digas comes before the verb.
Recall the vosotros negative imperative of ir.

activities.title: Dímelo, no me lo digas
activities.intro: The pronoun position flips completely between the two imperatives: it attaches after the verb in the affirmative and moves before it in the negative, which is built from the present subjunctive.

items.hr: Levántate ya, pero no te levantes de mal humor.
items.en: Get up now, but don't get up in a bad mood.
items.note: levantarse: levántate (affirmative) / no te levantes (negative)

items.hr: Cómpralo si te gusta, no lo compres si no.
items.en: Buy it if you like it, don't buy it if you don't.
items.note: comprarlo: cómpralo (affirmative) / no lo compres (negative)

items.hr: Dímelo ahora, no me lo digas luego.
items.en: Tell it to me now, don't tell it to me later.
items.note: decírmelo: dímelo (affirmative) / no me lo digas (negative), the hardest pronoun pair

items.hr: Sentaos aquí, no os sentéis allí.
items.en: Sit here, all of you, don't sit there.
items.note: sentaos (affirmative vosotros) / no os sentéis (negative vosotros)

items.hr: Ven conmigo, no vengas solo.
items.en: Come with me, don't come alone.
items.note: ven (affirmative) / no vengas (negative)

activities.title: Cambiando de sentido
activities.intro: Flip each command from one polarity to the other and relocate the pronoun as needed.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la negación de '¡Levántate!'?
questions.explanation: the pronoun moves before the negative form, which is the present subjunctive levantes.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la negación de '¡Dímelo!'?
questions.explanation: both pronouns move before the negative subjunctive form digas.

questions.prompt: Completa la negación: ¡Cállate! -> ¡No te ______!
questions.explanation: callarse negative imperative is the present subjunctive: te calles.

questions.prompt: Completa la negación: ¡Ven aquí! -> ¡No ______ aquí!
questions.explanation: venir negative imperative is the present subjunctive: vengas.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Don't buy it.'
questions.explanation: the pronoun lo moves before the negative subjunctive compres.

activities.title: Decidiendo una compra
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends debate a purchase, mixing affirmative and negative commands.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mira esta chaqueta, ¿la compro?
lines.en: Look at this jacket, should I buy it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cómprala si de verdad te gusta.
lines.en: Buy it if you really like it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No sé, es un poco cara.
lines.en: I don't know, it's a bit expensive.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Entonces no la compres, busca otra más barata.
lines.en: Then don't buy it, look for a cheaper one.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vale, dime qué te parece esta otra.
lines.en: Okay, tell me what you think of this other one.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No me la enseñes tan rápido, déjame verla bien.
lines.en: Don't show it to me so fast, let me see it properly.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perdona. Ahora sí, mírala con calma.
lines.en: Sorry. Now yes, look at it calmly.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Esta me gusta más, cómprate esta y no la otra.
lines.en: I like this one more, buy this one and not the other.

days.title: Cuando + subjuntivo para el futuro
days.objective: The learner can use cuando plus the subjunctive to describe a specific future moment, completing the pattern left open at A2.
days.paretoFocus: Talking about what will happen at a future moment defined by another event is a basic narrative skill, and Spanish structures it completely differently from English.
drills: Write one sentence with cuando plus the subjunctive about a future plan.
Say aloud the difference between cuando llego and cuando llegue.
Write one sentence combining the future tense with cuando plus the subjunctive.

items: Recall the negative imperative of comprar.
Remember the pronoun order in dímelo versus no me lo digas.
Recall the future tense of llegar.

activities.title: Un momento futuro
activities.intro: An earlier lesson taught cuando plus the present indicative only for a habitual, repeated action: 'Cuando viene, trae regalos'. This lesson completes the pattern: cuando plus the present subjunctive refers to a specific future moment, and Spanish never uses a future tense after cuando; 'cuando llegarás' is simply impossible.

items.hr: Cuando llegues, llámame.
items.en: When you arrive, call me.
items.note: a specific future moment: cuando + subjunctive

items.hr: Te lo diré cuando tenga tiempo.
items.en: I'll tell you when I have time.
items.note: future main clause, diré, combined with cuando + subjunctive

items.hr: Cuando seas mayor, lo entenderás.
items.en: When you're older, you'll understand it.
items.note: cuando + subjunctive, future main clause entenderás

items.hr: Cuando llego a casa, ceno enseguida.
items.en: When I get home, I have dinner right away.
items.note: a habitual, repeated action: cuando + present indicative, the pattern from A2

items.hr: Cuando llegue a casa, cenaré enseguida.
items.en: When I get home, I'll have dinner right away.
items.note: a specific future moment: cuando + subjunctive, never a future tense after cuando

activities.title: Un momento concreto
activities.intro: Practise distinguishing a habitual action from a specific future moment after cuando.

questions.prompt: Completa: Cuando ______ tiempo, te escribiré. (tener)
questions.explanation: a future moment after cuando always takes the present subjunctive; tendré is impossible after cuando, tengo is for habitual actions, and tenía is a past tense.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase describe una costumbre habitual, no un momento futuro concreto?
questions.explanation: present indicative after cuando marks a repeated habit; the other three describe a specific future moment and need the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa: Cuando ______ (ser) mayor, viajaré por el mundo.
questions.explanation: a future moment after cuando takes the present subjunctive of ser: sea.

questions.prompt: Completa (costumbre): Cuando ______ (hacer) frío, me pongo el abrigo.
questions.explanation: a habitual, repeated action after cuando keeps the present indicative.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Call me when you arrive.'
questions.explanation: a specific future moment after cuando takes the present subjunctive: llegues.

activities.title: Quedando para más tarde
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends arrange to meet later, using cuando plus the subjunctive for the future moment.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿A qué hora quedamos esta tarde?
lines.en: What time shall we meet this afternoon?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No lo sé todavía, cuando salga del trabajo te aviso.
lines.en: I don't know yet, when I leave work I'll let you know.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vale. Llámame cuando estés cerca de casa.
lines.en: Okay. Call me when you're near home.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo haré. Normalmente cuando salgo tardo media hora en llegar.
lines.en: I will. Usually when I leave it takes me half an hour to get there.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Entonces cuando llegues, ya tendré la cena lista.
lines.en: Then when you arrive, I'll already have dinner ready.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfecto, cuando tengo hambre siempre como rápido.
lines.en: Perfect, when I'm hungry I always eat fast.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Cuando terminemos de cenar, podemos ver una película.
lines.en: When we finish having dinner, we can watch a movie.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me parece perfecto, nos vemos cuando salga entonces.
lines.en: Sounds perfect to me, see you when I leave then.

days.title: Otras conjunciones temporales
days.objective: The learner can use en cuanto, tan pronto como, hasta que, mientras, después de que and antes de que correctly, knowing that only antes de que always takes the subjunctive.
days.paretoFocus: These conjunctions cover most of the ways to sequence events in a story or a plan, and antes de que is the one genuine exception to the known/unknown pattern that must simply be memorised.
drills: Write one sentence with en cuanto about a future plan.
Write one sentence with hasta que in the past and one in the future.
Say aloud a sentence with antes de que, remembering it always takes the subjunctive.

items: Recall the difference between cuando llego and cuando llegue.
Remember why cuando never takes a future tense.
Recall a sentence using cuando plus the subjunctive.

activities.title: En cuanto, hasta que, antes de que
activities.intro: Most time conjunctions follow the same split as cuando: the indicative for a completed or habitual moment, the subjunctive for a future one still to come. Antes de que is the one exception and always takes the subjunctive, because by definition the action it introduces has not yet happened relative to the main clause.

items.hr: En cuanto llegues, avísame.
items.en: As soon as you arrive, let me know.
items.note: en cuanto + subjunctive, a future moment

items.hr: Tan pronto como tenga noticias, te escribo.
items.en: As soon as I have news, I'll write to you.
items.note: tan pronto como works exactly like en cuanto, same known/unknown split

items.hr: Esperé hasta que llegó el autobús.
items.en: I waited until the bus arrived.
items.note: hasta que + indicative, a past completed event

items.hr: Voy a esperar hasta que llegues.
items.en: I'm going to wait until you arrive.
items.note: hasta que + subjunctive, a future moment

items.hr: Antes de que te vayas, quiero darte esto.
items.en: Before you leave, I want to give you this.
items.note: antes de que always takes the subjunctive, unlike the other time conjunctions

items.hr: Después de que termine la reunión, comeremos algo.
items.en: After the meeting ends, we'll eat something.
items.note: después de que + subjunctive, a future moment

activities.title: El orden de los sucesos
activities.intro: Practise the time conjunctions and the one that never follows the known/unknown split.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué conjunción temporal lleva siempre subjuntivo, sin importar si el momento ya pasó?
questions.explanation: unlike the others, which follow the known/unknown split, antes de que always takes the subjunctive because its action has not yet happened relative to the main clause.

questions.prompt: Completa correctamente: Tan pronto como ______ algo, te llamo. (saber)
questions.explanation: a future moment after a time conjunction takes the present subjunctive; sé is present indicative, sabía and supe are past tenses.

questions.prompt: Completa: Mientras tú ______ (cocinar), yo pongo la mesa.
questions.explanation: a habitual, simultaneous action after mientras takes the present indicative.

questions.prompt: Completa: Antes de que ______ (empezar) la película, apaga el móvil.
questions.explanation: antes de que always takes the subjunctive; empezar changes z to c before e.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Wait until I arrive.'
questions.explanation: a future moment after hasta que takes the present subjunctive: llegue.

activities.title: Antes de salir de viaje
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends coordinate final details before a trip.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: En cuanto llegues al aeropuerto, mándame un mensaje.
lines.en: As soon as you arrive at the airport, send me a message.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, y antes de que salga el vuelo te llamo también.
lines.en: Okay, and before the flight leaves I'll call you too.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perfecto. Voy a esperar hasta que me confirmes que ha salido.
lines.en: Perfect. I'll wait until you confirm it's left.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ayer esperé hasta que llegó tu mensaje, ahora te toca a ti.
lines.en: Yesterday I waited until your message arrived, now it's your turn.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mientras esperas en el aeropuerto, descansa un poco.
lines.en: While you wait at the airport, rest a little.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo haré. Después de que aterrice, te escribo enseguida.
lines.en: I will. After it lands, I'll write to you right away.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Genial. Antes de que se me olvide, ten cuidado con las maletas.
lines.en: Great. Before I forget, be careful with your bags.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No te preocupes, en cuanto pueda te cuento todo.
lines.en: Don't worry, as soon as I can I'll tell you everything.

days.title: Oraciones finales: para que
days.objective: The learner can express purpose with para que plus the subjunctive when two subjects are involved, contrasted with para plus infinitive for one subject.
days.paretoFocus: Explaining why you're doing something for someone else's benefit is a constant part of everyday explanation, and para que always requires the subjunctive.
drills: Write one pair of sentences, para + infinitive and para que + subjunctive, about the same situation.
Say aloud a sentence with para que about helping a friend.
Write one vosotros sentence with para que.

items: Recall why antes de que always takes the subjunctive.
Remember the difference between hasta que with a past event and a future one.
Recall a sentence using en cuanto.

activities.title: Para que + subjuntivo
activities.intro: Para que always takes the subjunctive and always involves two different subjects: the person acting and the person the action is for. With one subject, para plus the infinitive is used instead, with no que.

items.hr: Te lo explico para que lo entiendas.
items.en: I explain it to you so that you understand it.
items.note: para que + subjunctive, two different subjects

items.hr: Estudio para aprobar el examen.
items.en: I study to pass the exam.
items.note: para + infinitive, same subject, contrast

items.hr: Hablo despacio para que me entiendas mejor.
items.en: I speak slowly so that you understand me better.
items.note: para que + subjunctive

items.hr: Os doy la llave para que entréis sin esperar.
items.en: I give you the key so that you all can go in without waiting.
items.note: para que + subjunctive, vosotros form entréis

items.hr: Compra pan para que no falte nada en la cena.
items.en: Buy bread so that nothing is missing at dinner.
items.note: para que + subjunctive

activities.title: Con un propósito
activities.intro: Practise para que with the subjunctive against para plus infinitive.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta con dos sujetos distintos? Hablo despacio para que ______. (entender, tú)
questions.explanation: para que with a different subject always takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Elige la frase correcta para el mismo sujeto.
options: Estudio para que apruebe el examen.
Estudio para que apruebo el examen.
Estudio para que aprobaré el examen.
questions.explanation: with one subject, para plus the infinitive is used, not para que plus the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa: Os doy la llave para que ______ (entrar, vosotros) sin esperar.
questions.explanation: para que with vosotros as the subject takes the subjunctive entréis.

questions.prompt: Completa: Compra pan para que no ______ (faltar) nada en la cena.
questions.explanation: para que always takes the subjunctive: falte.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I explain it to you so that you understand it.'
questions.explanation: para que with two subjects always takes the subjunctive: entiendas.

activities.title: Explicando la lección
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A tutor explains something to a student, using para que and para plus infinitive.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No entiendo este ejercicio de matemáticas.
lines.en: I don't understand this math exercise.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Voy a explicártelo despacio para que lo entiendas bien.
lines.en: I'm going to explain it slowly so you understand it well.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Gracias. Necesito estudiar mucho para aprobar este curso.
lines.en: Thanks. I need to study a lot to pass this course.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Te voy a dar unos ejemplos para que practiques en casa.
lines.en: I'm going to give you some examples so you practise at home.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perfecto. ¿Me dejas tus apuntes para que los revise?
lines.en: Perfect. Will you lend me your notes so I can review them?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, te los doy para que los copies esta tarde.
lines.en: Sure, I'll give them to you so you can copy them this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Gracias por tu ayuda, quiero aprobar sin problemas.
lines.en: Thanks for your help, I want to pass without problems.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De nada, para eso estamos, para que aprendas bien.
lines.en: You're welcome, that's what we're here for, so you learn well.

days.title: Oraciones concesivas: aunque
days.objective: The learner can use aunque with either the indicative for a known fact or the subjunctive for a concession or something unknown, understanding that both are grammatical and the mood changes the meaning.
days.paretoFocus: Aunque appears everywhere in speech and writing, and the mood you pick after it silently changes what you are claiming to know, which makes it a meaning choice rather than a grammar rule.
drills: Write one pair of sentences with aunque, indicative then subjunctive, about the same topic.
Say aloud why the mood after aunque is a meaning choice, not a grammar error.
Write one sentence with aunque about something you genuinely don't know yet.

items: Recall a sentence using para que.
Remember why para que always needs two subjects.
Recall the difference between para and para que.

activities.title: Un hecho conocido o una concesión
activities.intro: Aunque can take either mood, and both are correct: the indicative asserts the fact as known to the speaker, while the subjunctive presents it as unknown or simply concedes the point without asserting it. Neither version is wrong; the mood changes what is being claimed.

items.hr: Aunque llueve, salgo a correr.
items.en: Although it's raining, I'm going out for a run.
items.note: indicative, a known fact: it really is raining

items.hr: Aunque llueva, saldré a correr.
items.en: Even if it rains, I'll go out for a run.
items.note: subjunctive, a concession about something uncertain: it may or may not rain

items.hr: Aunque es caro, lo voy a comprar.
items.en: Although it's expensive, I'm going to buy it.
items.note: indicative, a known fact: the speaker knows the price

items.hr: Aunque sea caro, lo compraré.
items.en: Even if it's expensive, I'll buy it.
items.note: subjunctive, a concession regardless of the actual price

items.hr: Aunque no conozco bien la ciudad, puedo ayudarte.
items.en: Although I don't know the city well, I can help you.
items.note: indicative, a known fact about the speaker's own knowledge

activities.title: Hecho conocido o concesión
activities.intro: Practise choosing the mood after aunque based on whether the fact is known or conceded.

questions.prompt: El hablante sabe que hace frío pero sale igual. ¿Qué opción es correcta?
questions.explanation: a known fact after aunque takes the indicative; haga would present it as unknown, and the other options use tenses that don't fit here.

questions.prompt: El hablante no sabe si tendrán tiempo, pero concede el punto igualmente. ¿Qué opción es correcta?
questions.explanation: an unknown or conceded situation after aunque takes the subjunctive; the indicative options wrongly assert it as known, or use tenses that don't fit a present concession.

questions.prompt: Completa: Aunque ______ (ser) tarde, voy a llamarla ahora mismo, porque ya sé la hora.
questions.explanation: the speaker states knowing the time as a fact, so aunque takes the indicative here.

questions.prompt: Completa: Aunque no ______ (llover) mañana, llevaré paraguas por si acaso.
questions.explanation: the speaker doesn't know if it will rain, so aunque takes the subjunctive here.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Although he is rich, he lives simply.'
questions.explanation: a known fact after aunque takes the indicative: es.

activities.title: Planes bajo la lluvia
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends discuss weekend plans, using aunque with both moods.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Van a anunciar lluvia para el sábado, ¿verdad?
lines.en: They're forecasting rain for Saturday, right?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, aunque llueva, yo pienso salir de todas formas.
lines.en: Yes, but even if it rains, I plan to go out anyway.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo también. Aunque hace frío ahora mismo, mañana dicen que mejora.
lines.en: Me too. Although it's cold right now, they say it'll improve tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Aunque no conozco bien la zona, podemos ir a ese parque nuevo.
lines.en: Although I don't know the area well, we can go to that new park.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buena idea. Aunque esté cerrado, siempre podemos pasear por el centro.
lines.en: Good idea. Even if it's closed, we can always walk around downtown.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale. Aunque es un poco lejos, iremos andando si hace bueno.
lines.en: Okay. Although it's a bit far, we'll walk there if the weather's nice.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Aunque llueva mucho, siempre podemos entrar en algún sitio.
lines.en: Even if it rains a lot, we can always go into somewhere.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cierto, aunque prefiero que salga el sol, la verdad.
lines.en: True, although I prefer the sun comes out, honestly.

days.title: Oraciones de modo y lugar
days.objective: The learner can use como, donde and según with either the indicative for a known way or place, or the subjunctive for an open, unspecified one.
days.paretoFocus: Giving someone freedom of choice, about how to do something or where to do it, is a common and natural act of politeness that needs the subjunctive to sound right.
drills: Write one pair of sentences with como, indicative then subjunctive.
Say aloud vive donde quieras and vivo donde nací back to back.
Write one sentence with según about something not yet decided.

items: Recall the difference between aunque with the indicative and with the subjunctive.
Remember a sentence using antes de que.
Recall a sentence using para que.

activities.title: Como, donde, según
activities.intro: Como, donde and según follow the same known/unknown split as aunque and the time conjunctions: indicative when the way, place or source is specific and known, subjunctive when it's still undecided, unspecified or open to more than one answer.

items.hr: Hazlo como quieras.
items.en: Do it however you like.
items.note: como + subjunctive, an open, unspecified way

items.hr: Lo hice como me explicaste.
items.en: I did it the way you explained to me.
items.note: como + indicative, a known, specific way

items.hr: Vive donde quieras.
items.en: Live wherever you like.
items.note: donde + subjunctive, an open, unspecified place

items.hr: Vivo donde nací.
items.en: I live where I was born.
items.note: donde + indicative, a known, specific place

items.hr: Según digas, cambiaremos de planes.
items.en: Depending on what you say, we'll change plans.
items.note: según + subjunctive, depending on something not yet said

activities.title: Un modo o un lugar libre
activities.intro: Choose indicative or subjunctive after como, donde or según depending on what's known.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta cuando el lugar es libre, no concreto? Vive donde ______. (querer, tú)
questions.explanation: an open, unspecified place after donde takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Elige la frase correcta para un lugar conocido y concreto.
questions.explanation: a known, specific place after donde takes the indicative.

questions.prompt: Completa: Hazlo como ______ (querer, tú), a mí no me importa cómo lo hagas.
questions.explanation: an open, unspecified way after como takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Completa: Lo hice como me lo ______ (explicar, tú) la semana pasada.
questions.explanation: a known, specific way already explained after como takes the indicative, here the indefinido.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'According to what you say, everything is fine.'
questions.explanation: según reporting what is actually being said takes the indicative: dices.

activities.title: Planeando un viaje libre
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends plan a trip with no fixed itinerary, giving each other freedom of choice.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Adónde quieres que vayamos este verano?
lines.en: Where do you want us to go this summer?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: La verdad, vamos donde tú prefieras, no tengo preferencia.
lines.en: Honestly, let's go wherever you prefer, I have no preference.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vale, según digas tú también, decidimos entre los dos.
lines.en: Okay, depending on what you say too, we'll decide together.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Hagámoslo como te resulte más fácil organizarlo.
lines.en: Let's do it however is easiest for you to organize.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo siempre viajo como me sale, sin mucho plan.
lines.en: I always travel however it comes out, without much of a plan.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfecto, entonces vamos donde nos apetezca cada día.
lines.en: Perfect, then we'll go wherever we feel like each day.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Según cómo esté el tiempo, decidimos la ruta.
lines.en: Depending on the weather, we'll decide the route.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me encanta ese plan, hagámoslo como quieras.
lines.en: I love that plan, let's do it however you like.

days.title: Consecuencia: así que, tan... que
days.objective: Link a cause and its result inside one sentence using así que, de modo que, tan... que and tanto... que.
days.paretoFocus: Narrating and explaining are full of results (it was so cold that we stayed home); these connectors are everyday and always take the indicative.
drills: Write three sentences describing a result using así que.
Rewrite two English 'so...that' sentences using tan... que or tanto... que.
Say aloud one sentence with de modo que about something that happened today.

items: Recall the connectors from the concession and manner clauses lessons.
Say one sentence using the pluscuamperfecto about something already finished.
Explain when tanto changes to tan, tanta or tantos.

activities.title: La consecuencia
activities.intro: Result clauses join a cause and its effect in one sentence. They always take the indicative, since a result is a fact, not a hypothesis.

items.hr: Llovía mucho, así que nos quedamos en casa.
items.en: It was raining a lot, so we stayed home.
items.note: así que introduces a plain result, always indicative

items.hr: No estudió nada, de modo que suspendió el examen.
items.en: He didn't study at all, so he failed the exam.
items.note: de modo que works the same way as así que

items.hr: Hace tanto frío que no puedo sentir los dedos.
items.en: It's so cold that I can't feel my fingers.
items.note: tanto agrees with the noun frío, unlike tan before an adjective

items.hr: El piso es tan pequeño que no cabe el sofá.
items.en: The flat is so small that the sofa doesn't fit.
items.note: tan goes before an adjective or adverb

items.hr: Tiene tantos libros que ya no le caben en las estanterías.
items.en: He has so many books that they no longer fit on the shelves.
items.note: tanto/a/os/as agrees in gender and number with the noun

activities.title: Así que y tan... que
activities.intro: Practise linking a cause with its result.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? 'No tenía dinero, ___ no pudo viajar.'
questions.explanation: así que introduces the plain result of not having money.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué falta? 'Es ___ tarde que no llegaremos a tiempo.'
questions.explanation: tan goes directly before tarde, an adverb here; tanto and its agreeing forms go with nouns.

questions.prompt: Cuando llegó el jefe, Marta ya ___ (terminar) el informe, así que se fue tranquila.
questions.explanation: The pluscuamperfecto marks an action finished before another past moment.

questions.prompt: Tiene ___ (tanto) paciencia que nunca se enfada.
questions.explanation: tanta agrees with the feminine singular noun paciencia.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'She has so much work that she can't go out.'
questions.explanation: tanto agrees with trabajo, and que introduces the result.

activities.title: Un fin de semana lluvioso
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A beach weekend got rained out; recount what went wrong and how it turned out, working in así que and tanto... que as you go.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tal el viaje a la playa?
lines.en: How was the trip to the beach?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Fatal. Llovía tanto que no pudimos salir del hotel.
lines.en: Terrible. It was raining so much that we couldn't leave the hotel.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vaya faena. ¿Y qué hicisteis?
lines.en: What a shame. What did you do?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Nada, así que nos quedamos jugando a las cartas todo el día.
lines.en: Nothing, so we stayed playing cards all day.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Al menos comisteis bien?
lines.en: At least did you eat well?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, el restaurante del hotel era tan bueno que repetimos dos veces.
lines.en: Yes, the hotel restaurant was so good that we went back twice.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Entonces no fue un desastre total.
lines.en: So it wasn't a total disaster.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, pero tenía tantas ganas de nadar que volveré en verano.
lines.en: No, but I wanted to swim so much that I'll go back in summer.

days.title: La causa, otra vez
days.objective: Express cause using como, ya que, puesto que, debido a, gracias a and por culpa de, choosing the right register and position.
days.paretoFocus: Causal connectors are essential for explanations and justification in speech and writing at this level.
drills: Write two reasons for missing an appointment, each opening with Como.
Turn a spoken porque sentence into a formal one with puesto que.
Write one sentence blaming the weather and one crediting a friend for something going well.

items: Recall three connectors that mean because, in different registers.
Say one sentence using a present subjunctive recommendation.
Explain the difference between debido a and como.

activities.title: La causa, otra vez
activities.intro: Cause has more shades than porque suggests: some words open the sentence and take a full clause, others attach directly to a plain noun, and the register runs from casual speech to formal writing or written justification.

items.hr: Como no tenía las llaves, llamé al timbre.
items.en: Since I didn't have the keys, I rang the bell.
items.note: como + cause always goes at the start of the sentence

items.hr: Ya que estás aquí, ayúdame con esto.
items.en: Since you're here, help me with this.
items.note: ya que can also open a sentence, more neutral than como

items.hr: Puesto que no hay más preguntas, terminamos la reunión.
items.en: Since there are no more questions, we're ending the meeting.
items.note: puesto que, a more formal register

items.hr: El vuelo se retrasó debido a la niebla.
items.en: The flight was delayed due to the fog.
items.note: debido a + noun; before a full clause it becomes debido a que

items.hr: Aprobé gracias a tu ayuda, pero perdí el autobús por culpa del tráfico.
items.en: I passed thanks to your help, but I missed the bus because of the traffic.
items.note: gracias a for a positive cause, por culpa de for a negative one

activities.title: Practica la causa
activities.intro: Choose the right causal connector for each context.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la opción correcta? '___ no tenía coche, fui en autobús.'
questions.explanation: Como + a full clause at the start of the sentence means since/because.

questions.prompt: 'El partido se canceló ___ la lluvia.'
questions.explanation: debido a attaches directly to a noun phrase like la lluvia; como, ya que and puesto que need a full clause after them.

questions.prompt: Llegamos tarde ___ culpa de un atasco.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is por culpa de.

questions.prompt: El médico me recomienda que ___ (dejar) de fumar, ya que es malo para la salud.
questions.explanation: recomendar que triggers the present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I passed thanks to your help.'
questions.explanation: gracias a introduces a positive cause.

activities.title: Un atasco y una reunión
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Explain why you missed a meeting, using the fuller set of causal connectors.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Por qué no viniste a la reunión?
lines.en: Why didn't you come to the meeting?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Llegué tarde por culpa de un atasco enorme.
lines.en: I arrived late because of a huge traffic jam.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vaya. ¿Y qué te dijeron?
lines.en: Wow. And what did they tell you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Nada, ya que el jefe tampoco pudo venir.
lines.en: Nothing, since the boss couldn't come either.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Menos mal. ¿Se aplazó la reunión?
lines.en: Good thing. Was the meeting postponed?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, puesto que faltaba la mitad del equipo.
lines.en: Yes, since half the team was missing.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cuándo es la nueva fecha?
lines.en: And when is the new date?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: El viernes, debido a que el jueves hay otro evento.
lines.en: Friday, due to there being another event on Thursday.

days.title: Condiciones más allá de si
days.objective: Express conditions other than with si, using siempre que, con tal de que, a menos que and en caso de que with the present subjunctive.
days.paretoFocus: These connectors are common in agreements, plans and instructions, and they extend the conditional system beyond si without adding any new tense.
drills: Write three sentences agreeing to lend something, each with a different condition attached.
Say one warning about what to do if a plan falls through.
Turn a si sentence about weekend plans into one using a different condition word.

items: Recall the rule for si with the present indicative.
List two connectors that always take the subjunctive.
Say one sentence with querer que and the present subjunctive.

activities.title: Condiciones sin si
activities.intro: Besides si, Spanish has a handful of fixed phrases that set up a condition and pull the following verb into the present subjunctive: one for permission with an exception, one for a proviso, one that rules a case out, and one that warns of a possibility. None of them has a past-tense version in this course.

items.hr: Puedes venir siempre que llegues antes de las nueve.
items.en: You can come as long as you arrive before nine.
items.note: siempre que + present subjunctive means as long as / provided that

items.hr: Te ayudo con tal de que me ayudes tú también.
items.en: I'll help you provided that you help me too.
items.note: con tal de que + subjunctive

items.hr: Saldremos a menos que llueva.
items.en: We'll go out unless it rains.
items.note: a menos que + subjunctive

items.hr: En caso de que necesites algo, llámame.
items.en: In case you need anything, call me.
items.note: en caso de que + subjunctive

items.hr: Iremos al parque siempre que haga buen tiempo, a menos que tengas otro plan.
items.en: We'll go to the park as long as the weather's good, unless you have another plan.
items.note: combining two condition connectors in one sentence

activities.title: Practica las condiciones
activities.intro: Choose the right condition connector and mood.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Te presto el coche con tal de que lo ___ con cuidado.'
questions.explanation: con tal de que always takes the present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: 'Llévate el paraguas ___ empiece a llover.'
questions.explanation: en caso de que means in case.

questions.prompt: No podremos ir a menos que ___ (tener) tiempo libre el sábado.
questions.explanation: a menos que requires the present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Quiero que me ___ (avisar) en caso de que haya algún problema.
questions.explanation: querer que also triggers the present subjunctive, here combined with en caso de que.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We'll go out unless it rains.'
questions.explanation: a menos que + present subjunctive expresses unless.

activities.title: Planes para la excursión
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Agree on a plan for Saturday, stacking several conditions.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Vienes a la excursión del sábado?
lines.en: Are you coming to Saturday's trip?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, siempre que no llueva.
lines.en: Yes, as long as it doesn't rain.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Y si llueve, ¿qué hacemos?
lines.en: And if it rains, what do we do?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En caso de que llueva, nos quedamos en el pueblo.
lines.en: In case it rains, we'll stay in the village.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vale. ¿Puedo llevar a mi hermano?
lines.en: Okay. Can I bring my brother?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, con tal de que se porte bien.
lines.en: Sure, provided he behaves.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Te lo prometo. ¿A qué hora salimos?
lines.en: I promise. What time do we leave?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A las ocho, a menos que alguien llegue tarde.
lines.en: At eight, unless someone arrives late.

days.title: Comparativas con de lo que
days.objective: Form comparative clauses correctly, using de lo que before a following clause instead of que, and igual de... que for equal comparisons.
days.paretoFocus: This is a common learner error that instantly signals a non-native level; the de lo que rule is small but very high-frequency in real opinions.
drills: Write two sentences using de lo que with a following clause.
Write one sentence with igual de... que.
Correct a wrong sentence that uses que instead of de lo que.

items: Recall when to use de lo que instead of que.
Say one sentence using the negative imperative.
Explain the agreement of del que and de la que.

activities.title: Comparar con una cláusula
activities.intro: When más or menos is followed by a full clause rather than just a noun, Spanish uses de lo que, not que. When the comparison is with a noun, del que / de la que agree with that noun. For equal comparisons with adjectives or adverbs, use igual de... que.

items.hr: Es más difícil de lo que parece.
items.en: It's more difficult than it seems.
items.note: before a clause, de lo que replaces que

items.hr: Gastamos más dinero del que teníamos.
items.en: We spent more money than we had.
items.note: del que agrees with dinero, masculine

items.hr: El examen fue más largo de lo que pensábamos.
items.en: The exam was longer than we thought.

items.hr: Este piso es igual de caro que el otro.
items.en: This flat is just as expensive as the other one.
items.note: igual de + adjective + que, for equal comparisons

items.hr: Habla igual de rápido que su hermana.
items.en: He speaks just as fast as his sister.
items.note: igual de also works with adverbs

activities.title: De lo que e igual de
activities.intro: Choose que, de lo que or del que correctly.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'El proyecto es más complicado ___ imaginábamos.'
questions.explanation: Before a clause, use de lo que, not que alone.

questions.prompt: 'Gastamos más tiempo ___ teníamos.'
questions.explanation: del que agrees with the masculine noun tiempo.

questions.prompt: Este coche es igual de rápido ___ el mío.
questions.explanation: igual de + adjective is followed by que, not de lo que, since no clause follows.

questions.prompt: No ___ (tú, hablar) tan alto, por favor, es más molesto de lo que crees.
questions.explanation: The negative imperative uses the present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'It's more difficult than it seems.'
questions.explanation: de lo que introduces the comparison because a clause follows.

activities.title: Comentando un examen
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Yesterday's exam turned out harder than expected; compare it with today's using the clause comparative and an equal comparison.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tal el examen de ayer?
lines.en: How was yesterday's exam?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Fatal, fue más difícil de lo que esperaba.
lines.en: Terrible, it was more difficult than I expected.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿En serio? A mí me pareció fácil.
lines.en: Really? It seemed easy to me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pues a mí me costó más tiempo del que tenía.
lines.en: Well, it took me more time than I had.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y el de matemáticas?
lines.en: And the maths one?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ese fue igual de difícil que el de ayer.
lines.en: That one was just as difficult as yesterday's.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Menos mal que ya se acabaron.
lines.en: Good thing they're over now.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, aunque estudié menos de lo que debería.
lines.en: Yes, although I studied less than I should have.

days.title: Indicativo o subjuntivo: repaso
days.objective: Apply one decision procedure to choose indicative or subjunctive across all types of adverbial clauses covered so far.
days.paretoFocus: Ten separate rules are unusable in real time; a single test, known or habitual fact versus future, unknown or hypothetical, predicts the mood in every case.
drills: Write one pair of sentences with aunque, one indicative and one subjunctive.
Explain out loud the one-test decision procedure.
Rewrite three earlier example sentences from memory.

items: Recall the general rule for indicative versus subjunctive.
List three time conjunctions that always take the subjunctive.
Say one sentence with a place clause using donde.

activities.title: Un solo test
activities.intro: One rule covers every adverbial clause seen so far: a known or habitual fact takes the indicative, and something not yet realised, future or unknown takes the subjunctive. Cause is always a stated fact, so it is always indicative; conditions beyond si are always subjunctive, because they describe something not yet settled.

items.hr: Regla general: hecho conocido o habitual = indicativo; algo no realizado, futuro o desconocido = subjuntivo.
items.en: General rule: a known or habitual fact takes the indicative; something not yet realised, future or unknown takes the subjunctive.
items.note: the one-test decision procedure

items.hr: Cuando llego a casa, ceno. / Cuando llegue a casa, cenaré.
items.en: When I get home, I have dinner. / When I get home, I'll have dinner.
items.note: habit = indicative, future = subjunctive

items.hr: Aunque llueve, salgo. / Aunque llueva, saldré.
items.en: Although it's raining, I'm going out. / Even if it rains, I'll go out.
items.note: known fact = indicative, hypothetical concession = subjunctive

items.hr: Como siempre dice la verdad, le creo.
items.en: Since he always tells the truth, I believe him.
items.note: cause is always indicative, it states a fact

items.hr: Te ayudo con tal de que me lo pidas por favor.
items.en: I'll help you provided that you ask me nicely.
items.note: condition beyond si is always subjunctive, no exceptions

activities.title: Indicativo o subjuntivo
activities.intro: Apply the one-test rule to choose the correct mood.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Aunque ___ mucho dinero, no soy feliz.' (hecho real: sí tengo dinero)
questions.explanation: A known fact keeps the indicative even after aunque.

questions.prompt: 'En cuanto ___ la noticia, te llamaré.'
questions.explanation: A future time clause always takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Puesto que ya ___ (saber, tú) la respuesta, dímela.
questions.explanation: Cause states a fact, so it stays in the indicative.

questions.prompt: Marta busca un lugar donde ___ (poder) trabajar tranquila.
questions.explanation: The place is not yet a specific known one, so the subjunctive applies.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I'll help you provided that you ask me nicely.'
questions.explanation: con tal de que always takes the subjunctive.

activities.title: Planes con condiciones
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Negotiate coming to a party, mixing several adverbial clauses.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Vendrás a la fiesta aunque tengas trabajo?
lines.en: Will you come to the party even if you have work?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, aunque tenga trabajo, iré un rato.
lines.en: Yes, even if I have work, I'll go for a while.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y si al final no puedes?
lines.en: And if in the end you can't?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En cuanto sepa algo, te aviso.
lines.en: As soon as I know something, I'll let you know.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vale. Como siempre llegas tarde, te espero en la puerta.
lines.en: Okay. Since you're always late, I'll wait for you at the door.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Qué gracioso. Llegaré a tiempo, siempre que no haya tráfico.
lines.en: Very funny. I'll arrive on time, as long as there's no traffic.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Eso espero.
lines.en: I hope so.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tranquilo, cuando llegue, te escribo.
lines.en: Don't worry, when I arrive, I'll text you.

days.title: Conectores del discurso
days.objective: Link ideas across sentences using discourse connectors for contrast, consequence, addition and summary, in writing and speech.
days.paretoFocus: These connectors are graded directly in the writing task and are what turns separate sentences into an argument.
drills: Write one short paragraph using sin embargo and por lo tanto.
Pair up por un lado with por otro in one sentence.
Close an argument with en resumen.

items: Recall a consequence connector from an earlier lesson.
Say one sentence with a consecutive clause.
List two contrast connectors and explain the difference between them.

activities.title: Los conectores
activities.intro: Discourse connectors link separate sentences into one argument: sin embargo and en cambio mark contrast, por lo tanto marks consequence, además marks addition, and por un lado / por otro lado / en resumen organise a whole paragraph.

items.hr: El piso es pequeño; sin embargo, tiene mucha luz.
items.en: The flat is small; however, it has a lot of light.
items.note: sin embargo = contrast, like however

items.hr: No estudió nada; por lo tanto, suspendió.
items.en: He didn't study at all; therefore, he failed.
items.note: por lo tanto = consequence

items.hr: El trabajo está bien pagado; además, tiene buen horario.
items.en: The job is well paid; besides, it has good hours.
items.note: además = addition

items.hr: A mí me gusta el campo; en cambio, a mi hermana le gusta la ciudad.
items.en: I like the countryside; whereas my sister likes the city.
items.note: en cambio contrasts two different subjects

items.hr: Por un lado, el piso es barato; por otro, está muy lejos del centro. En resumen, no es la opción ideal.
items.en: On the one hand, the flat is cheap; on the other, it's very far from the centre. In short, it's not the ideal option.
items.note: por un lado / por otro pair up, en resumen closes an argument

activities.title: Conecta las ideas
activities.intro: Choose the connector that fits the logic of each sentence.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Llovía mucho; ___, decidimos salir igualmente.'
questions.explanation: There is a contrast between the rain and the decision to go out anyway.

questions.prompt: 'No tiene experiencia; ___, no le dieron el puesto.'
questions.explanation: por lo tanto introduces a consequence.

questions.prompt: El hotel es caro; tiene piscina y gimnasio. ___, está muy bien situado.
questions.explanation: Además adds a further point in the same direction, after a short list of extras.

questions.prompt: Hacía mucho calor, así ___ abrimos las ventanas.
questions.explanation: así que is the fixed result connector.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'On the one hand it's cheap, on the other it's far away.'
questions.explanation: por un lado and por otro pair up to present two sides.

activities.title: Dos trabajos, dos opiniones
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Weigh up two job offers using discourse connectors.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tal el trabajo nuevo?
lines.en: How's the new job?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Por un lado, pagan bien; por otro, el horario es horrible.
lines.en: On the one hand, they pay well; on the other, the schedule is terrible.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y el otro trabajo que te ofrecieron?
lines.en: And the other job they offered you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ese paga menos; en cambio, tengo más tiempo libre.
lines.en: That one pays less; whereas I have more free time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuál vas a elegir?
lines.en: Which one will you choose?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Todavía no lo sé; sin embargo, el tiempo libre me importa mucho.
lines.en: I still don't know; however, free time matters a lot to me.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tiene sentido. ¿Y el dinero?
lines.en: That makes sense. And the money?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No es suficiente; por lo tanto, tendré que pensarlo bien.
lines.en: It's not enough; therefore, I'll have to think it over carefully.

days.title: Un argumento bien conectado
days.objective: Write and speak a short connected argument that states an opinion, gives reasons, contrasts a counterpoint and closes with a conclusion, using the block's connectors.
days.paretoFocus: This is the opinion composition task in miniature: an argument is graded on cohesion, not just on grammar.
drills: Write a five-sentence opinion paragraph using at least three connectors.
Say your paragraph aloud without reading it.
Rewrite your conclusion using en resumen.

items: Recall the structure of an opinion paragraph.
Say one causal sentence with puesto que.
List three connectors of contrast.

activities.title: Un argumento completo
activities.intro: A short opinion argument follows a shape: an opening opinion, both sides of the issue, a pivot to your own conclusion, extra support, and a closing summary. The connectors from the previous lesson are what carry that shape.

items.hr: En mi opinión, trabajar desde casa es mejor que ir a una oficina.
items.en: In my opinion, working from home is better than going to an office.
items.note: opening an opinion

items.hr: Por un lado, ahorras tiempo; por otro, a veces te sientes solo.
items.en: On the one hand, you save time; on the other, you sometimes feel alone.
items.note: presenting both sides

items.hr: Sin embargo, creo que las ventajas son mayores que los inconvenientes.
items.en: However, I think the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
items.note: pivoting to your conclusion with sin embargo

items.hr: Además, cada vez más empresas lo permiten, así que es una tendencia real.
items.en: Besides, more and more companies allow it, so it's a real trend.
items.note: extra support, chaining además with así que

items.hr: En resumen, aunque no es perfecto, prefiero trabajar desde casa.
items.en: In short, although it's not perfect, I prefer working from home.
items.note: closing with en resumen and a concession

activities.title: Construye el argumento
activities.intro: Complete an argument by choosing the connector that fits each step.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué conector cierra mejor un argumento?
questions.explanation: en resumen signals a closing summary.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué conector introduce un contraste con lo dicho antes?
questions.explanation: sin embargo introduces a contrast with the previous idea.

questions.prompt: Vivir en el campo es tranquilo; ___, hay menos oportunidades de trabajo.
questions.explanation: sin embargo contrasts the calm of the countryside with fewer job opportunities.

questions.prompt: ___ no tengo coche, prefiero vivir cerca del centro.
questions.explanation: A formal causal connector opens the sentence and states the reason first.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'In short, I prefer working from home.'
questions.explanation: en resumen opens the closing sentence of the argument.

activities.title: Un debate sobre las redes
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Build a short spoken argument about social media, step by step.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Tú qué opinas sobre las redes sociales?
lines.en: What do you think about social media?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En mi opinión, tienen ventajas y desventajas.
lines.en: In my opinion, they have advantages and disadvantages.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Por ejemplo?
lines.en: For example?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Por un lado, te ayudan a estar en contacto; por otro, quitan mucho tiempo.
lines.en: On the one hand, they help you stay in touch; on the other, they take up a lot of time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Eso es verdad.
lines.en: That's true.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sin embargo, creo que el problema es el uso, no la herramienta.
lines.en: However, I think the problem is the use, not the tool.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cómo terminarías el argumento?
lines.en: And how would you end the argument?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En resumen, todo depende de cómo las uses.
lines.en: In short, it all depends on how you use them.

days.title: Que: especificativa y explicativa
days.objective: Distinguish restrictive from non-restrictive relative clauses with que, and use the comma correctly, since it changes the meaning.
days.paretoFocus: The same sentence with and without commas means two different things, and this trips learners up in both reading and writing.
drills: Write one restrictive and one non-restrictive sentence about your family.
Read both sentences aloud, pausing at the commas.
Explain how the comma changes meaning.

items: Recall a condition connector from an earlier lesson.
Say one sentence with a comparative clause.
Explain the difference between a restrictive and a non-restrictive clause.

activities.title: La coma que cambia el sentido
activities.intro: A restrictive relative clause has no commas and identifies which part of a group you mean. A non-restrictive relative clause has commas and just adds extra information about something already identified.

items.hr: Los estudiantes que aprobaron el examen están contentos.
items.en: The students who passed the exam are happy.
items.note: restrictive, no commas, only those who passed

items.hr: Los estudiantes, que aprobaron el examen, están contentos.
items.en: The students, who passed the exam, are happy.
items.note: non-restrictive, commas, adds extra info about all of them

items.hr: Mi hermano, que vive en Sevilla, viene a verme cada verano.
items.en: My brother, who lives in Seville, visits me every summer.
items.note: non-restrictive, since there is only one brother in question

items.hr: El libro que me prestaste es buenísimo.
items.en: The book you lent me is really good.
items.note: restrictive, specifies which book

items.hr: En la escritura formal, las comas de la cláusula no restrictiva son obligatorias.
items.en: In formal writing, the commas of the non-restrictive clause are compulsory.
items.note: the rule stated directly

activities.title: Especificativa o explicativa
activities.intro: Decide whether a clause identifies a subgroup or just adds information.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué opción es una cláusula restrictiva (identifica a un subgrupo)?
options: Los alumnos que suspendieron repetirán el examen.
Los alumnos, que suspendieron, repetirán el examen.
Los alumnos, que son inteligentes, repetirán el examen.
Mis alumnos, que son diez, repetirán el examen.
questions.answer: Los alumnos que suspendieron repetirán el examen.
questions.explanation: No commas means the clause identifies a subset, only those who failed.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la versión correcta si tienes un único coche?
options: Mi coche, que es rojo, es rápido.
Mi coche que es rojo es rápido.
Mi coche, que rojo es, es rápido.
Mi coche que, es rojo, es rápido.
questions.answer: Mi coche, que es rojo, es rápido.
questions.explanation: A single referent needs the non-restrictive comma pair.

questions.prompt: El piso ___ vimos ayer ya se ha alquilado.
questions.explanation: que introduces the restrictive clause with no commas needed.

questions.prompt: Te presto el libro con tal de que me lo ___ (devolver) la semana que viene.
questions.explanation: con tal de que still requires the present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The book you lent me is really good.'
questions.explanation: que introduces a restrictive clause identifying which book.

activities.title: Hablando de compañeros
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Describe colleagues using both restrictive and non-restrictive clauses.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Quién es esa chica?
lines.en: Who is that girl?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es la compañera que trabaja conmigo en el proyecto.
lines.en: She's the colleague who works with me on the project.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ah, ¿tu compañera Marta, que vive cerca de aquí?
lines.en: Ah, your colleague Marta, who lives near here?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Esa misma. Es la única persona que entiende el problema.
lines.en: That's the one. She's the only person who understands the problem.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Qué suerte tenerla en el equipo.
lines.en: How lucky to have her on the team.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, y el jefe, que confía mucho en ella, le ha dado más responsabilidad.
lines.en: Yes, and the boss, who trusts her a lot, has given her more responsibility.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Se lo merece.
lines.en: She deserves it.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Totalmente, es la persona que más ha trabajado este año.
lines.en: Totally, she's the person who has worked the most this year.

days.title: Quien, el que, la que
days.objective: Use quien after a preposition with a human antecedent, and el que / la que / los que / las que as alternatives to que, agreeing in gender and number.
days.paretoFocus: After a preposition, Spanish requires quien or el que, never a bare que, which is a frequent transfer error from English.
drills: Write two sentences with a preposition plus quien.
Rewrite them using el que or la que instead.
Say one sentence about a friend using con quien.

items: Recall the de lo que rule from an earlier lesson.
Say one restrictive relative clause.
Explain when que alone is not enough after a preposition.

activities.title: Quien y el que
activities.intro: English happily says 'the woman I spoke to' with no relative pronoun stuck to the preposition, but Spanish never drops it: a preposition always needs a form of quien, or a matching el que, right there beside it. Without a preposition, bare quien survives only in fixed sayings and general statements about whoever.

items.hr: La mujer con quien hablé ayer es la nueva directora.
items.en: The woman I spoke with yesterday is the new director.
items.note: after a preposition with a human antecedent, use quien

items.hr: El chico de quien te hablé llega mañana.
items.en: The guy I told you about arrives tomorrow.
items.note: de quien, not de que

items.hr: Los compañeros con los que trabajo son muy simpáticos.
items.en: The colleagues I work with are very nice.
items.note: los que works after a preposition too, agreeing in number and gender

items.hr: Esta es la profesora de la que todos hablan.
items.en: This is the teacher everyone talks about.
items.note: la que agrees with profesora

items.hr: Quien mucho abarca, poco aprieta.
items.en: He who grasps too much, holds little.
items.note: quien can also mean whoever, starting a sentence in fixed sayings

activities.title: Después de una preposición
activities.intro: Choose the correct relative after a preposition.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'El amigo ___ te hablé se llama Pablo.'
questions.explanation: A preposition plus a human antecedent needs de quien.

questions.prompt: 'Las chicas ___ estudio son de Bilbao.'
questions.explanation: con las que agrees with chicas, feminine plural.

questions.prompt: El vecino ___ hablé ayer se muda la semana que viene.
questions.explanation: con quien follows the preposition con with a human antecedent.

questions.prompt: Este barrio es más caro de lo ___ pensaba.
questions.explanation: de lo que is required before a clause, not de lo alone.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The colleagues I work with are very nice.'
questions.explanation: con los que agrees with compañeros after the preposition con.

activities.title: ¿Quién es esa persona?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about people through several relationships, using quien and el que after prepositions.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Conoces a la persona de quien te hablé?
lines.en: Do you know the person I told you about?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, es el chico con quien fui a la universidad.
lines.en: Yes, he's the guy I went to university with.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué casualidad! ¿Y los amigos con los que sale ahora?
lines.en: What a coincidence! And the friends he hangs out with now?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Son compañeros con los que trabaja en el hospital.
lines.en: They're colleagues he works with at the hospital.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y la mujer de la que hablaba antes?
lines.en: And the woman he was talking about earlier?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Esa es su hermana, con quien vive.
lines.en: That's his sister, who he lives with.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ahora lo entiendo todo.
lines.en: Now I understand everything.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, quien mucho pregunta, mucho aprende.
lines.en: Yes, whoever asks a lot, learns a lot.

days.title: Donde, cuando, como
days.objective: Use donde, cuando and como as relative adverbs referring to place, time and manner, as alternatives to en que / en el que.
days.paretoFocus: These keep descriptions of places, moments and ways of doing things natural, instead of forcing an awkward preposition plus que.
drills: Turn three en que sentences into natural ones using the matching relative adverb.
Describe a place from your childhood using donde.
Say a sentence about the day you met a friend using cuando.

items: Recall the hypothetical use of aunque.
Say one sentence using quien after a preposition.
Explain the difference between cuando as a relative and cuando as a plain conjunction.

activities.title: Donde, cuando, como
activities.intro: Instead of forcing en que or en el que onto every place, moment or way of doing something, Spanish often swaps in a single adverb that already carries the meaning, much like English collapses 'the place in which' down to simply 'where.'

items.hr: El pueblo donde nací ya no existe.
items.en: The village where I was born no longer exists.
items.note: donde = en que / en el que

items.hr: Fue en 2010, cuando empecé la universidad.
items.en: It was in 2010, when I started university.
items.note: cuando = en que, referring to time

items.hr: No me gusta el modo como me lo dijo.
items.en: I don't like the way he told me.
items.note: como = manner, often interchangeable with en que

items.hr: El bar donde quedamos siempre está lleno.
items.en: The bar where we always meet is always full.
items.note: donde replaces en el que naturally with places

items.hr: Recuerdo el día en que nos conocimos.
items.en: I remember the day we met.
items.note: with an explicit noun like día, en que is the standard form; everyday speech usually shortens it to just el día que

activities.title: Relativos de lugar, tiempo y modo
activities.intro: Choose the relative adverb that fits.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Esta es la casa ___ crecí.'
questions.explanation: donde refers to the place.

questions.prompt: 'No entiendo el modo ___ funciona esto.'
questions.explanation: como refers to the manner.

questions.prompt: Fue en verano ___ nos conocimos.
questions.explanation: cuando refers back to the time, verano.

questions.prompt: Aunque ___ (llover), saldremos igual.
questions.explanation: aunque plus subjunctive marks a hypothetical concession.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The village where I was born no longer exists.'
questions.explanation: donde introduces the relative clause of place.

activities.title: Cómo nos conocimos
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Tell the story of how you met your partner, using donde, cuando and como.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Dónde os conocisteis tú y tu pareja?
lines.en: Where did you and your partner meet?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En el bar donde trabajaba yo entonces.
lines.en: At the bar where I used to work then.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué romántico! ¿Y cuándo empezasteis a salir?
lines.en: How romantic! And when did you start dating?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Fue en enero, cuando hacía muchísimo frío.
lines.en: It was in January, when it was really cold.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cómo se lo pediste?
lines.en: And how did you ask him or her out?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No me gusta el modo como se lo pedí, fue muy torpe.
lines.en: I don't like the way I asked, it was very clumsy.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Seguro que no fue tan malo.
lines.en: I'm sure it wasn't that bad.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bueno, el resultado es lo que importa.
lines.en: Well, the result is what matters.

days.title: Cuyo
days.objective: Use cuyo, cuya, cuyos and cuyas to express possession inside a relative clause, agreeing with the thing possessed, not with the owner.
days.paretoFocus: Learners systematically make cuyo agree with the owner by analogy with English whose; this is the one point in the whole relative system that reliably gets reversed.
drills: Write three sentences about different people's houses, cars and jobs, letting the possessive form change each time.
Swap the owner's gender in one sentence and check whether the possessive form actually needs to move.
Say one sentence about a person whose job you find interesting.

items: Recall a discourse connector for contrast.
Say one sentence with donde as a relative.
Explain why cuyo agrees with the possessed noun and not with the owner.

activities.title: Cuyo
activities.intro: cuyo works like an adjective placed right before the possessed noun, and it agrees with that noun in gender and number, never with the owner. This is the reverse of English whose, which never changes form.

items.hr: Es un escritor cuyos libros son famosos en todo el mundo.
items.en: He's a writer whose books are famous all over the world.
items.note: cuyos agrees with libros, masculine plural, not with escritor

items.hr: Vive en una casa cuya puerta es azul.
items.en: She lives in a house whose door is blue.
items.note: cuya agrees with puerta, feminine singular, not with casa

items.hr: Conozco a una mujer cuyo hijo estudia medicina.
items.en: I know a woman whose son studies medicine.
items.note: cuyo agrees with hijo, masculine singular, even though the owner is female

items.hr: Es una empresa cuyas oficinas están en varias ciudades.
items.en: It's a company whose offices are in several cities.
items.note: cuyas agrees with oficinas, feminine plural

items.hr: El vecino, cuyo perro ladra toda la noche, no se disculpa nunca.
items.en: The neighbour, whose dog barks all night, never apologises.
items.note: cuyo comes right before the possessed noun

activities.title: La concordancia de cuyo
activities.intro: Choose the form of cuyo that agrees with the possessed noun.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Es una actriz ___ películas ganaron varios premios.'
