questions.explanation: cuyas agrees with películas, feminine plural, not with the actress.

questions.prompt: 'Tengo un amigo ___ madre es médica.'
questions.explanation: cuya agrees with madre, feminine singular, regardless of the friend's gender.

questions.prompt: Es un pueblo ___ nombre no recuerdo.
questions.explanation: cuyo agrees with nombre, masculine singular.

questions.prompt: El piso es barato; ___, está lejos del centro.
questions.explanation: sin embargo marks the contrast between price and location.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'He's a writer whose books are famous.'
questions.explanation: cuyos agrees with libros, the thing possessed.

activities.title: En la presentación del libro
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Introduce people at a book event using cuyo and its agreeing forms.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Conoces a esa autora?
lines.en: Do you know that author?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, es la escritora cuyos libros están en todas las librerías.
lines.en: Yes, she's the writer whose books are in every bookshop.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y el hombre que está con ella?
lines.en: And the man who's with her?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es su editor, cuya empresa publica también revistas.
lines.en: He's her editor, whose company also publishes magazines.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Interesante. ¿Y esa mujer de allí?
lines.en: Interesting. And that woman over there?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es una crítica cuyas opiniones respeto mucho.
lines.en: She's a critic whose opinions I respect a lot.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Deberías presentarte.
lines.en: You should introduce yourself.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Buena idea, es una oportunidad cuyo valor no quiero perder.
lines.en: Good idea, it's an opportunity whose value I don't want to lose.

days.title: Relativas con subjuntivo
days.objective: Choose indicative or subjunctive inside a relative clause depending on whether the antecedent is known to exist or not, contrasting tengo un piso que tiene terraza with busco un piso que tenga terraza.
days.paretoFocus: This is the clearest demonstration in the language of what the subjunctive marks, an antecedent whose existence is not asserted, and it ties together everything the course has taught about the mood.
drills: Write one pair of sentences: tengo un/a... que with the indicative, and busco un/a... que with the subjunctive.
Say a sentence starting with No conozco a nadie que.
Ask a question starting with ¿Conoces a alguien que...?

items: Recall the aunque hypothetical concession.
Say one sentence with cuyo.
Explain why a negated antecedent always triggers the subjunctive.

activities.title: El antecedente que quizá no existe
activities.intro: Inside a relative clause, the indicative describes a specific, known antecedent, while the subjunctive describes one that may not exist yet, has not been found, or is completely negated. The same sentence pattern with que switches meaning depending only on the mood.

items.hr: Tengo un piso que tiene terraza.
items.en: I have a flat that has a terrace.
items.note: the flat exists and is specific, so the indicative

items.hr: Busco un piso que tenga terraza.
items.en: I'm looking for a flat that has a terrace.
items.note: no specific flat is guaranteed to exist yet, so the subjunctive

items.hr: Conozco a alguien que habla japonés.
items.en: I know someone who speaks Japanese.
items.note: a real, specific person, indicative

items.hr: ¿Conoces a alguien que hable japonés?
items.en: Do you know anyone who speaks Japanese?
items.note: the person may or may not exist, subjunctive

items.hr: No hay nadie aquí que sepa la respuesta.
items.en: There's nobody here who knows the answer.
items.note: a negated antecedent never exists, so the subjunctive is automatic

activities.title: Busco un piso que...
activities.intro: For each gap, test whether the flat, person or thing before que is a specific one already in hand, then pick the mood that matches.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Necesito un empleado que ___ hablar inglés.' (aún no lo he encontrado)
questions.explanation: The ideal employee is not yet a specific known person, so the subjunctive applies.

questions.prompt: 'Tengo un compañero que ___ hablar inglés perfectamente.' (existe, lo conozco)
questions.explanation: A real, known person takes the indicative.

questions.prompt: No conozco a nadie que ___ (querer) hacer ese trabajo.
questions.explanation: A negated antecedent always takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Aunque el piso ___ (ser) barato, no lo alquilaré si no tiene ascensor.
questions.explanation: aunque plus subjunctive treats the fact as not decisive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I'm looking for a flat that has a terrace.'
questions.explanation: tenga is subjunctive because no specific flat has been found yet.

activities.title: Buscando piso
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Look for a flat, contrasting what you have with what you are looking for.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tipo de piso buscas?
lines.en: What kind of flat are you looking for?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Busco un piso que tenga dos habitaciones y esté cerca del centro.
lines.en: I'm looking for a flat that has two bedrooms and is near the centre.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo tengo un piso que tiene tres habitaciones, pero está lejos.
lines.en: I have a flat that has three bedrooms, but it's far away.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¿Conoces a alguien que alquile pisos por esa zona?
lines.en: Do you know anyone who rents flats in that area?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sí, conozco a un agente que trabaja allí.
lines.en: Yes, I know an agent who works there.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfecto. Necesito algo que no sea muy caro.
lines.en: Perfect. I need something that isn't very expensive.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Le pregunto si tiene algo que encaje contigo.
lines.en: I'll ask him if he has something that fits you.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Gracias, avísame en cuanto sepas algo.
lines.en: Thanks, let me know as soon as you know something.

days.title: Lo que y lo cual
days.objective: Use lo que and lo cual to refer back to an entire previous idea rather than to a specific noun.
days.paretoFocus: This neuter relative is what lets a speaker comment on a whole situation, essential for opinions and narration.
drills: Write two sentences that comment on a whole previous idea using lo que.
Rewrite one of them with lo cual.
Say a sentence starting with Lo que más me gusta es...

items: Recall a restrictive relative clause with que.
Say one sentence with the relative subjunctive.
Explain the difference between lo que and que.

activities.title: Lo que y lo cual
activities.intro: English 'which' can sometimes point back at an entire clause rather than the noun right before it; Spanish needs a special neuter word for that job, since que on its own always points at a noun. lo que doubles as a sentence-opener meaning what, and does the same work inside an indirect question.

items.hr: Llegó tarde, lo que me molestó bastante.
items.en: He arrived late, which annoyed me quite a lot.
items.note: lo que refers to the whole fact of arriving late, not to a noun

items.hr: No me avisaron, lo cual fue un problema.
items.en: They didn't warn me, which was a problem.
items.note: lo cual works the same way, slightly more formal

items.hr: Lo que más me gusta de este trabajo es el horario.
items.en: What I like most about this job is the schedule.
items.note: lo que can also start a sentence, meaning what

items.hr: No entiendo lo que dices.
items.en: I don't understand what you're saying.
items.note: lo que means what in an indirect question

items.hr: Aprobó el examen, lo que demuestra que estudió mucho.
items.en: He passed the exam, which shows he studied a lot.
items.note: lo que introducing a comment on the whole clause

activities.title: Comentar una idea entera
activities.intro: Choose the neuter relative that refers to a whole idea.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Perdió las llaves, ___ le costó mucho dinero.'
questions.explanation: lo que refers to the whole fact of losing the keys, not to a specific noun.

questions.prompt: '___ más me gusta de ella es su sinceridad.'
questions.explanation: Lo que opens the sentence meaning what.

questions.prompt: No me llamó, ___ me pareció una falta de respeto.
questions.explanation: lo que comments on the whole previous clause.

questions.prompt: Los libros ___ me prestaste ya te los devolví.
questions.explanation: A plain restrictive relative clause just needs que.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I don't understand what you're saying.'
questions.explanation: lo que means what in this indirect question.

activities.title: Noticias de un amigo
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend quit his job out of nowhere; react to the gossip and tack your own comment onto each new fact as it comes.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Sabes que Marcos dejó el trabajo?
lines.en: Do you know Marcos quit his job?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No lo sabía. ¿Qué fue lo que pasó?
lines.en: I didn't know. What was it that happened?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Discutió con el jefe, lo cual era cuestión de tiempo.
lines.en: He argued with the boss, which was a matter of time.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo que no entiendo es por qué aguantó tanto.
lines.en: What I don't understand is why he put up with it for so long.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Necesitaba el dinero, lo que es comprensible.
lines.en: He needed the money, which is understandable.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro. ¿Y ahora qué va a hacer?
lines.en: Sure. And now what is he going to do?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ni idea.
lines.en: No idea.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo que sí sé es que está buscando algo nuevo.
lines.en: What I do know is that he's looking for something new.

days.title: El se impersonal
days.objective: Use impersonal se with a verb in the third person singular to talk about people in general, without a specific subject.
days.paretoFocus: This is the natural Spanish way to say you, one or people generically, and it appears constantly in signs, recipes and general statements.
drills: Write three impersonal se sentences about a city you know.
Ask a question using ¿Cómo se dice...?
Say one sentence with no se puede.

items: Recall a sentence using con quien.
Say one sentence with lo que referring to a whole idea.
Explain when se is impersonal rather than reflexive.

activities.title: El se impersonal
activities.intro: Spanish often skips naming a subject altogether when talking about people in general, much as English leans on 'you' or 'one': se attaches to a third-person-singular verb and the whole sentence reads as a general truth about nobody in particular.

items.hr: Aquí se come muy bien.
items.en: You eat very well here.
items.note: impersonal se plus verb in the singular, no specific subject

items.hr: Se vive tranquilo en este pueblo.
items.en: Life is peaceful in this village.
items.note: with an intransitive verb, always singular

items.hr: No se puede fumar dentro del edificio.
items.en: You can't smoke inside the building.
items.note: se plus puede plus infinitive, a very common impersonal pattern

items.hr: Se trabaja mucho en esta empresa.
items.en: People work a lot at this company.
items.note: se plus verb, a generic statement about how things are

items.hr: ¿Cómo se dice esto en español?
items.en: How do you say this in Spanish?
items.note: the impersonal se in a very common everyday question

activities.title: Practica el se impersonal
activities.intro: Complete each generic statement with se.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? '___ duerme bien en esta casa, hay mucho silencio.'
questions.explanation: Se plus the verb in the singular states a generic fact.

questions.prompt: 'No ___ puede aparcar aquí.'
questions.explanation: se puede plus infinitive is the everyday impersonal pattern.

questions.prompt: Aquí ___ vive muy tranquilo.
questions.explanation: se marks the impersonal, generic subject.

questions.prompt: La chica ___ hablé es profesora.
questions.explanation: con quien follows a preposition with a human antecedent.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'You can't smoke inside the building.'
questions.explanation: se puede plus infinitive expresses a general prohibition.

activities.title: Vivir en el barrio
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Describe what life is like in your neighbourhood using the impersonal se.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tal se vive en este barrio?
lines.en: What's it like living in this neighbourhood?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Se vive muy bien, es tranquilo y céntrico.
lines.en: It's very good, it's quiet and central.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Se puede aparcar fácilmente?
lines.en: Can you park easily?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No mucho, se necesita paciencia los fines de semana.
lines.en: Not much, you need patience on weekends.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y se come bien por aquí?
lines.en: And is the food good around here?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Se come genial, hay muchos bares con buena comida.
lines.en: The food is great, there are lots of bars with good food.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Me lo estás vendiendo bien.
lines.en: You're selling it well to me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es que se vive de verdad tranquilo aquí.
lines.en: It's just that life here is really peaceful.

days.title: El se pasivo
days.objective: Use passive se with the verb agreeing in number with the noun that follows it, contrasting the singular and plural forms as the diagnostic between impersonal and passive se.
days.paretoFocus: Se vende piso and se venden pisos look nearly identical, yet the agreement carries the entire distinction, and it is a structural error that survives long into B1 uncorrected.
drills: Write one singular and one plural passive se sentence about the same shop.
Say both aloud and notice the verb change.
Write a sign for something you would sell or rent.

items: Recall a relative adverb sentence with donde.
Say one impersonal se sentence.
Explain the agreement rule that distinguishes impersonal from passive se.

activities.title: El se pasivo
activities.intro: The look-alike se from the last lesson hides a second pattern: here the noun that follows is the real grammatical subject, so flip that noun to plural and the verb has to flip right along with it, exactly the test that tells the two constructions apart.

items.hr: Se vende piso.
items.en: Flat for sale.
items.note: singular noun, singular verb

items.hr: Se venden pisos.
items.en: Flats for sale.
items.note: plural noun, so the verb must agree and become plural too

items.hr: Se habla español.
items.en: Spanish is spoken.
items.note: español is singular, so the verb stays singular

items.hr: Se alquilan habitaciones.
items.en: Rooms for rent.
items.note: habitaciones is plural, the verb agrees

items.hr: Se necesita camarero. Se necesitan camareros.
items.en: Waiter needed. Waiters needed.
items.note: the exact same pattern, singular versus plural, side by side

activities.title: Singular o plural
activities.intro: Choose the form of the verb that agrees with the noun.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta para un cartel que anuncia varios pisos?
questions.explanation: pisos is plural, so the verb must be plural too.

questions.prompt: 'En esta tienda ___ periódicos en varios idiomas.'
questions.explanation: periódicos is plural, so the verb agrees in the plural.

questions.prompt: Se ___ (necesitar) camareros para el fin de semana.
questions.explanation: camareros is plural, so the verb takes the plural form.

questions.prompt: Ese es el bar ___ nos conocimos.
questions.explanation: donde refers back to the place, the bar.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Rooms for rent.'
questions.explanation: habitaciones is plural, so alquilan agrees with it.

activities.title: Carteles en la calle
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about signs around the neighbourhood, noticing singular versus plural.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has visto el cartel de la puerta?
lines.en: Have you seen the sign on the door?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, dice: se alquila habitación.
lines.en: Yes, it says: room for rent.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ah, pensaba que se alquilaban dos.
lines.en: Oh, I thought two were for rent.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, solo una, y también se vende el piso de arriba.
lines.en: No, just one, and the flat upstairs is also for sale.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Se venden más pisos en el edificio?
lines.en: Are more flats for sale in the building?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, se venden tres en total.
lines.en: Yes, three in total.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y en la tienda de la esquina?
lines.en: And at the corner shop?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ahí se necesita un dependiente, vi el cartel ayer.
lines.en: There they need a shop assistant, I saw the sign yesterday.

days.title: Otros impersonales
days.objective: Use the other common ways to speak generically in Spanish: dicen que, se dice que, uno, la gente and the generic tú, choosing among them naturally.
days.paretoFocus: Real spoken Spanish mixes these constantly; relying only on se sounds textbook-stiff.
drills: Write one sentence each with dicen que, uno and la gente.
Say a generalisation using the generic tú.
Rewrite a se dice que sentence using dicen que.

items: Recall a cuyo sentence about a place.
Say one passive se sentence.
Explain why la gente takes a singular verb.

activities.title: Otras formas impersonales
activities.intro: Besides se, Spanish generalises with dicen que and se dice que (both meaning it is said), uno as a generic subject, la gente (which always takes a singular verb, even though it means people), and the generic tú, common in spoken advice.

items.hr: Dicen que va a llover este fin de semana.
items.en: They say it's going to rain this weekend.
items.note: dicen que, third person plural, no specific subject

items.hr: Se dice que el nuevo restaurante es excelente.
items.en: It's said that the new restaurant is excellent.
items.note: se dice que, same meaning as dicen que, slightly more formal

items.hr: Uno nunca sabe lo que va a pasar.
items.en: One never knows what's going to happen.
items.note: uno as a generic subject, common in reflection and opinion

items.hr: La gente aquí es muy amable.
items.en: People here are very kind.
items.note: la gente takes a singular verb even though it means people

items.hr: Cuando eres joven, no valoras el tiempo libre.
items.en: When you're young, you don't value free time.
items.note: the generic tú, very common in spoken advice and generalisations

activities.title: Dicen que, uno, la gente
activities.intro: Choose the right generic form for each sentence.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? '___ que el jefe se va de la empresa.'
questions.explanation: Dicen que is the fixed generic expression, third person plural.

questions.prompt: 'La gente aquí ___ muy trabajadora.'
questions.explanation: la gente is grammatically singular.

questions.prompt: ___ nunca sabe qué va a pasar mañana.
questions.explanation: Uno works as a generic, impersonal subject.

questions.prompt: Conozco a un chico ___ hermana trabaja en el mismo edificio que yo.
questions.explanation: cuya agrees with hermana, feminine singular, not with the owner.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'They say it's going to rain this weekend.'
questions.explanation: Dicen que introduces a generic, unattributed statement.

activities.title: Rumores en la ciudad
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about rising prices, mixing the different generic forms.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Dicen que van a subir el precio del billete de autobús.
lines.en: They say they're going to raise the bus ticket price.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, se dice que será el mes que viene.
lines.en: Yes, it's said it will be next month.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Uno ya no sabe en qué gastar el dinero.
lines.en: One no longer knows what to spend money on.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: La gente se está quejando mucho en las redes.
lines.en: People are complaining a lot online.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Cuando vives en una ciudad grande, todo sube.
lines.en: When you live in a big city, everything goes up.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es verdad, uno se acostumbra, pero cuesta.
lines.en: It's true, you get used to it, but it's hard.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y qué se puede hacer?
lines.en: And what can be done?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Poco, la gente solo puede quejarse y esperar.
lines.en: Not much, people can only complain and wait.

days.title: Describir y definir
days.objective: Combine relative clauses and se constructions to describe people, places and things fluently, in one integrated review.
days.paretoFocus: Real descriptions constantly mix relatives, cuyo, lo que and se, and this lesson is the rehearsal for doing that without hesitating.
drills: Describe your neighbourhood using at least one relative and one se construction.
Say a full description of an ideal flatmate using the relative subjunctive.
Rewrite one of your sentences adding cuyo.

items: Recall the relative clause with the subjunctive.
Say one discourse connector sentence.
List three relative words and explain what each refers to.

activities.title: Describir con todo lo aprendido
activities.intro: Real descriptions mix several tools at once: relatives, cuyo, lo que and the se constructions. This lesson combines them in natural sentences instead of practising each one alone.

items.hr: Es un barrio donde se vive tranquilo y cuyas calles siempre están limpias.
items.en: It's a neighbourhood where life is peaceful and whose streets are always clean.
items.note: combining donde, cuyo and impersonal se

items.hr: Busco un compañero de piso que sea ordenado y con quien pueda compartir gastos.
items.en: I'm looking for a flatmate who is tidy and with whom I can share expenses.
items.note: relative subjunctive plus con quien

items.hr: Se necesita alguien que hable dos idiomas, algo que no es fácil de encontrar.
items.en: Someone who speaks two languages is needed, something that isn't easy to find.
items.note: se necesita, relative subjunctive and lo que together

items.hr: Es la tienda donde se venden los mejores dulces de la ciudad.
items.en: It's the shop where the best sweets in the city are sold.
items.note: donde plus passive se

items.hr: La persona cuya opinión más respeto es mi abuela, que siempre dice lo que piensa.
items.en: The person whose opinion I respect most is my grandmother, who always says what she thinks.
items.note: cuya plus a non-restrictive que clause plus lo que

activities.title: Describe y define
activities.intro: Combine relatives and se constructions to complete each description.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Es un pueblo ___ se vive muy bien.'
questions.explanation: donde refers to the place, the village.

questions.prompt: 'Necesito un compañero que ___ responsable.'
questions.explanation: The ideal flatmate is not a specific known person yet, so the subjunctive applies.

questions.prompt: Es la calle ___ se celebra el mercado los domingos.
questions.explanation: donde introduces the relative clause of place.

questions.prompt: Busco un piso que ___ (tener) terraza.
questions.explanation: The relative subjunctive marks an antecedent not yet found.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'It's the shop where the best sweets are sold.'
questions.explanation: donde introduces the place, and se venden agrees with the plural dulces.

activities.title: El barrio ideal
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Describe a new neighbourhood, combining relatives, cuyo and se constructions.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo es el barrio nuevo?
lines.en: What's the new neighbourhood like?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es un sitio donde se vive tranquilo, cuyas calles están siempre limpias.
lines.en: It's a place where life is peaceful, whose streets are always clean.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Suena bien. ¿Y los vecinos?
lines.en: Sounds good. And the neighbours?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Todavía busco un vecino con quien pueda llevarme bien.
lines.en: I'm still looking for a neighbour I can get along with.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Hay tiendas cerca?
lines.en: Are there shops nearby?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, hay una tienda donde se venden productos frescos todos los días.
lines.en: Yes, there's a shop where fresh products are sold every day.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Eso es lo que más me importa a mí.
lines.en: That's what matters most to me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A mí también, es la razón por la que elegí este barrio.
lines.en: Me too, it's the reason I chose this neighbourhood.

days.title: Perífrasis con infinitivo
days.objective: Use the common infinitive periphrases (empezar a, volver a, acabar de, dejar de, ponerse a, llegar a, soler) to express the beginning, repetition, recent completion, cessation, sudden start, achievement and habit of an action.
days.paretoFocus: These seven verbs pack a huge amount of everyday meaning into a two-word pattern, and native speakers use them constantly instead of adverbs.
drills: Write one sentence each with empezar a, dejar de and volver a.
Say a sentence about something you have just done using acabar de.
Describe a personal achievement using llegar a.

items: Recall a sentence using lo que.
Say one sentence with the impersonal se.
Explain the difference between dejar de and acabar de.

activities.title: Perífrasis con infinitivo
activities.intro: A periphrasis of verb plus a plus infinitive, or verb plus de plus infinitive, adds a shade of meaning a single tense cannot: starting, repeating, having just finished, stopping, starting suddenly, or eventually managing to do something.

items.hr: Empecé a estudiar español hace dos años.
items.en: I started studying Spanish two years ago.
items.note: empezar a + infinitive = start

items.hr: Volvió a llover por la tarde.
items.en: It rained again in the afternoon.
items.note: volver a + infinitive = do again

items.hr: Acabo de llegar a casa.
items.en: I've just arrived home.
items.note: acabar de + infinitive = have just done

items.hr: Dejó de fumar el año pasado.
items.en: He gave up smoking last year.
items.note: dejar de + infinitive = stop doing

items.hr: Se puso a llorar sin motivo, y al final llegó a entender el problema.
items.en: She started crying for no reason, and in the end she came to understand the problem.
items.note: ponerse a = start suddenly, llegar a = eventually manage to

items.hr: Suele llover mucho en esta región durante el otoño.
items.en: It usually rains a lot in this region during autumn.
items.note: soler + infinitive = to usually do something, a habit

activities.title: Empezar, dejar, volver a
activities.intro: Choose the periphrasis that fits each meaning.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Después de años de intentarlo, ___ hablar francés con soltura.'
questions.explanation: llegar a expresses eventually achieving something.

questions.prompt: No estaba nevando, pero ___ nevar de repente durante el partido.
questions.explanation: ponerse a expresses a sudden start; since it wasn't snowing before, stopping (dejó de), doing it again (volvió a) or having just finished (acabó de) don't fit.

questions.prompt: ___ (acabar de) terminar el informe, así que ahora puedo descansar.
questions.explanation: acabar de + infinitive means to have just done something.

questions.prompt: Llegó tarde otra vez, ___ me molestó bastante.
questions.explanation: lo que comments on the whole previous idea.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'He gave up smoking last year.'
questions.explanation: dejar de + infinitive means to stop doing something.

activities.title: Dejar un hábito
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about quitting smoking, using several infinitive periphrases.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Fumas todavía?
lines.en: Do you still smoke?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, dejé de fumar hace seis meses.
lines.en: No, I quit smoking six months ago.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué bien! ¿Y cómo lo conseguiste?
lines.en: Great! And how did you manage it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Al principio fue difícil, pero llegué a acostumbrarme.
lines.en: At first it was hard, but I eventually got used to it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿No has vuelto a fumar nunca?
lines.en: Have you never smoked again?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Una vez volví a probarlo, pero no me gustó nada.
lines.en: Once I tried it again, but I didn't like it at all.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cuándo empezaste a fumar?
lines.en: And when did you start smoking?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Empecé a fumar con dieciocho años, un gran error.
lines.en: I started smoking at eighteen, a big mistake.

days.title: Perífrasis con gerundio
days.objective: Use gerund periphrases (seguir, llevar, ir, andar plus gerundio) to express continuation, duration, gradual progress and a somewhat critical ongoing action.
days.paretoFocus: These give shades of still doing, for X time doing and gradually doing that a single verb tense cannot express as naturally.
drills: Write one sentence with llevar plus time plus gerundio about yourself.
Say a sentence with seguir plus gerundio about a habit.
Describe gradual progress using ir plus gerundio.

items: Recall an impersonal se sentence about a city.
Say one sentence with an infinitive periphrasis.
Explain what llevar plus gerundio expresses that the present perfect doesn't.

activities.title: Perífrasis con gerundio
activities.intro: seguir, llevar, ir and andar plus a gerund describe an action in progress from different angles: continuing, lasting a certain time, progressing gradually, or repeating with a critical tone.

items.hr: Sigo estudiando español todos los días.
items.en: I'm still studying Spanish every day.
items.note: seguir + gerundio = continue doing

items.hr: Llevo dos años estudiando español.
items.en: I've been studying Spanish for two years.
items.note: llevar + time + gerundio = duration up to now

items.hr: Poco a poco vamos entendiendo mejor la gramática.
items.en: Bit by bit we're understanding the grammar better.
items.note: ir + gerundio = gradual progress

items.hr: Anda diciendo por ahí que le deben dinero.
items.en: He's going around saying that he's owed money.
items.note: andar + gerundio, often with a critical or gossipy tone

items.hr: Llevamos horas esperando el autobús.
items.en: We've been waiting for the bus for hours.
items.note: llevar + gerundio, very common for complaining about duration

activities.title: Seguir, llevar, ir, andar
activities.intro: Choose the gerund periphrasis that fits each meaning.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Llevo tres horas ___ este ejercicio.'
questions.explanation: llevar + time + gerundio expresses duration up to now.

questions.prompt: 'Anda ___ que va a cambiar de trabajo.'
questions.explanation: andar + gerundio needs the gerund form.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (seguir) trabajando en el mismo sitio desde hace cinco años.
questions.explanation: seguir + gerundio expresses that an action continues.

questions.prompt: Aquí ___ trabaja muchísimo, pero la gente vive tranquila.
questions.explanation: se marks the impersonal, generic subject.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We've been waiting for the bus for hours.'
questions.explanation: llevar + time + gerundio expresses how long the waiting has lasted.

activities.title: Cuánto tiempo llevas...
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about a job and a rumour, using gerund periphrases.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Todavía trabajas en la misma empresa?
lines.en: Are you still working at the same company?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, sigo trabajando allí, llevo cinco años ya.
lines.en: Yes, I'm still working there, I've been there five years now.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y te gusta?
lines.en: And do you like it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Poco a poco voy sintiéndome más cómodo.
lines.en: Bit by bit I'm feeling more comfortable.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: He oído que hay problemas con el nuevo jefe.
lines.en: I've heard there are problems with the new boss.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, la gente anda quejándose bastante últimamente.
lines.en: Yes, people have been complaining quite a lot lately.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Espero que se solucione pronto.
lines.en: I hope it gets sorted out soon.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Yo también, llevamos meses esperando un cambio.
lines.en: Me too, we've been waiting months for a change.

days.title: Perífrasis con participio
days.objective: Use participle periphrases (llevar, tener, dejar plus past participle) to express accumulated results, agreeing the participle with the object.
days.paretoFocus: These express I already have X done more naturally than a full perfect tense when emphasising the accumulated result of repeated or partial actions.
drills: Write one sentence with llevar plus participle, agreeing correctly.
Write one with tener plus participle about your week.
Check the agreement in both sentences.

items: Recall a passive se sentence.
Say one gerund periphrasis sentence.
Explain why the participle agrees with the object here but not after haber.

activities.title: Perífrasis con participio
activities.intro: llevar, tener and dejar plus a past participle describe an accumulated or already-achieved result. Unlike the participle after haber, this participle behaves like an adjective and agrees in gender and number with the object it describes.

items.hr: Llevo escritas tres páginas del informe.
items.en: I've got three pages of the report written so far.
items.note: the participle agrees with páginas, feminine plural

items.hr: Tengo hechos los deberes de toda la semana.
items.en: I've got the whole week's homework done.
items.note: tener + participle, agrees with deberes

items.hr: Dejó preparada la cena antes de salir.
items.en: She left dinner ready before going out.
items.note: dejar + participle, agrees with cena

items.hr: Llevamos leídos cinco capítulos del libro.
items.en: We've read five chapters of the book so far.
items.note: agrees with capítulos, emphasises progress

items.hr: Tiene organizada toda la fiesta.
items.en: She has the whole party organised.
items.note: tener + participle, a result already achieved

activities.title: Llevar, tener, dejar + participio
activities.intro: Complete each sentence with the participle agreeing correctly.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Llevo ___ dos capítulos del libro.'
questions.explanation: The participle agrees with capítulos, masculine plural.

questions.prompt: 'Ya tiene ___ toda la casa para la fiesta.'
questions.explanation: The participle agrees with casa, feminine singular.

questions.prompt: Dejó ___ (preparar) la mesa antes de la llegada de los invitados.
questions.explanation: preparada agrees with mesa, feminine singular.

questions.prompt: En este mercado ___ frutas y verduras frescas cada mañana.
questions.explanation: The passive se agrees in the plural with productos.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I've got the whole week's homework done.'
questions.explanation: hechos agrees with deberes, masculine plural.

activities.title: Todo bajo control
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Report on how much progress has been made on several tasks, using participle periphrases.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo va el informe?
lines.en: How's the report going?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Llevo escritas ya diez páginas.
lines.en: I've got ten pages written so far.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué rápido! ¿Y los deberes de los niños?
lines.en: That's fast! And the kids' homework?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tienen hechos los deberes de toda la semana.
lines.en: They've got the whole week's homework done.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Qué organizados. ¿Y la cena de mañana?
lines.en: How organised. And tomorrow's dinner?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Dejé preparada la cena para mañana.
lines.en: I've left tomorrow's dinner ready.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Se nota que lo tienes todo controlado.
lines.en: It's clear you have everything under control.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bueno, tengo planeada toda la semana, la verdad.
lines.en: Well, I've got the whole week planned, to be honest.

days.title: Ser y estar, otra vez
days.objective: Use the adjectives whose meaning changes depending on ser or estar (listo, aburrido, rico, verde), applying the definition-versus-state distinction the course has used since the start.
days.paretoFocus: These pairs are tested constantly, and a wrong choice changes the meaning of the sentence, not just the register.
drills: Write three pairs of sentences using the same adjective with ser and with estar.
Say each pair aloud and explain the meaning difference.
Describe a food using estar rico and a person using ser rico.

items: Recall how to introduce a general rumour or belief impersonally.
Say one sentence with a participle periphrasis.
Explain why está muerto still uses estar despite being a permanent state.

activities.title: Adjetivos que cambian de sentido
activities.intro: Some adjectives mean one thing with ser and another with estar. The split is definition versus state, not permanent versus temporary; that test would fail on está muerto, a permanent state that still takes estar, as this course has said since the very first ser/estar lesson.

items.hr: Mi hermano es muy listo. La cena ya está lista.
items.en: My brother is very clever. Dinner is ready now.
items.note: ser listo = clever, a defining quality; estar listo = ready, a state

items.hr: Esta película es aburrida. Estoy aburrido, no tengo nada que hacer.
items.en: This film is boring. I'm bored, I have nothing to do.
items.note: ser aburrido defines the thing; estar aburrido describes the person's current state

items.hr: Es un hombre muy rico. Este pastel está riquísimo.
items.en: He's a very wealthy man. This cake is delicious.
items.note: ser rico = wealthy; estar rico = tasty, a quality noticed in the moment

items.hr: Este pimiento es verde, no rojo; el plátano que compré está verde, todavía no se puede comer.
items.en: This pepper is green, not red; the banana I bought is green, it can't be eaten yet.
items.note: ser verde categorises the pepper's colour type; estar verde describes the banana's current, temporary state of ripeness

items.hr: Mi abuelo está muerto desde hace diez años.
items.en: My grandfather has been dead for ten years.
items.note: a permanent fact can still take estar, because the split is definition versus state, not duration

activities.title: Ser o estar
activities.intro: Choose ser or estar depending on whether the sentence defines or describes a state.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Ya ___ lista la cena, podemos sentarnos a comer.'
questions.explanation: estar lista here means ready, a state, not a defining trait.

questions.prompt: 'Mi compañera ___ muy lista, aprende todo enseguida.'
questions.explanation: ser lista means clever, a defining quality.

questions.prompt: Este café ___ (estar) buenísimo, ¿lo has probado?
questions.explanation: estar describes a quality noticed in the moment, here the taste.

questions.prompt: ___ que va a hacer buen tiempo este fin de semana.
questions.explanation: Dicen que is the fixed generic expression.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I'm bored, I have nothing to do.'
questions.explanation: estar aburrido describes the person's current state.

activities.title: Una cena y una hermana lista
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about dinner and a bored relative, contrasting ser and estar with the same adjectives.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tal la cena?
lines.en: How's dinner?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Está riquísima, prueba esto.
lines.en: It's delicious, try this.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Mmm, sí. Oye, ¿tu hermana es tan lista como dicen?
lines.en: Mmm, yes. Hey, is your sister as clever as they say?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Muchísimo, pero ahora mismo está muy aburrida en casa.
lines.en: Very much, but right now she's really bored at home.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Por qué? ¿No tiene planes?
lines.en: Why? Doesn't she have plans?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, y encima el plátano que iba a comer está verde todavía.
lines.en: No, and on top of that the banana she was going to eat is still green.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué mala suerte!
lines.en: What bad luck.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bueno, al menos ya está lista la cena, que la anime un poco.
lines.en: Well, at least dinner is ready now, that should cheer her up a bit.

days.title: Estar + participio
days.objective: Use estar plus past participle to describe the resulting state of an action, agreeing the participle with the subject, and distinguish it from the action itself expressed with a full verb.
days.paretoFocus: This is the everyday way to describe how things are as a consequence of something having happened, without needing a passive sentence.
drills: Write three sentences describing the state of objects around you using estar plus participle.
Check the agreement in each.
Say one sentence contrasting the action and its result.

items: Recall a sentence contrasting ser and estar with the same adjective.
Say one sentence describing a place using a relative.
Explain why está cerrada describes a state, not an action.

activities.title: El resultado de una acción
activities.intro: estar plus a past participle describes the state something is left in as a result of an action, not the action itself. The participle behaves like an adjective here and agrees in gender and number with the subject.

items.hr: La puerta está cerrada.
items.en: The door is closed.
items.note: the result of someone having closed it; the participle agrees with puerta

items.hr: Las ventanas están abiertas.
items.en: The windows are open.
items.note: agrees in the feminine plural with ventanas

items.hr: El trabajo ya está terminado.
items.en: The work is already finished.
items.note: describes the current state, not the action of finishing

items.hr: Los platos están rotos.
items.en: The plates are broken.
items.note: agrees with platos, masculine plural

items.hr: La tienda está cerrada los domingos.
items.en: The shop is closed on Sundays.
items.note: a recurring state, still estar plus participle

activities.title: Estar + participio
activities.intro: Complete each sentence with the participle agreeing correctly.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Las tiendas ___ cerradas los domingos.'
questions.explanation: están agrees in the plural with tiendas.

questions.prompt: 'El informe ya ___ terminado.'
questions.explanation: estar plus participle describes the resulting state.

questions.prompt: La ventana está ___ (romper), hay que arreglarla.
questions.explanation: rota agrees with ventana, feminine singular.

questions.prompt: Vivimos en una calle ___ nunca pasa nada interesante.
questions.explanation: donde refers back to the place, the street.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The plates are broken.'
questions.explanation: rotos agrees with platos, masculine plural.

activities.title: Puertas, ventanas y platos
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Check on the state of a shop, an office and some dishes, using estar plus participle.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Está abierta la tienda de la esquina?
lines.en: Is the corner shop open?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, está cerrada los lunes.
lines.en: No, it's closed on Mondays.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vaya. ¿Ya has acabado el informe?
lines.en: Darn. Have you finished the report yet?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, ya está terminado, lo envié esta mañana.
lines.en: Yes, it's already finished, I sent it this morning.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perfecto. ¿Y las ventanas de la oficina?
lines.en: Perfect. And the office windows?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Están abiertas, hacía mucho calor dentro.
lines.en: They're open, it was very hot inside.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ten cuidado, las persianas están un poco rotas.
lines.en: Be careful, the blinds are a bit broken.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, gracias por avisarme.
lines.en: Okay, thanks for letting me know.

days.title: Por y para: el contraste completo
days.objective: Choose correctly between por and para across all their major values, including the pair that flips meaning depending on which one is used.
days.paretoFocus: Por and para are two of the most frequent words in Spanish and mixing them up changes who benefits from an action, so getting the contrast right is a core mark of fluent, natural speech.
drills: Write three sentences about your week, one with para for a deadline, one with por for a cause, one with por for an exchange.
Say the sentence trabajo para ella and trabajo por ella aloud and explain the difference out loud.
List five more values of por and five of para from memory.

items: Recall a sentence using acabar de plus infinitive.
Say one sentence with para expressing a deadline.
Explain in your own words why trabajo para mi jefa and trabajo por mi jefa mean different things.

activities.title: Por y para
activities.intro: Para points toward a recipient or a deadline; por points to a substitution, an exchange, movement through a place, or an imprecise time of day. Two sentences built from the exact same words except for this one preposition can end up meaning opposite things, which is the fastest way to feel the contrast stick.

items.hr: Trabajo para mi jefa.
items.en: I work for her. (she's my employer)
items.note: she is my employer: para marks purpose or recipient

items.hr: Trabajo por mi jefa.
items.en: I'm covering for her.
items.note: I'm standing in for her: por marks substitution, the exact same sentence with the opposite sense

items.hr: Necesito la respuesta para el lunes.
items.en: I need the answer by Monday.
items.note: para marks the deadline

items.hr: Pagué treinta euros por este libro.
items.en: I paid thirty euros for this book.
items.note: por marks the exchange, what was given for what

items.hr: Caminamos por la playa por la tarde, sin prisa.
items.en: We walked along the beach in the afternoon, without hurrying.
items.note: the first por marks movement through the beach; the second, por la tarde, marks an imprecise time of day

activities.title: Por o para
activities.intro: Practise choosing between por and para in context.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Acabo de terminar el informe ___ el director; se lo entrego mañana.'
questions.explanation: para marks the recipient of the report, the person it is destined for; acabo de terminar reviews the periphrasis acabar de plus infinitive.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Llegamos tarde ___ el tráfico.'
questions.explanation: por introduces the cause: the traffic is the reason.

questions.prompt: Trabajo ___ mi hermana esta semana porque está enferma.
questions.explanation: I'm standing in for her: substitution takes por, not para.

questions.prompt: Este ordenador es ___ mi hermana, se lo regalo mañana.
questions.explanation: para marks the recipient of the gift.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'This gift is for you.'
questions.explanation: para + pronoun marks the recipient.

activities.title: Un favor en la oficina
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A colleague asks you to cover a shift and explain who a report is for, exercising por and para.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Puedes trabajar por mí el sábado? Tengo una boda.
lines.en: Can you work for me on Saturday? I have a wedding.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, trabajo por ti este sábado, no hay problema.
lines.en: Okay, I'll cover for you this Saturday, no problem.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Gracias. Por cierto, ¿ese informe es para el director?
lines.en: Thanks. By the way, is that report for the director?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, es para él, lo necesita para el lunes.
lines.en: Yes, it's for him, he needs it by Monday.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y por qué trabajas hasta tan tarde?
lines.en: And why are you working so late?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Porque quiero terminarlo por la noche, así mañana estoy libre.
lines.en: Because I want to finish it at night, so tomorrow I'm free.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buena idea. ¿Cuánto pagaron por el nuevo proyector?
lines.en: Good idea. How much did they pay for the new projector?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pagaron casi mil euros por él, fue caro.
lines.en: They paid almost a thousand euros for it, it was expensive.

days.title: Verbos que van con preposición
days.objective: Use verbs that require a fixed preposition (soñar con, contar con, acordarse de, fijarse en, insistir en, depender de, tratar de, enamorarse de, quedar en) correctly, as fixed units rather than by translating from English.
days.paretoFocus: These verb-preposition pairings are arbitrary and rarely match English, so getting them wrong is one of the most immediate markers of a non-native speaker; learning them as fixed units fixes that fast.
drills: Write five sentences, one for each verb-preposition pair you find hardest.
Say soñar con, acordarse de and fijarse en aloud with a different object each time.
Translate 'I'm counting on you' and 'I forgot about the meeting' using contar con and acordarse de.

items: Recall a sentence using seguir plus gerund.
Say one sentence with acordarse de.
Recall that depender always takes the preposition de.

activities.title: Verbo + preposición fija
activities.intro: Many Spanish verbs are always followed by a specific preposition that has nothing to do with the English equivalent. Learn each verb together with its preposition, the same way you learn a noun together with its article.

items.hr: Siempre sueño con volver a Sevilla.
items.en: I always dream of going back to Seville.
items.note: soñar con, not soñar de

items.hr: Cuento contigo para el proyecto.
items.en: I'm counting on you for the project.
items.note: contar con someone

items.hr: No me acuerdo de su nombre.
items.en: I don't remember his name.
items.note: acordarse de, never acordarse a

items.hr: Nadie se fijó en el error.
items.en: Nobody noticed the mistake.
items.note: fijarse en = to notice

items.hr: El resultado depende de vosotros.
items.en: The result depends on you all.
items.note: depender de, always de, and vosotros as the ordinary plural you in Spain

activities.title: Verbo + preposición
activities.intro: Choose or supply the preposition each verb requires.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Insisto ___ hablar con el jefe hoy mismo.'
questions.explanation: insistir en, always en.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Se enamoró ___ un compañero de trabajo.'
questions.explanation: enamorarse de, always de.

questions.prompt: Quedamos ___ vernos a las ocho delante del cine.
questions.explanation: quedar en = to agree/arrange to.

questions.prompt: No trates ___ convencerme, ya he decidido.
questions.explanation: tratar de = to try to.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I'm counting on you all for this project.'
questions.explanation: contar con + pronoun.

activities.title: Planes y promesas
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Catch up with a friend about dreams, promises and reminders, exercising verbs with their fixed prepositions.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Sigues soñando con abrir tu propio negocio?
lines.en: Are you still dreaming of opening your own business?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, sueño con ello desde hace años.
lines.en: Yes, I've been dreaming of it for years.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Pues cuenta conmigo si necesitas ayuda.
lines.en: Well, count on me if you need help.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Gracias, siempre me acuerdo de tu oferta.
lines.en: Thanks, I always remember your offer.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y ya te has fijado en algún local?
lines.en: And have you noticed any premises yet?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, todo depende de si me dan el préstamo.
lines.en: Yes, it all depends on whether they give me the loan.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Quedamos en hablarlo con calma este fin de semana?
lines.en: Shall we arrange to talk it over calmly this weekend?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfecto, quedamos en eso el sábado.
lines.en: Perfect, let's arrange that for Saturday.

days.title: Los verbos de cambio
days.objective: Choose the correct Spanish verb of change (ponerse, volverse, hacerse, quedarse, llegar a ser, convertirse en) according to whether the change is sudden, lasting, deliberate, the result of an event, or a transformation.
days.paretoFocus: English collapses all of these into 'to become', so choosing the wrong Spanish verb is grammatical but instantly sounds foreign; a decision rule based on the kind of change fixes it in one pass.
drills: For each of the six verbs, write one sentence with a different kind of change.
Say aloud the difference between se puso nervioso and se volvió agresivo.
Explain out loud when to use quedarse instead of the others.

items: Recall a sentence with a periphrasis using participio, like tener plus participle.
Say one sentence with ponerse describing a sudden emotion.
Explain the difference between hacerse rico and volverse loco.

activities.title: Seis formas de decir become
activities.intro: Spanish splits become by the kind of change, not by a single verb. Use ponerse for a sudden, temporary state; volverse for a lasting, involuntary change; hacerse for something deliberate and gradual, often social or professional; quedarse for the state left behind by an event; llegar a ser for something reached after effort; convertirse en for a full transformation into something else.

items.hr: Se puso rojo cuando lo vio.
items.en: He turned red when he saw him.
items.note: ponerse: sudden, temporary

items.hr: Con los años se volvió muy desconfiado.
items.en: Over the years he became very distrustful.
items.note: volverse: lasting, involuntary

items.hr: Se hizo abogado después de muchos años de esfuerzo.
items.en: He became a lawyer after many years of effort.
items.note: hacerse: deliberate, gradual, achieved by will

items.hr: Se quedó viudo muy joven.
items.en: He was left a widower very young.
items.note: quedarse: the state that results from an event

items.hr: El pueblo se convirtió en una ciudad importante.
items.en: The village turned into an important city.
items.note: convertirse en: a full transformation into something else

activities.title: Los verbos de cambio
activities.intro: Choose the verb of change that matches the kind of change described.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Después de terminar la carrera y trabajar diez años, ___ director del hospital.'
questions.explanation: an outcome reached only after sustained effort takes llegar a ser.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Al oír la noticia, ___ pálida durante un instante, y enseguida recuperó el color.'
questions.explanation: a sudden, temporary reaction that passes quickly takes ponerse, not quedarse, which would name a lasting state left behind.

questions.prompt: Tras el accidente, ___ (quedarse) cojo para siempre.
questions.explanation: quedarse names the lasting state left by an event.

questions.prompt: Con la crisis, mucha gente ___ (volverse) más ahorradora.
questions.explanation: an involuntary, lasting change of character or attitude takes volverse.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The village turned into an important city.'
questions.explanation: convertirse en marks a full transformation into something else.

activities.title: Cambios en la familia
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Catch up on how people around you have changed, exercising the verbs of change.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Sabes que mi primo se hizo médico al final?
lines.en: Did you know my cousin ended up becoming a doctor?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¡Qué bien! ¿Y tu tío, sigue tan tranquilo?
lines.en: That's great! And your uncle, is he still so calm?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No, con la jubilación se volvió bastante gruñón.
lines.en: No, with retirement he's become quite grumpy.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vaya. Yo tengo decidido hacerme autónomo el año que viene.
lines.en: Wow. I've already decided to become self-employed next year.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué valiente! ¿Y si te pones nervioso el primer día?
lines.en: How brave! And what if you get nervous the first day?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Seguro que me pongo nervioso, pero se me pasará.
lines.en: I'm sure I'll get nervous, but it will pass.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Con el tiempo tu negocio se convertirá en algo grande.
lines.en: In time your business will turn into something big.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Eso espero, aunque de momento me quedo sin apenas tiempo libre.
lines.en: I hope so, though for now I'm left with hardly any free time.

days.title: El orden de palabras y el énfasis
days.objective: Reorder Spanish sentences to give emphasis, using fronting, lo + adjective + que, and cleft sentences with lo que ... es.
days.paretoFocus: Spanish moves words around far more freely than English to highlight what matters, and mastering these patterns lets a learner sound expressive rather than flatly literal.
drills: Take three plain statements and rewrite each with fronting for emphasis.
Say one sentence using lo + adjective + que to express surprise.
Build one cleft sentence with lo que ... es.

items: Recall a sentence contrasting ser and estar with the same adjective.
Say one sentence with a verb of change.
Explain what fronting does to a sentence's emphasis.

activities.title: Poner en primer lugar lo importante
activities.intro: Spanish can move the element it wants to highlight to the front of the sentence. Lo plus an adjective plus que expresses surprise at a degree; a cleft sentence with lo que ... es isolates exactly what you mean.

items.hr: Ese libro ya lo he leído.
items.en: That book, I've already read it.
items.note: fronting the object for emphasis, doubled by lo

items.hr: ¡Lo caro que está todo!
items.en: How expensive everything is!
items.note: lo + adjective + que expresses degree

items.hr: No te imaginas lo cansada que estoy.
items.en: You can't imagine how tired I am.
items.note: same pattern inside a subordinate clause

items.hr: Lo que necesito es un poco de tranquilidad.
items.en: What I need is a bit of peace and quiet.
items.note: cleft sentence isolating the object of need

items.hr: Lo que me preocupa es el examen de mañana.
items.en: What worries me is tomorrow's exam.
items.note: cleft sentence isolating the subject: el examen is the grammatical subject of preocupar, unlike the object-isolating example above

activities.title: Énfasis en la frase
activities.intro: Practise fronting and the cleft construction to highlight the right part of the sentence.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'A mi hermana no ___ aguanto cuando se pone así.'
questions.explanation: fronting the direct object requires the doubling pronoun, la for mi hermana; le is only for indirect objects.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Con ___ interesante que es esta película, deberíamos verla otra vez.'
questions.explanation: lo + adjective + que expresses the degree.

questions.prompt: No sabes ___ contenta que estoy con el resultado.
questions.explanation: lo + adjective + que, here inside a subordinate clause.

questions.prompt: ___ que más valoro de mis amigos es la sinceridad.
questions.explanation: the cleft construction opens with lo que.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'What I need is a bit of peace and quiet.'
questions.explanation: cleft sentence: lo que + verb + es + the highlighted element.

activities.title: Quejas y confesiones
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Vent about a busy week and say what really matters to you, using fronting and cleft sentences for emphasis.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tal la semana? Te veo agotada.
lines.en: How was the week? You look exhausted.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No te imaginas lo cansada que estoy, ha sido durísima.
lines.en: You can't imagine how tired I am, it's been really tough.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y el proyecto nuevo? A mí no me convence.
lines.en: And the new project? I'm not convinced by it.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ese proyecto ya lo he terminado, menos mal.
lines.en: That project, I've already finished it, thank goodness.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué envidia! Yo sigo con el mío hasta el viernes.
lines.en: I'm jealous! I'm still working on mine until Friday.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo que necesito ahora es un fin de semana tranquilo.
lines.en: What I need now is a quiet weekend.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Es verdad, tu compañera es muy lista, se adapta genial al nuevo horario.
lines.en: True, your colleague is really sharp, she adapts great to the new schedule.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, lo que más admiro de ella es esa capacidad de organizarse.
lines.en: Yes, what I admire most about her is that ability to organize herself.

days.title: Diminutivos y aumentativos: -ito, -illo, -azo
days.objective: Use diminutive and augmentative suffixes (-ito, -illo, -azo) to add affection, smallness, irony or intensity, and judge when they suit the register of a sentence.
days.paretoFocus: Diminutives are everywhere in everyday spoken Spanish, carrying warmth, softening a request or adding irony, so recognising and using them correctly is essential for sounding natural rather than stiff.
drills: Turn five nouns into their diminutive with -ito or -ita.
Say one sentence where a diminutive softens a request.
Explain when a diminutive would sound out of place, such as in a formal letter.

items: Recall a sentence with a cleft construction using lo que.
Say one diminutive that expresses affection rather than size.
Explain the difference between un momento and un momentito.

activities.title: Diminutivos, aumentativos y matices
activities.intro: The suffix -ito/-ita is the everyday diminutive: it can mean literally smaller, but far more often it adds affection, softens a request, or makes something sound casual. -illo/-illa often adds a touch of irony or unimportance. -azo can be an augmentative of size or force, or, on a noun, name a blow with that thing. All of them are common in speech and rare in formal writing.

items.hr: Espera un momentito, ya voy.
items.en: Wait just a sec, I'm coming.
items.note: momentito softens the request, not really about size

items.hr: Mi abuela vive en un pueblecito de la sierra.
items.en: My grandmother lives in a little village in the mountains.
items.note: pueblecito: small, and affectionate

items.hr: Tiene un problemilla con el coche, nada grave.
items.en: He's got a little issue with the car, nothing serious.
items.note: problemilla plays down the problem, with a touch of irony

items.hr: Se dio un golpazo contra la puerta.
items.en: He gave himself a huge bang against the door.
items.note: golpazo: -azo names a forceful blow

items.hr: Es un cochazo, debe de haberle costado una fortuna.
items.en: It's a huge, flashy car, it must have cost him a fortune.
items.note: -azo as an augmentative of size and impressiveness here

activities.title: Diminutivos y aumentativos
activities.intro: Choose the suffix that fits the tone of each sentence.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál transmite mejor cariño e informalidad? 'Ven aquí, ___.'
questions.explanation: -ito adds warmth and affection here.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la más apropiada en una carta formal de trabajo? 'Adjunto el documento ___.'
questions.explanation: diminutives and augmentatives are out of place in formal register.

questions.prompt: Vive en un pueblo muy pequeño y bonito, un ___ de montaña.
questions.explanation: the -ec- interfix appears before -ito on short nouns like pueblo, giving pueblecito, the everyday Peninsular form.

questions.prompt: Se dio un golpe fortísimo contra la mesa, un auténtico ___.
questions.explanation: -azo names a forceful blow.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Wait just a sec, I'm coming.'
questions.explanation: momentito softens the request.

activities.title: Un favor rápido
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Ask a small favour and downplay a problem, using diminutives and augmentatives naturally.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Tienes un segundito? Necesito un favor.
lines.en: Have you got a sec? I need a favor.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, dime, ¿qué problemilla tienes ahora?
lines.en: Sure, tell me, what little problem do you have now?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Nada grave, la puerta del coche está un poco abollada.
lines.en: Nothing serious, the car door is a bit dented.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¡Vaya golpazo debiste de darte!
lines.en: You must have given the door a huge whack!

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué va! Fue una tontería. ¿Me prestas el coche este finde?
lines.en: No way! It was nothing. Can you lend me your car this weekend?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, pero ten cuidadito con la puerta esta vez.
lines.en: Okay, but you'd better be careful with the door this time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Prometido. Te invito a un cafelito por las molestias.
lines.en: Promised. I'll treat you to a little coffee for the trouble.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Trato hecho, nos vemos luego en el bar de la esquina.
lines.en: Deal, see you later at the corner bar.

days.title: Expresiones fijas de cada día
days.objective: Recognise and use common everyday Spanish idioms in context, without translating them literally from English.
days.paretoFocus: Idioms carry a huge share of everyday spoken meaning, and a learner who understands them stops being surprised by ordinary conversation.
drills: Write one short scene using no tener ni idea.
Say meter la pata aloud with an example of when it happened to you.
Explain what tomar el pelo means without translating it word for word.

items: Recall a sentence using a diminutive to soften a request.
Say one idiom that means to be unaware of something.
Explain the literal words of costar un ojo de la cara and what it actually means.

activities.title: Dichos de cada día
activities.intro: Idioms cannot be translated word for word; each one is learned as a fixed block with its real meaning. These are genuine, everyday expressions you will hear constantly in ordinary conversation, not curiosities.

items.hr: No tengo ni idea de dónde ha puesto las llaves.
items.en: I have no idea where he's put the keys.
items.note: no tener ni idea = to have no clue at all

items.hr: Metí la pata delante de todos en la reunión.
items.en: I put my foot in it in front of everyone at the meeting.
items.note: meter la pata = to make an embarrassing mistake

items.hr: Deja de tomarme el pelo, sé que no es verdad.
items.en: Stop pulling my leg, I know it's not true.
items.note: tomar el pelo a alguien = to tease/kid someone

items.hr: Ese piso en el centro cuesta un ojo de la cara.
items.en: That flat in the center costs an arm and a leg.
items.note: costar un ojo de la cara = to be very expensive

items.hr: Al final todo salió a pedir de boca.
items.en: In the end everything turned out perfectly.
items.note: salir a pedir de boca = to go exactly as hoped

activities.title: Expresiones idiomáticas
activities.intro: Complete or choose the idiom that fits each situation.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'meter la pata'?
questions.explanation: meter la pata means to make an embarrassing mistake.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál completa la frase? 'No sé nada del tema, no tengo ni ___.'
questions.explanation: no tener ni idea = to have no clue.

questions.prompt: Ese viaje nos costó un ___ de la cara.
questions.explanation: costar un ojo de la cara = to be very expensive.

questions.prompt: Deja de tomarme el ___, cuéntame la verdad.
questions.explanation: tomar el pelo a alguien = to tease someone.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I have no idea where he's put the keys.'
questions.explanation: no tener ni idea = to have no clue at all; ha puesto reviews the pretérito perfecto.

activities.title: Una reunión que salió mal
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Tell a friend about an awkward meeting, using idioms naturally.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tal la reunión de ayer? Te veo raro.
lines.en: How was yesterday's meeting? You seem off.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Fatal, metí la pata delante de todo el equipo.
lines.en: Terrible, I put my foot in it in front of the whole team.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vaya. ¿Y qué dijo el jefe?
lines.en: Wow. And what did the boss say?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No tengo ni idea, se quedó callado y ya está.
lines.en: No idea, he just went quiet and that was it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No te preocupes, seguro que no fue para tanto.
lines.en: Don't worry, it probably wasn't that big a deal.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Eso espero, porque luego alguien empezó a tomarme el pelo.
lines.en: I hope so, because afterwards someone started teasing me about it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bueno, al menos el proyecto en sí salió a pedir de boca.
lines.en: Well, at least the project itself turned out perfectly.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, menos mal, aunque contratar ayuda externa nos costó un ojo de la cara.
lines.en: Yes, thank goodness, though hiring outside help cost us an arm and a leg.

days.title: Repaso: precisión y registro
days.objective: Consolidate por/para, governed prepositions, verbs of change, emphatic word order, diminutives and idioms in connected, natural speech.
days.paretoFocus: Bringing all of this block's precision tools together in one review is what turns isolated rules into fluent, natural production.
drills: Retell your week using at least one example of por, one verb of change, and one idiom.
Say one sentence with a diminutive that softens a request.
Explain aloud the difference between llegar a ser and convertirse en.

items: Recall the pair trabajo para mi jefa and trabajo por mi jefa and their different meanings.
Say one verb that always takes the preposition de.
Explain when a cleft sentence with lo que is useful.

activities.title: Todo junto
activities.intro: Real speech never isolates one rule at a time the way a lesson does; reaching for exactly the right preposition, verb of change or turn of phrase means drawing on several of this block's tools within the same breath, which is what today's examples model.

items.hr: Al final me hice autónomo, algo con lo que llevaba tiempo soñando.
items.en: In the end I became self-employed, something I'd been dreaming about for a while.
items.note: hacerse + soñar con + relative with lo que

items.hr: Fue un cambio grande, pero salió a pedir de boca.
items.en: It was a big change, but it turned out perfectly.
items.note: idiom reviewed inside a normal sentence

items.hr: Al principio me puse nerviosísimo, la verdad.
items.en: At first I got really nervous, to be honest.
items.note: ponerse + the superlativo absoluto -ísimo of nervioso, not an augmentative like -azo or -ón

items.hr: Lo que más me costó fue confiar en mis propias decisiones.
items.en: What cost me most was trusting my own decisions.
items.note: cleft sentence + confiar en, a governed preposition

items.hr: No fue barato montar el negocio, costó un ojo de la cara.
items.en: It wasn't cheap to set up the business, it cost an arm and a leg.
items.note: idiom closing the story

items.hr: Al final todo salió bien, aunque tuve que resolver un problemilla con el banco.
items.en: In the end everything went well, though I had to sort out a little issue with the bank.
items.note: problemilla, the diminutive reviewed alongside today's idioms and prepositions

activities.title: Repaso de precisión
activities.intro: Fill each gap by drawing on whichever tool from this block actually fits that sentence, not just the one you practised last.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Monté el negocio ___ mí mismo, nadie me obligó.'
questions.explanation: por mí mismo means by myself, on my own; por here marks that I acted alone, without help, not a reason or cause.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Con el tiempo, aquel pequeño taller ___ una empresa conocida.'
questions.explanation: a full transformation into something else takes convertirse en.

questions.prompt: Al principio no confiaba ___ mí mismo, pero mejoré con la práctica.
questions.explanation: confiar en, a fixed governed preposition.

questions.prompt: Fue carísimo, nos costó un ___ de la cara montarlo todo.
questions.explanation: costar un ojo de la cara, reviewing the idiom.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'What cost me most was trusting my own decisions.'
questions.explanation: cleft sentence lo que ... fue, plus confiar en.

activities.title: Contar toda la historia
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Tell the whole story of starting a business, weaving together this block's structures.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Cuéntamelo todo, ¿cómo decidiste montar el negocio?
lines.en: Tell me the whole thing, how did you decide to set up the business?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Llevaba años soñando con ello, así que al final me hice autónomo.
lines.en: I'd been dreaming about it for years, so in the end I became self-employed.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y no te puso nerviosísimo dejar tu trabajo fijo?
lines.en: And didn't it make you super nervous to leave your steady job?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Muchísimo, al principio no confiaba en mí mismo.
lines.en: A lot, at first I didn't trust myself.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Es normal. ¿Y el dinero, de dónde salió?
lines.en: That's normal. And the money, where did it come from?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Monté el negocio por mí mismo, sin ayuda de nadie, y costó un ojo de la cara.
lines.en: I set up the business by myself, without anyone's help, and it cost an arm and a leg.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y ahora? Parece que va bastante bien.
lines.en: And now? It seems to be going pretty well.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, aquel pequeño taller se convirtió en una empresa conocida en la zona.
lines.en: Yes, that little workshop turned into a well-known company in the area.

days.title: El contrato de trabajo y los derechos laborales
days.objective: Describe how an employment contract works, including its type, probation period, working hours, holidays and notice period, without quoting specific legal figures.
days.paretoFocus: Work dominates adult conversation, and describing contracts and rights in general terms rather than reciting figures that change is exactly the register both the exam and a real workplace expect.
drills: Describe your own contract, real or imagined, using at least three of today's terms.
Say one sentence about what a periodo de prueba is for.
Explain the difference between un contrato indefinido and un contrato temporal.

items: Recall a sentence with an idiom describing something expensive.
Say one sentence describing a company using ser or estar correctly.
Explain what a periodo de preaviso is, in general terms.

activities.title: El mundo laboral
activities.intro: This lesson describes how employment works as a process, not with real figures, since wages, holiday minimums and notice periods change and vary by sector. The contract itself is what states the exact numbers in any real case.

items.hr: Firmé un contrato indefinido después del periodo de prueba.
items.en: I signed a permanent contract after the probation period.
items.note: indefinido = permanent/open-ended here, unrelated to the pretérito indefinido verb tense of the same name

items.hr: El contrato indica cuántos días de vacaciones me corresponden.
items.en: The contract states how many vacation days I'm entitled to.
items.note: describing the process, not quoting a number

items.hr: Si quiero dejar el trabajo, tengo que respetar el preaviso.
items.en: If I want to leave the job, I have to respect the notice period.
items.note: si + present indicative, real condition

items.hr: La nómina llega a la cuenta a final de mes.
items.en: My salary is paid into the account at the end of the month.
items.note: nómina = salary/payslip; it refers to the monthly pay deposited, not just the paper slip

items.hr: Si te despiden sin motivo justificado, normalmente tienes derecho a algún tipo de indemnización.
items.en: If you're dismissed without a justified reason, you're usually entitled to some form of compensation.
items.note: the contract or the law sets the actual amount, not stated here

activities.title: Contratos y derechos
activities.intro: Practise describing employment conditions without quoting figures.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Antes de ser fijo, pasé por un periodo de ___.'
questions.explanation: periodo de prueba = probation period.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Un contrato ___ no tiene fecha de fin.'
questions.explanation: indefinido describes a contract with no set end date.

questions.prompt: Si quiero irme de la empresa, debo respetar el periodo de ___.
questions.explanation: preaviso = the notice period stated in the contract.

questions.prompt: Me pagan la ___ a final de cada mes.
questions.explanation: nómina = payslip/payroll.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The contract states how many vacation days I'm entitled to.'
questions.explanation: indicar + interrogative clause; corresponder = to be entitled to.

activities.title: Hablando del nuevo contrato
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Discuss the terms of a new job contract with a friend.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ya has firmado el contrato nuevo?
lines.en: Have you already signed the new contract?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, es un contrato indefinido, pero primero hay un periodo de prueba.
lines.en: Yes, it's a permanent contract, but first there's a probation period.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y las vacaciones? ¿Cuántos días te tocan?
lines.en: And the holidays? How many days do you get?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: El contrato lo indica todo, no me acuerdo del número exacto ahora.
lines.en: The contract states it all, I don't remember the exact number right now.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y si un día quieres dejarlo?
lines.en: And if one day you want to quit?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tengo que avisar con tiempo, respetar el preaviso.
lines.en: I have to give notice in advance, respect the notice period.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tiene sentido, así la empresa puede prepararse.
lines.en: That makes sense, so the company can prepare.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, es más justo para todos. Lo importante es que la nómina llega puntual cada mes.
lines.en: Yes, it's fairer for everyone that way. The important thing is the payslip arrives on time every month.

days.title: Buscar trabajo en el mercado laboral actual
days.objective: Talk about the job market, job ads and the process of applying for work, from browsing offers to attending an interview.
days.paretoFocus: Job searching is a near-universal B1 topic in exam speaking and writing tasks, and knowing the vocabulary for offers, applications and interviews lets a learner handle it fluently.
drills: Describe your ideal job offer using at least four new words.
Say one sentence about what makes a good curriculum.
Explain what carta de presentación means.

items: Recall a sentence about a contract's notice period.
Say one sentence with lo que to express what you value in a job.
