Explain the difference between presentarse a un puesto and postularse a un puesto.

activities.title: Buscar y solicitar empleo
activities.intro: This lesson covers the vocabulary of job hunting: reading offers, sending an application, and going through an interview. American Spanish often prefers postularse for a job where Spain says presentarse or apuntarse, both correct, always labelled.

items.hr: Vi una oferta de empleo que encajaba con mi perfil.
items.en: I saw a job offer that matched my profile.
items.note: oferta de empleo = job offer/vacancy

items.hr: Envié mi currículum y una carta de presentación.
items.en: I sent my resume and a cover letter.
items.note: currículum, common short form of currículum vitae

items.hr: Me llamaron para una entrevista la semana siguiente.
items.en: They called me for an interview the following week.
items.note: entrevista de trabajo

items.hr: En España se dice presentarse a un puesto; en gran parte de América se dice postularse a un puesto.
items.en: In Spain you say presentarse a un puesto; in much of America you say postularse a un puesto.
items.note: labelled American variant, same meaning: to apply for a position

items.hr: Al final me seleccionaron entre muchos candidatos.
items.en: In the end they selected me among many candidates.
items.note: ser seleccionado, the outcome of the process

activities.title: El proceso de selección
activities.intro: Practise the vocabulary of job hunting and applications.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Antes de la entrevista, tienes que preparar bien tu ___.'
questions.explanation: currículum = the document listing your experience, needed before an interview.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma peninsular para 'to apply for a job'?
questions.explanation: in Spain, presentarse; postularse is the common American equivalent, not wrong, just a different variety.

questions.prompt: Vi una ___ de empleo interesante en el tablón de la universidad.
questions.explanation: oferta de empleo = job offer.

questions.prompt: Me llamaron para una ___ el jueves por la tarde.
questions.explanation: entrevista = interview.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I sent my resume and a cover letter.'
questions.explanation: carta de presentación = cover letter, the exact phrase needed for the next lesson.

activities.title: Preparando la entrevista
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Prepare for a job interview with a friend, using the vocabulary of job hunting.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo va la búsqueda de trabajo?
lines.en: How's the job search going?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bien, vi una oferta que encajaba perfecto con mi perfil.
lines.en: Good, I saw an offer that matched my profile perfectly.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ya has enviado el currículum?
lines.en: Have you already sent the resume?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, con una carta de presentación bien pensada.
lines.en: Yes, with a well thought out cover letter.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y te han llamado?
lines.en: And have they called you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, tengo una entrevista el martes que viene.
lines.en: Yes, I have an interview next Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué vas a decir si te preguntan por qué quieres el puesto?
lines.en: What are you going to say if they ask why you want the position?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Que lo que más valoro de esta empresa es el buen ambiente de trabajo.
lines.en: That what I value most about this company is the good work environment.

days.title: Escribir una carta de presentación formal
days.objective: Write a formal cover letter in Spanish, using the correct opening, structure, register and closing conventions.
days.paretoFocus: The formal cover letter is a genre the exam and real job applications both demand, and its conventions (salutation, structure, formal register, closing) are fixed and easy to get wrong without explicit teaching.
drills: Write your own three-paragraph cover letter for an invented job offer.
List the formal opening and closing phrases from today's lesson.
Explain why usted is used throughout a formal cover letter.

items: Recall a sentence describing a job offer.
Say one formal opening phrase for a letter.
Explain what Estimado/a Sr./Sra. means and when to use it.

activities.title: Estructura de la carta formal
activities.intro: A formal cover letter opens with a fixed salutation, states the position and where you saw it, briefly summarises your relevant experience, and closes with a fixed formal phrase. Usted is used throughout; the register stays formal, and diminutives such as momentito, common in spoken Spanish, never appear here.

items.hr: Estimada Sra. Roldán:
items.en: Dear Ms. Roldán,
items.note: the fixed formal salutation

items.hr: Me dirijo a usted en relación con la oferta de comercial publicada por su empresa.
items.en: I am writing to you regarding the sales position advertised by your company.
items.note: the fixed formal opening for a cover letter

items.hr: Cuento con tres años de experiencia en el sector y considero que mi perfil encaja con el puesto.
items.en: I have three years of experience in the sector and I believe my profile fits the position.
items.note: cuento con, the governed preposition reviewed from an earlier lesson

items.hr: Adjunto mi currículum para su valoración.
items.en: I attach my resume for your consideration.
items.note: adjuntar, the standard formal verb for attaching a document

items.hr: Quedo a su disposición para una entrevista. Atentamente,
items.en: I remain available for an interview. Sincerely,
items.note: the fixed formal closing

activities.title: La carta de presentación
activities.intro: Practise the fixed phrases and register of a formal cover letter.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el saludo formal correcto para abrir la carta?
questions.explanation: a formal salutation never uses a diminutive; Estimadita would be entirely inappropriate in this register.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el cierre formal correcto?
questions.explanation: the fixed closing formula for a formal letter.

questions.prompt: Me ___ a usted en relación con la oferta publicada por su empresa.
questions.explanation: dirigirse a alguien = to address someone, the standard opening verb.

questions.prompt: ___ mi currículum para su valoración.
questions.explanation: adjuntar = to attach, the standard formal verb for enclosing a document.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I remain available for an interview.'
questions.explanation: the fixed closing formula before Atentamente.

activities.title: Redactando la carta
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Get feedback from a friend on the cover letter you are drafting for a job application.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo vas con la carta de presentación?
lines.en: How's the cover letter coming along?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ya tengo el saludo, puse Estimada Sra. Roldán.
lines.en: I've got the greeting, I put Dear Ms. Roldán.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bien, ¿y explicaste por qué te interesa el puesto?
lines.en: Good, and did you explain why you're interested in the position?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, dije que cuento con tres años de experiencia en el sector.
lines.en: Yes, I said I have three years of experience in the sector.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Recuerda adjuntar el currículum y ser formal, nada de expresiones informales.
lines.en: Remember to attach the resume and be formal, no informal expressions.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tranquilo, no he puesto ni un solo momentito ni nada parecido.
lines.en: Don't worry, I haven't put a single 'just a sec' or anything like that.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perfecto. ¿Y cómo la vas a cerrar?
lines.en: Perfect. And how are you going to close it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Con quedo a su disposición para una entrevista, atentamente.
lines.en: With 'I remain available for an interview, sincerely.'

days.title: Estudios y formación continua
days.objective: Talk about education, training courses and lifelong learning, including going back to study as an adult.
days.paretoFocus: Talking about education and ongoing training is a core personal-and-academic-domain topic, useful for both the exam and real conversations about careers and self-improvement.
drills: Describe a course you would like to take and why.
Say one sentence about the difference between estudiar and formarse.
Explain what aprendizaje a lo largo de la vida means in your own words.

items: Recall a formal phrase from a cover letter.
Say one sentence with a verb of change describing someone who became a teacher.
Explain the difference between un curso presencial and un curso a distancia.

activities.title: Formarse toda la vida
activities.intro: This lesson covers vocabulary for education beyond school: courses, qualifications, and the idea that learning continues throughout adult life. A curso presencial meets in person; a curso a distancia or online happens remotely.

items.hr: Decidí volver a estudiar para sacarme un título.
items.en: I decided to go back to studying to get a qualification.
items.note: volver a + infinitivo, periphrasis reviewed

items.hr: Me apunté a un curso de formación por las tardes.
items.en: I signed up for a training course in the evenings.
items.note: apuntarse a = to sign up for

items.hr: Prefiero un curso presencial porque aprendo mejor en persona.
items.en: I prefer an in-person course because I learn better face to face.
items.note: presencial vs a distancia

items.hr: El aprendizaje a lo largo de la vida cada vez importa más.
items.en: Lifelong learning matters more and more.
items.note: aprendizaje a lo largo de la vida = lifelong learning

items.hr: Nunca es tarde para formarse en algo nuevo.
items.en: It's never too late to train in something new.
items.note: formarse = to train/educate oneself

activities.title: Estudiar de adulto
activities.intro: Practise vocabulary about education and lifelong learning.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Prefiero estudiar en casa, así que elegí un curso ___.'
questions.explanation: a distancia = remote/online, matching studying from home.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Después de dejarlo hace años, decidió ___ a estudiar por las noches.'
questions.explanation: volver a + infinitivo = to do something again; volver a estudiar = to go back to studying.

questions.prompt: Me ___ a un curso de formación que empieza el mes que viene.
questions.explanation: apuntarse a = to sign up for.

questions.prompt: Nunca es tarde para ___ en algo nuevo.
questions.explanation: formarse = to train/educate oneself.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'She signed up for a training course in the evenings.'
questions.explanation: apuntarse a + curso, reviewed in a new sentence.

activities.title: Volver a las aulas
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. You just signed up for an evening course; catch up with a friend on why now and what it's like starting again after years away from a classroom.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Es verdad que vas a volver a estudiar?
lines.en: Is it true you're going back to studying?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, me he apuntado a un curso de formación por las tardes.
lines.en: Yes, I've signed up for a training course in the evenings.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Presencial o a distancia?
lines.en: In person or remote?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A distancia, así puedo seguir trabajando a la vez.
lines.en: Remote, that way I can keep working at the same time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué bien! ¿Y de qué tema es?
lines.en: That's great! And what's it about?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: La verdad, cuando empecé no tenía ni idea del tema, pero ahora me encanta.
lines.en: Honestly, when I started I had no clue about the subject, but now I love it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Nunca es tarde para formarse en algo nuevo, como dices siempre.
lines.en: It's never too late to train in something new, like you always say.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exacto, y este curso me está abriendo muchas puertas.
lines.en: Exactly, and this course is opening a lot of doors for me.

days.title: Comprar o alquilar una vivienda
days.objective: Discuss the process of renting or buying a home, including the contract, deposit and the main clauses a tenant or buyer should check.
days.paretoFocus: Housing is one of the most practically important B1 topics, and knowing how to discuss contracts, deposits and conditions in general terms lets a learner navigate a real rental or purchase.
drills: List three things a rental contract should specify.
Say one sentence about the difference between alquilar and comprar.
Explain what una fianza is for.

items: Recall a sentence about signing an employment contract.
Say one sentence contrasting alquilar and comprar.
Explain what el/la propietario/a and el/la inquilino/a mean.

activities.title: Alquilar o comprar
activities.intro: This lesson covers the vocabulary of housing: renting versus buying, the contract, the deposit, and the roles of landlord and tenant. As with work, prefer describing how the process works over quoting a real market price.

items.hr: Firmamos el contrato de alquiler por un año.
items.en: We signed the rental contract for a year.
items.note: contrato de alquiler = rental contract

items.hr: El propietario nos pidió una fianza antes de entregarnos las llaves.
items.en: The landlord asked us for a deposit before handing over the keys.
items.note: propietario/a = landlord/owner; fianza = deposit

items.hr: Como inquilinos, tenemos derecho a que nos devuelvan la fianza al final.
items.en: As tenants, we're entitled to get the deposit back at the end.
items.note: inquilino/a = tenant

items.hr: Estamos pensando en pedir una hipoteca para comprar un piso.
items.en: We're thinking about applying for a mortgage to buy a flat.
items.note: hipoteca = mortgage

items.hr: Antes de firmar, conviene leer bien todas las cláusulas del contrato.
items.en: Before signing, it's worth reading all the clauses of the contract carefully.
items.note: cláusula = clause

activities.title: El contrato de alquiler
activities.intro: Practise vocabulary about renting and buying a home.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'El ___ nos pidió una fianza antes de entregarnos las llaves.'
questions.explanation: propietario = the landlord, the one who asks for the deposit.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Para comprar el piso, pedimos una ___ al banco.'
questions.explanation: hipoteca = mortgage, the loan for buying a home.

questions.prompt: Como ___, tenemos derecho a que nos devuelvan la fianza al final del contrato.
questions.explanation: inquilino/a = tenant.

questions.prompt: Antes de firmar, conviene leer bien todas las ___ del contrato.
questions.explanation: cláusula = clause.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We signed the rental contract for a year.'
questions.explanation: por + duration; contrato de alquiler is the fixed phrase for rental contract.

activities.title: Buscando piso
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Discuss the pros and cons of renting versus buying with a friend.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Al final vais a alquilar o a comprar?
lines.en: In the end are you going to rent or buy?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: De momento alquilar, comprar nos costaría un ojo de la cara ahora mismo.
lines.en: For now, rent, buying would cost us an arm and a leg right now.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tiene sentido. ¿Y el contrato ya está firmado?
lines.en: Makes sense. And is the contract already signed?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, lo firmamos por un año, con el propietario presente.
lines.en: Yes, we signed it for a year, with the landlord present.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Os pidió mucha fianza?
lines.en: Did he ask for a big deposit?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo normal, y leímos bien todas las cláusulas antes de firmar nada.
lines.en: The usual amount, and we read all the clauses carefully before signing anything.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bien hecho. Algún día ese ahorro se convertirá en la entrada de un piso propio.
lines.en: Well done. Someday that saving will turn into the down payment for your own flat.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Esa es la idea, aunque de momento estamos tranquilos como inquilinos.
lines.en: That's the idea, though for now we're happy as tenants.

days.title: El barrio y la vida urbana
days.objective: Describe a neighbourhood and everyday urban life, including its services, atmosphere and problems.
days.paretoFocus: Describing where you live and its surroundings is a constant conversational and exam topic, and vocabulary for services and urban problems lets that description go beyond the basics.
drills: Describe your neighbourhood in five sentences using today's vocabulary.
Say one sentence about a problem a city might face.
Explain what convivencia vecinal means.

items: Recall a sentence about a rental contract.
Say one sentence with lo que to describe what you like about your area.
Explain the difference between el centro and las afueras.

activities.title: Vivir en la ciudad
activities.intro: This lesson describes neighbourhoods and city life in general terms, without naming any real district, so the vocabulary transfers to any city the learner actually lives in.

items.hr: Vivo en un barrio tranquilo, cerca de un parque grande.
items.en: I live in a quiet neighbourhood, near a big park.
items.note: barrio = neighbourhood

items.hr: Lo que más me gusta de mi calle es que hay poco ruido.
items.en: What I like most about my street is that there's little noise.
items.note: cleft sentence reviewed

items.hr: El ayuntamiento está arreglando las aceras de esta zona.
items.en: The city council is fixing the pavements in this area.
items.note: ayuntamiento, a generic institution noun, never named

items.hr: En las afueras hay menos vida, pero es más barato vivir.
items.en: In the outskirts there's less going on, but it's cheaper to live.
items.note: afueras = outskirts

items.hr: La convivencia vecinal mejora cuando todos cuidan las zonas comunes.
items.en: Neighbourly coexistence improves when everyone looks after the shared areas.
items.note: convivencia vecinal = neighbourly coexistence

activities.title: Describir el barrio
activities.intro: Practise describing a neighbourhood and city life.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Vivo en ___, lejos del centro pero donde es mucho más barato vivir.'
questions.explanation: afueras = the outskirts, the area far from the center.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'El ___ está reformando las aceras de mi calle.'
questions.explanation: ayuntamiento = the city council, the generic body responsible for streets.

questions.prompt: Lo que más me gusta de mi barrio es lo ___ (quiet) que es por las noches.
questions.explanation: lo + adjective + que reviewed, expressing degree.

questions.prompt: La ___ vecinal mejora cuando todos cuidan las zonas comunes.
questions.explanation: convivencia vecinal = neighbourly coexistence.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I live in a quiet neighbourhood, where there's a big park nearby.'
questions.explanation: donde introduces a relative clause locked to this word order.

activities.title: Enseñando el barrio
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Show a friend around your neighbourhood and talk about urban life.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué tranquilo es esto! ¿Siempre ha sido así?
lines.en: This is so quiet! Has it always been like this?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bastante, aunque el ayuntamiento lleva meses arreglando las aceras.
lines.en: Pretty much, though the council has been fixing the pavements for months.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y hay buena convivencia vecinal aquí?
lines.en: And is there good neighbourly coexistence here?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, todos cuidamos las zonas comunes, es lo que más me gusta.
lines.en: Yes, we all look after the shared areas, that's what I like most.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿No preferirías vivir más cerca del centro?
lines.en: Wouldn't you prefer to live closer to the center?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: La verdad, prefiero las afueras, es más barato y más tranquilo.
lines.en: Honestly, I prefer the outskirts, it's cheaper and quieter.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tiene sentido, sobre todo ahora que has firmado el contrato por un año.
lines.en: Makes sense, especially now that you've signed the contract for a year.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exacto, así que de momento me quedo por aquí sin pensarlo más.
lines.en: Exactly, so for now I'm staying around here without thinking about it more.

days.title: El transporte y la movilidad
days.objective: Discuss everyday transport options, commuting habits and urban mobility, comparing peninsular and American vocabulary where they differ.
days.paretoFocus: Getting around is a daily necessity and a constant exam theme, and knowing both the peninsular terms and their American counterparts prepares a learner for both production and the varied listening/reading input at this level.
drills: Describe how you get to work or study using at least three transport words.
Say the peninsular and American word for bus.
Explain when you would rather walk than take the bus.

items: Recall a sentence describing your neighbourhood.
Say one sentence with an idiom meaning to have no clue.
Explain what convivencia vecinal means.

activities.title: Moverse por la ciudad
activities.intro: This lesson covers everyday transport vocabulary. In Spain, coger el autobús is completely ordinary and used without a second thought; in much of America, coger has a vulgar sense in this context and tomar el autobús is used instead. Both forms are correct in their own variety.

items.hr: Cojo el autobús todos los días para ir al trabajo.
items.en: I take the bus every day to go to work.
items.note: peninsular: coger el autobús, used normally and without any hesitation

items.hr: En gran parte de América se dice tomar el autobús en lugar de coger el autobús.
items.en: In much of America you say tomar el autobús instead of coger el autobús.
items.note: labelled American equivalent, not a mistake

items.hr: Prefiero ir en bici cuando no llueve.
items.en: I prefer to go by bike when it's not raining.
items.note: ir en + means of transport

items.hr: El coche se quedó parado en un atasco enorme.
items.en: The car got stuck in a huge traffic jam.
items.note: atasco = traffic jam; en América se dice también un embotellamiento

items.hr: Voy andando siempre que puedo, es más sano.
items.en: I walk whenever I can, it's healthier.
items.note: ir andando = to go on foot

items.hr: En España se dice conducir y aparcar el coche; en gran parte de América se dice manejar y estacionar el carro.
items.en: In Spain you say conducir and aparcar el coche; in much of America you say manejar and estacionar el carro.
items.note: labelled American equivalents: conducir/manejar = to drive; aparcar/estacionar = to park

activities.title: Ir de un sitio a otro
activities.intro: Practise transport vocabulary, including peninsular and American variants.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma habitual en España para 'to take the bus'?
questions.explanation: in Spain, coger el autobús is the ordinary everyday expression.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Hoy hay mucho tráfico, seguro que hay un ___ enorme.'
questions.explanation: atasco = traffic jam.

questions.prompt: Prefiero ir ___ cuando no llueve, así hago ejercicio.
questions.explanation: ir andando = to go on foot.

questions.prompt: En gran parte de América se dice ___ el autobús en vez de coger el autobús.
questions.explanation: tomar el autobús is the common American equivalent of the peninsular coger el autobús.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I take the bus every day to go to work.'
questions.explanation: coger, the ordinary peninsular verb, used without comment.

activities.title: El trayecto al trabajo
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Compare how you and a friend get around the city, including a note on regional vocabulary.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo vas al trabajo normalmente?
lines.en: How do you usually get to work?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Cojo el autobús, tarda unos veinte minutos.
lines.en: I take the bus, it takes about twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo prefiero ir andando cuando hace buen tiempo.
lines.en: I prefer to walk when the weather's nice.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Yo también, aunque hoy hay un atasco tremendo por las obras.
lines.en: Me too, though today there's a huge traffic jam because of the roadworks.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Por cierto, ¿cómo te fue en la entrevista de la semana pasada?
lines.en: By the way, how did last week's interview go?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Muy bien, empiezo el mes que viene, y está cerca, puedo ir en bici.
lines.en: Very well, I start next month, and it's close, I can go by bike.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué suerte! Así te ahorras el autobús todos los días.
lines.en: How lucky! That way you save yourself the bus every day.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, aunque cuando llueve seguro que cojo el autobús igual.
lines.en: Yes, though when it rains I'll definitely take the bus anyway.

days.title: Viajes y turismo
days.objective: Plan and describe a trip, including booking, transport and typical tourist activities, using an invented travel agency and destinations.
days.paretoFocus: Travel is one of the richest B1 topics for narrating plans, giving opinions and describing experiences, and it recycles nearly every past and future structure the course has taught.
drills: Plan an imaginary trip using at least four travel words.
Say one sentence about what you'd like to visit in the Pyrenees.
Explain what conviene reservar con antelación means.

items: Recall a sentence about taking the bus or walking somewhere.
Say one sentence using the future of probability.
Explain the difference between un billete de ida and un billete de ida y vuelta.

activities.title: Planear un viaje
activities.intro: Names matter here: any business you book through, hotel you stay at, or company you deal with should be invented, but the mountains, islands and cities around it stay real, since nothing here claims that any actual company offers these services.

items.hr: Reservé el viaje a través de la agencia Viajes Brújula.
items.en: I booked the trip through Brújula Travel Agency.
items.note: invented agency name, used consistently

items.hr: Compré un billete de ida y vuelta a las Canarias.
items.en: I bought a round trip ticket to the Canaries.
items.note: billete de ida y vuelta vs solo de ida

items.hr: Conviene reservar el alojamiento con antelación en temporada alta.
items.en: It's worth booking accommodation in advance during high season.
items.note: con antelación = in advance

items.hr: Nos alojamos en un hotel pequeño cerca del casco antiguo.
items.en: We stayed in a small hotel near the old town.
items.note: casco antiguo, a generic term for old town, usable anywhere

items.hr: Este verano queremos hacer senderismo por los Pirineos.
items.en: This summer we want to go hiking in the Pyrenees.
items.note: hacer senderismo = to go hiking

activities.title: Reservar y viajar
activities.intro: Practise vocabulary for planning and describing a trip.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Como vamos a volver, mejor comprar un billete de ___.'
questions.explanation: ida y vuelta = round trip, needed because they plan to return.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'En temporada alta, conviene reservar el hotel con ___.'
questions.explanation: con antelación = in advance.

questions.prompt: ___ (reservar, nosotros) el viaje a través de una agencia especializada en las Canarias.
questions.explanation: reservar in the nosotros preterite form.

questions.prompt: Este verano queremos hacer ___ por los Pirineos.
questions.explanation: hacer senderismo = to go hiking.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We stayed in a small hotel near the old town.'
questions.explanation: alojarse = to stay/lodge; casco antiguo = old town.

activities.title: En la agencia de viajes
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Plan a trip to the Canaries with a friend using travel vocabulary.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Al final reservasteis el viaje a las Canarias?
lines.en: Did you end up booking the trip to the Canaries?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, a través de Viajes Brújula, nos hicieron un buen precio.
lines.en: Yes, through Brújula Travel Agency, they gave us a good price.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Compraste billete de ida y vuelta?
lines.en: Did you buy a round trip ticket?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, y reservamos el hotel con antelación porque es temporada alta.
lines.en: Of course, and we booked the hotel in advance because it's high season.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y qué vais a hacer allí?
lines.en: And what are you going to do there?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sobre todo playa, aunque también queremos hacer senderismo por la isla.
lines.en: Mostly the beach, though we also want to go hiking on the island.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Suena genial! ¿Recuerdas cuando escribiste aquella carta tan formal a la agencia por el error de la reserva?
lines.en: Sounds great! Do you remember when you wrote that really formal letter to the agency about the booking mistake?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, terminé con 'quedo a su disposición' y todo, muy serio.
lines.en: Of course, I even ended with 'I remain available', very serious.

days.title: Las vacaciones y el tiempo libre
days.objective: Talk about holidays and free time, including plans, preferences and how people typically choose to spend their time off.
days.paretoFocus: Holidays and leisure are frequent, low-stakes conversation topics that let a learner practise plans, preferences and opinions fluently.
drills: Describe your ideal holiday in five sentences.
Say one sentence about a hobby you do in your free time.
Explain the difference between unas vacaciones and un día libre.

items: Recall a sentence about booking a hotel in advance.
Say one sentence with a verb of change describing a hobby that became a passion.
Explain what casco antiguo means.

activities.title: Descansar y desconectar
activities.intro: Free time reveals something work rarely does: whether someone reaches for total idleness, a hobby that turned into a habit, or simply time with friends says as much about their personality as their schedule.

items.hr: Este año quiero pasar las vacaciones sin hacer nada en absoluto.
items.en: This year I want to spend the holidays doing absolutely nothing.
items.note: pasar las vacaciones = to spend the holidays

items.hr: Me apetece desconectar del trabajo por completo unas semanas.
items.en: I feel like disconnecting from work completely for a few weeks.
items.note: desconectar de = to unplug from

items.hr: Los fines de semana suelo quedar con amigos o leer tranquilamente.
items.en: On weekends I usually meet up with friends or read quietly.
items.note: soler + infinitivo, periphrasis reviewed

items.hr: Lo que más disfruto en vacaciones es no tener horarios.
items.en: What I enjoy most on holiday is not having a schedule.
items.note: cleft sentence reviewed

items.hr: Empecé a hacer yoga por diversión y se convirtió en una rutina diaria.
items.en: I started doing yoga for fun and it turned into a daily routine.
items.note: empezar a + infinitivo and convertirse en, both reviewed

activities.title: Tiempo libre y descanso
activities.intro: Practise vocabulary about holidays and leisure.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Necesito ___ del trabajo unos días, estoy agotada.'
questions.explanation: desconectar de = to disconnect from, exactly what you need after a tiring stretch of work.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Los sábados ___ quedar con amigos por la tarde.'
questions.explanation: soler + infinitivo describes a habitual action.

questions.prompt: Este año quiero ___ las vacaciones sin hacer nada en absoluto.
questions.explanation: pasar las vacaciones = to spend the holidays.

questions.prompt: Lo que más ___ en vacaciones es no tener horarios.
questions.explanation: cleft sentence: lo que + verb, here disfrutar = to enjoy.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I feel like disconnecting from work completely for a few weeks.'
questions.explanation: apetecer, a gustar-class verb, plus desconectar de.

activities.title: Planes para las vacaciones
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about holiday plans and how you like to spend free time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué planes tienes para las vacaciones?
lines.en: What plans do you have for the holidays?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ninguno, la verdad, solo quiero desconectar del trabajo por completo.
lines.en: None, honestly, I just want to disconnect from work completely.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ni siquiera vas a seguir con el curso de formación?
lines.en: Not even going to continue with the training course?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ese sí, pero solo un par de horas a la semana, nada más.
lines.en: That one yes, but just a couple of hours a week, nothing more.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo suelo quedar con amigos y leer los fines de semana.
lines.en: I usually meet up with friends and read on weekends.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo que más disfruto yo es no tener horarios fijos por una vez.
lines.en: What I enjoy most is not having fixed schedules for once.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Se nota, has empezado a hacer yoga y ahora es tu rutina diaria.
lines.en: You can tell, you've started doing yoga and now it's your daily routine.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es verdad, se ha convertido en algo esencial para desconectar.
lines.en: True, it's become something essential for disconnecting.

days.title: La alimentación y los hábitos alimentarios
days.objective: Discuss diet, eating habits and food preferences, including peninsular and American vocabulary for common foods.
days.paretoFocus: Food and eating habits are a constant, practical topic, and the peninsular/Latin American vocabulary split here (patata/papa across Latin America, judías verdes/ejotes in Mexico and Central America) is exactly the kind of variety exposure the exam expects at this level.
drills: Describe your typical daily diet using at least four food words.
Say the peninsular and American word for potato.
Explain the difference between comer sano and estar a dieta.

items: Recall a sentence about disconnecting from work.
Say one sentence using an idiom about something turning out well.
Explain what llevar una dieta equilibrada means.

activities.title: Comer bien

lines.hr: ¿Sigues usando tanto las redes sociales?
lines.en: Do you still use social media as much?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, pero ahora comparto menos para que no todo el mundo vea mi vida.
lines.en: Yes, but now I share less so that not everyone sees my life.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo prefiero un grupo de chat pequeño, solo con la familia.
lines.en: I prefer a small chat group, just with family.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es más tranquilo. En los grupos grandes se comparte de todo.
lines.en: It's calmer. In big groups everything gets shared.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y no te preocupa la privacidad?
lines.en: And doesn't privacy worry you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, por eso reviso la configuración para que solo mis contactos vean mis publicaciones.
lines.en: Yes, that's why I check the settings so that only my contacts see my posts.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buena idea. Yo también debería hacerlo.
lines.en: Good idea. I should do that too.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Hazlo esta semana, antes de que subas más fotos.
lines.en: Do it this week, before you post more photos.

days.title: Las noticias y los medios de comunicación
days.objective: Talk about news and media using an invented newspaper and broadcaster, reporting what they said with the correct tense shift.
days.paretoFocus: News is a core B1 reading and listening genre on the exam, and reporting a source's words recycles reported speech in the past, this course's hardest B1 narrative skill.
drills: Write two invented headlines for a newspaper called El Diario Trébol.
Report, in your own words, something a radio station announced this morning.
List three words you'd expect in a news broadcast.

items: How do you shift the tense when you report what someone said in the past?
What ending marks the future of regular -ar verbs?
Name one connector used to link ideas in a written text.

activities.title: Las noticias de hoy
activities.intro: Meet an invented newspaper, El Diario Trébol, and an invented broadcaster, Radio Confluencia. Use them to practise reported speech in the past and the future for predictions.

items.hr: El Diario Trébol informó de que el precio de la vivienda había subido otra vez.
items.en: El Diario Trébol reported that housing prices had gone up again.
items.note: reported speech with pluscuamperfecto

items.hr: Según Radio Confluencia, mañana hará mucho viento en la costa.
items.en: According to Radio Confluencia, tomorrow it will be very windy on the coast.
items.note: future for a prediction

items.hr: El periodista dijo que la noticia se había confirmado esa misma tarde.
items.en: The journalist said the news had been confirmed that very afternoon.
items.note: reported speech with pluscuamperfecto

items.hr: En la portada del Diario Trébol siempre se destaca el titular más importante.
items.en: On El Diario Trébol's front page, the most important headline always stands out.
items.note: passive se, agreeing with the singular subject el titular

items.hr: Dudo que esa noticia sea del todo cierta, hay que contrastarla.
items.en: I doubt that news is entirely true, it needs to be checked.
items.note: dudar que plus subjunctive

activities.title: Informando de las noticias
activities.intro: Practise reporting news in the past and predicting news in the future.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta? 'El Diario Trébol informó de que el precio ___ subido el mes anterior.'
questions.explanation: pluscuamperfecto for an event before the reported past moment.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué palabra nombra el título grande que encabeza una noticia?
questions.explanation: el titular is the headline, the short title heading a news story.

questions.prompt: Según Radio Confluencia, mañana ___ (hacer) mucho viento en la costa.
questions.explanation: future simple for a prediction.

questions.prompt: El periódico ___ leo cada mañana es el Diario Trébol.
questions.explanation: relative que, known antecedent.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I doubt that news is entirely true.'
questions.explanation: dudar que triggers the subjunctive sea.

activities.title: Comentando la prensa
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. El Diario Trébol and Radio Confluencia both ran a story this morning; catch up on what each outlet said and whether it checks out.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has visto la portada del Diario Trébol hoy?
lines.en: Have you seen El Diario Trébol's front page today?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, dicen que el precio de la vivienda ha subido otra vez.
lines.en: Yes, they say housing prices have gone up again.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué mal! ¿Y de qué más informan?
lines.en: That's bad! And what else are they reporting on?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Según Radio Confluencia, mañana hará mucho viento en la costa.
lines.en: According to Radio Confluencia, tomorrow it will be very windy on the coast.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Menos mal que no es nada grave.
lines.en: At least it's nothing serious.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Dudo que esa otra noticia del titular sea del todo cierta, la verdad.
lines.en: I doubt that other headline story is entirely true, honestly.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tienes razón, hay que contrastar siempre las fuentes.
lines.en: You're right, you should always check your sources.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Por eso yo leo dos periódicos distintos antes de opinar.
lines.en: That's why I read two different newspapers before forming an opinion.

days.title: La publicidad y el consumo
days.objective: Talk about advertising and consumer habits, describing how ads try to change what people become or do.
days.paretoFocus: Advertising language is full of verbs of change and comparison, both B1 grammar points that need real practice contexts.
drills: Describe an invented advert you saw recently.
Write two comparatives comparing two products.
Explain, in Spanish, why an advert did or didn't convince you.

items: How do you form the comparative of superiority with an adjective?
Name a verb that means 'to become' used with an adjective.
What's the difference between por, which marks cause, and para, which marks purpose?

activities.title: El poder de la publicidad
activities.intro: Advertising language recycles verbs of change (hacerse, volverse) and comparatives, both taught earlier, inside a new topic.

items.hr: La publicidad quiere que nos hagamos clientes fieles de una marca.
items.en: Advertising wants us to become loyal customers of a brand.
items.note: querer que plus subjunctive, plus hacerse

items.hr: Este anuncio es mucho más convincente que el anterior.
items.en: This ad is much more convincing than the previous one.
items.note: comparative of superiority

items.hr: La gente se vuelve más exigente cuando compara precios antes de comprar.
items.en: People become more demanding when they compare prices before buying.
items.note: volverse for a gradual change

items.hr: Compro esta marca para ahorrar, no por la publicidad.
items.en: I buy this brand to save money, not because of the advertising.
items.note: para for purpose, por for cause

items.hr: Antes de comprar, conviene que leas bien las condiciones del anuncio.
items.en: Before buying, it's a good idea for you to read the ad's conditions carefully.
items.note: convenir que plus subjunctive

activities.title: Anuncios y marcas
activities.intro: Practise verbs of change and por/para in the context of advertising.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta? 'Con los años, sin proponérselo, la gente ___ más exigente al comparar precios.'
questions.explanation: volverse fits a gradual, general change.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'un anuncio convincente'?
questions.explanation: convincente means it convinces you.

questions.prompt: Compro esta marca ___ ahorrar, no por la publicidad.
questions.explanation: para expresses the purpose of buying.

questions.prompt: Este anuncio es mucho más convincente ___ el anterior.
questions.explanation: más...que forms the comparative.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Before buying, it's a good idea for you to read the conditions.'
questions.explanation: conviene que triggers the subjunctive leas.

activities.title: Hablando de un anuncio
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Discuss an advert, exercising verbs of change and por/para.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Viste el anuncio nuevo de la marca de zapatillas?
lines.en: Did you see the new sneaker brand's advert?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, quieren que nos hagamos clientes fieles, como siempre.
lines.en: Yes, they want us to become loyal customers, as always.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: A mí me pareció mucho más convincente que el anterior.
lines.en: I found it much more convincing than the previous one.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Puede ser, pero yo compro por el precio, no por la publicidad.
lines.en: Maybe, but I buy for the price, not for the advertising.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Haces bien. La gente se vuelve muy exigente cuando compara antes de comprar.
lines.en: Good for you. People become very demanding when they compare before buying.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exacto, y conviene que leas siempre la letra pequeña del anuncio.
lines.en: Exactly, and it's a good idea to always read the ad's fine print.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tienes razón, muchas veces ahí está la letra pequeña importante.
lines.en: You're right, often the important fine print is there.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Por eso nunca compro nada sin comparar dos o tres opciones.
lines.en: That's why I never buy anything without comparing two or three options.

days.title: El dinero, el ahorro y las finanzas personales
days.objective: Discuss money, saving and personal budgeting, giving advice and describing plans.
days.paretoFocus: Personal finance sits squarely in the DELE's ámbito personal, and giving advice recycles the conditional, this course's most everyday register move.
drills: Write three pieces of money advice using deberías.
Describe one saving goal you have for this year.
List three words related to a personal budget.

items: How do you form the conditional of regular verbs?
What's the difference between ahorrar and gastar?
Name a phrase that expresses a future plan using pensar.

activities.title: Ahorrar y gastar
activities.intro: Personal finance recycles the conditional for advice and the pluscuamperfecto, both taught earlier, inside a new, practical topic.

items.hr: Deberías ahorrar un poco cada mes, aunque sea poco.
items.en: You should save a little each month, even if it's a small amount.
items.note: deberías for advice

items.hr: Yo, en tu lugar, haría un presupuesto antes de gastar.
items.en: In your place, I would make a budget before spending.
items.note: conditional for advice

items.hr: Cuando cobre este mes, pienso ahorrar la mitad.
items.en: When I get paid this month, I plan to save half.
items.note: cuando plus subjunctive, future value

items.hr: Había gastado casi todo el sueldo cuando llegó el recibo de la luz.
items.en: I had spent almost my whole salary when the electricity bill arrived.
items.note: pluscuamperfecto

items.hr: Es importante que controles tus gastos fijos cada mes.
items.en: It's important that you keep track of your fixed expenses each month.
items.note: value judgement plus subjunctive

activities.title: Gestionar el dinero
activities.intro: Practise the conditional for advice and the pluscuamperfecto with money topics.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Yo, en tu lugar, ___ un presupuesto antes de gastar.'
questions.explanation: conditional simple for hypothetical advice.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'ahorrar'?
questions.explanation: ahorrar means to save money.

questions.prompt: Cuando ___ (cobrar) este mes, pienso ahorrar la mitad.
questions.explanation: cuando plus subjunctive for a future event.

questions.prompt: ___ (gastar) casi todo el sueldo cuando llegó el recibo de la luz.
questions.explanation: pluscuamperfecto: an event completed before another past event.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'You should save a little each month.'
questions.explanation: deberías plus infinitive gives advice.

activities.title: Hablando de ahorro
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about saving money, exercising the conditional for advice and the pluscuamperfecto.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo llevas el ahorro este mes?
lines.en: How's your saving going this month?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Fatal, ya me había quedado sin nada cuando vi la factura de la luz.
lines.en: Terrible, I'd already run out of money by the time I saw the electricity bill.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Deberías guardar algo aparte cada mes, aunque sea una cantidad pequeña.
lines.en: You should set something aside each month, even if it's a small amount.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ya lo sé, cuando cobre, aparto la mitad sin falta esta vez.
lines.en: I know, when I get paid, I'm setting aside half without fail this time.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo, en tu lugar, me haría un presupuesto antes de gastar nada.
lines.en: In your place, I'd make myself a budget before spending anything.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Buena idea, es hora de que vigile mejor mis gastos fijos.
lines.en: Good idea, it's time I kept a better eye on my fixed expenses.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Empieza por apuntar todo lo que gastas en una semana.
lines.en: Start by writing down everything you spend in a week.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, lo voy a intentar desde mañana.
lines.en: Okay, I'm going to try that starting tomorrow.

days.title: Comprar por internet y los derechos del consumidor
days.objective: Talk about online shopping and consumer rights, describing what to do when a purchase goes wrong.
days.paretoFocus: Consumer complaints are a real DELE writing and speaking prompt, and this recycles the negative imperative and relative clauses with the subjunctive over an uncertain antecedent.
drills: Write two sentences describing an online purchase you'd make.
List two consumer rights a buyer generally has.
Practise the negative imperative with a shopping-related verb.

items: How is the negative imperative formed?
When does a relative clause need the subjunctive instead of the indicative?
Name one direct object pronoun.

activities.title: Comprar con seguridad
activities.intro: Online shopping recycles the negative imperative and relative clauses over an uncertain antecedent, both taught earlier, inside a new practical topic.

items.hr: No compres nada sin leer antes las opiniones de otros clientes.
items.en: Don't buy anything without first reading other customers' reviews.
items.note: negative imperative

items.hr: Busco una tienda que tenga buena política de devoluciones.
items.en: I'm looking for a shop that has a good returns policy.
items.note: relative clause plus subjunctive, uncertain antecedent

items.hr: Si el producto llega roto, normalmente tienes derecho a devolverlo sin coste.
items.en: If the product arrives broken, you usually have the right to return it at no cost.
items.note: si plus present indicative, real condition

items.hr: El pedido que hice la semana pasada todavía no ha llegado.
items.en: The order I placed last week still hasn't arrived.
items.note: relative que, known antecedent, indicative

items.hr: En cuanto recibas la confirmación, guárdala por si hay algún problema.
items.en: As soon as you receive the confirmation, keep it in case there's a problem.
items.note: en cuanto plus subjunctive

activities.title: Los derechos del consumidor
activities.intro: Practise the negative imperative and relative clauses in the context of online shopping.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Busco una tienda que ___ buena política de devoluciones.'
questions.explanation: the antecedent tienda is uncertain, so the relative clause needs the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'devolver un producto'?
options: mandarlo de vuelta a la tienda
questions.answer: mandarlo de vuelta a la tienda
questions.explanation: devolver means to send something back.

questions.prompt: No ___ (comprar, tú) nada sin leer antes las opiniones.
questions.explanation: negative imperative tú, present subjunctive form.

questions.prompt: En cuanto ___ (recibir, tú) la confirmación, guárdala.
questions.explanation: en cuanto plus subjunctive for a future event.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'If the product arrives broken, you have the right to return it.'
questions.explanation: a real condition with si plus present indicative.

activities.title: Una compra por internet
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Discuss an online purchase, exercising the negative imperative and relative clauses.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Al final compraste las botas por internet?
lines.en: Did you end up buying the boots online?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, busqué una tienda que tenía buena política de devoluciones, y al final encontré una.
lines.en: Yes, I looked for a shop that had a good returns policy, and in the end I found one.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bien hecho. Nunca compres en un sitio sin comprobar antes las valoraciones.
lines.en: Good move. Never buy from a site without checking the ratings first.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ya lo sé, por eso miré varias antes de decidirme. El pedido lo hice la semana pasada y aún no ha llegado.
lines.en: I know, that's why I checked several before deciding. I placed the order last week and it still hasn't arrived.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No te preocupes, si llega roto o algo falla, normalmente tienes derecho a devolverlo sin coste.
lines.en: Don't worry, if it arrives broken or something's wrong, you usually have the right to return it at no cost.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Eso espero. Ya guardé la confirmación que me llegó nada más pagar, por si surge algún problema.
lines.en: I hope so. I already saved the confirmation that arrived right after I paid, just in case there's a problem.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Muy bien. Siempre es mejor tener todo apuntado.
lines.en: Very good. It's always better to have everything written down.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Totalmente, así no hay discusión si algo sale mal.
lines.en: Totally, that way there's no argument if something goes wrong.

days.title: La familia y las relaciones hoy
days.objective: Discuss family and relationships, expressing feelings about family news and touching on how family structures are changing today.
days.paretoFocus: Family is core ámbito personal vocabulary, and reacting to family news recycles emotion clauses with the subjunctive.
drills: Describe, in Spanish, one way families today differ from your grandparents' generation.
Write two sentences with me alegra que and me preocupa que.
Practise reporting a piece of family news someone told you.

items: Why does a verb of emotion need two different subjects to trigger the subjunctive?
How do you report what someone said in the past, with the tense shift?
Name one comparative structure for equality.

activities.title: La familia hoy
activities.intro: Family topics recycle emotion clauses with the subjunctive and the tense shift in reported speech, both taught earlier, inside a new topic.

items.hr: Me alegra que mi hermana esté tan decidida a volver a estudiar este año.
items.en: I'm glad my sister is so determined to go back to studying this year.
items.note: emotion plus subjunctive

items.hr: Hoy en día muchas familias tienen una estructura distinta a la tradicional.
items.en: Nowadays many families have a structure different from the traditional one.
items.note: vocabulary, comparison with distinta a

items.hr: Mis padres me dijeron que la cena familiar era importante para ellos.
items.en: My parents told me the family dinner was important to them.
items.note: reported speech, tense shift

items.hr: Me preocupa que mis abuelos vivan tan lejos de nosotros.
items.en: It worries me that my grandparents live so far from us.
items.note: emotion plus subjunctive

items.hr: Cada generación tiene una forma distinta de entender la familia.
items.en: Each generation has a different way of understanding family.
items.note: vocabulary

activities.title: Sentimientos sobre la familia
activities.intro: Practise emotion clauses with the subjunctive and reported speech about family.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Me alegra que mi hermana ___ volver a estudiar.'
questions.explanation: verbs of emotion with two different subjects need the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'una familia numerosa'?
options: una familia con un solo hijo
questions.explanation: numerosa means large in number.

questions.prompt: Me preocupa que mis abuelos ___ (vivir) tan lejos de nosotros.
questions.explanation: me preocupa que triggers the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Mis padres me dijeron que la cena familiar ___ (ser) importante para ellos.
questions.explanation: reported speech: present becomes imperfect in the past.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Each generation has a different way of understanding family.'
questions.explanation: simple present indicative describing a general truth.

activities.title: Noticias de familia
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about family news, exercising emotion clauses with the subjunctive.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Sabes algo de tu hermana últimamente?
lines.en: Do you know anything about your sister lately?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, me alegra mucho que al final se anime a volver a las clases.
lines.en: Yes, I'm really glad she's finally getting motivated to go back to classes.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Qué buena noticia! ¿Y tus abuelos, cómo están?
lines.en: What great news! And your grandparents, how are they?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bien, aunque no me hace gracia que estén siempre tan lejos de todos nosotros.
lines.en: Good, though I'm not thrilled that they're always so far from all of us.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Es normal, al final cada generación vive la familia a su manera.
lines.en: That's normal, in the end every generation experiences family in its own way.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Totalmente, en mi casa pasa igual: mis padres siempre decían que reunirse a cenar unía mucho a la familia.
lines.en: Totally, it's the same in my house: my parents always used to say that getting together for dinner brought the family closer.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Para los míos también, aunque ahora la hacemos menos a menudo.
lines.en: For mine too, although now we do it less often.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Nosotros intentamos mantenerla, aunque sea solo los domingos.
lines.en: We try to keep it up, even if it's only on Sundays.

days.title: Las generaciones y una población que cambia
days.objective: Describe demographic change and generational differences using comparatives and superlatives.
days.paretoFocus: Discussing demographic trends is common in B1 reading texts and lets you recycle A2 comparatives and superlatives inside genuinely B1 content.
drills: Write two sentences comparing your generation to your grandparents'.
Describe one demographic trend using cada vez más or cada vez menos.
Practise a superlative about a place you know.

items: How do you form a superlative like 'the oldest'?
What does 'cada vez más' mean?
Name the future tense used for a prediction about tomorrow.

activities.title: Una población que cambia
activities.intro: Demographic change recycles comparatives, superlatives and the future of prediction, all taught earlier, inside genuinely B1 content.

items.hr: La población está envejeciendo, cada vez hay menos jóvenes que mayores.
items.en: The population is aging, with fewer and fewer young people compared to older people.
items.note: estar plus gerundio, cada vez menos

items.hr: Mi generación es mucho más digital que la de mis padres.
items.en: My generation is much more digital than my parents'.
items.note: comparative of superiority

items.hr: Este es probablemente el barrio más envejecido de la ciudad.
items.en: This is probably the most aged neighbourhood in the city.
items.note: superlative

items.hr: Dentro de unas décadas, habrá muchas más personas mayores de ochenta años, según las previsiones.
items.en: In a few decades, there will be many more people over eighty, according to the forecasts.
items.note: future for a prediction

items.hr: Cuanta más gente mayor vive sola, más necesarios son los servicios de apoyo.
items.en: The more elderly people live alone, the more necessary support services are.
items.note: cuanto más... más = the more... the more, a correlative structure linking two increasing quantities

activities.title: Cambios de población
activities.intro: Practise comparatives, superlatives and the future in the context of demographic change.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Mi generación es mucho ___ digital que la de mis padres.'
questions.explanation: más...que forms the comparative of superiority.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'envejecer'?
questions.explanation: envejecer means to grow older.

questions.prompt: Este es probablemente el barrio más ___ (envejecer) de la ciudad.
questions.explanation: superlative with a past participle used as an adjective.

questions.prompt: Dentro de veinte años ___ (haber) más de dos millones de personas mayores de ochenta años, según las previsiones.
questions.explanation: future simple of haber for a prediction.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The population is aging, there are fewer and fewer young people.'
questions.explanation: estar plus gerundio for a process in progress.

activities.title: El envejecimiento de la población
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Discuss demographic change, exercising comparatives and the future of prediction.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has leído algo sobre el envejecimiento de la población?
lines.en: Have you read anything about the aging of the population?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, en mi zona ya hay claramente menos gente joven que mayor.
lines.en: Yes, in my area there's now clearly fewer young people than older people.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Se nota mucho en mi barrio, la verdad.
lines.en: It really shows in my neighbourhood, honestly.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Este debe de ser uno de los barrios con más población mayor de toda la ciudad.
lines.en: This must be one of the neighbourhoods with the most elderly population in the whole city.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y qué se puede hacer?
lines.en: And what can be done?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Habrá que crear más servicios de apoyo para la gente mayor que vive sola.
lines.en: There will need to be more support services created for elderly people who live alone.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tienes razón, además nosotros hemos crecido con la tecnología mucho más que ellos.
lines.en: You're right, plus we've grown up with technology much more than they have.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, por eso también hace falta enseñarles a usar la tecnología.
lines.en: Yes, that's also why we need to teach them to use technology.

days.title: La migración y vivir en otro país
days.objective: Talk about migration and living abroad, expressing adaptation and hopes using purpose clauses and governed prepositions.
days.paretoFocus: Migration is one of the DELE's ámbito público themes, and adapting to a new country recycles purpose clauses and the prepositions verbs govern.
drills: Describe, in Spanish, one challenge of moving to a new country.
Write a sentence with acostumbrarse a.
Practise para que with a sentence about helping someone settle in.

items: What preposition does acostumbrarse take?
When is para que followed by the subjunctive?
Name the periphrasis for 'to start doing something'.

activities.title: Vivir en otro país
activities.intro: Migration recycles governed prepositions, purpose clauses and periphrases, all taught earlier, inside a new topic.

items.hr: Cuesta acostumbrarse a otro idioma y otras costumbres al principio.
items.en: It's hard to get used to another language and other customs at first.
items.note: acostumbrarse a, governed preposition

items.hr: Muchas familias emigran para que sus hijos tengan más oportunidades.
items.en: Many families emigrate so that their children have more opportunities.
items.note: para que plus subjunctive

items.hr: Al llegar, empecé a aprender el idioma desde el primer día.

items.note: value judgement plus subjunctive

items.note: impersonal uno, adaptarse a

activities.title: Adaptarse a un nuevo país
activities.intro: Practise governed prepositions and purpose clauses in the context of migration.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Muchas familias emigran para que sus hijos ___ más oportunidades.'
questions.explanation: para que always takes the subjunctive.

questions.explanation: pretérito indefinido, empezar a periphrasis.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'It's normal that at first you miss home cooking.'

activities.title: Adaptarse a un nuevo país
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Discuss moving abroad, exercising governed prepositions and purpose clauses.

lines.speaker: Partner

lines.en: How's the adaptation to your new country going?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Al principio no fue nada fácil acostumbrarme a las costumbres de aquí, la verdad.
lines.en: At first it really wasn't easy for me to get used to the customs here, honestly.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Me imagino. ¿Y por qué decidiste emigrar?
lines.en: I can imagine. And why did you decide to emigrate?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En nuestro caso, emigramos sobre todo para que los niños crecieran con más posibilidades.
lines.en: In our case, we emigrated mainly so that the kids would grow up with more opportunities.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tiene sentido. ¿Echas de menos algo de casa?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, al principio es normal que una eche de menos hasta las cosas más tontas de casa.
lines.en: Yes, at first it's normal to miss even the silliest little things from home.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Seguro que con el tiempo te acostumbras a todo.
lines.en: I'm sure that with time you'll get used to everything.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Eso espero. De hecho, empecé a estudiar el idioma nada más llegar, sin esperar ni un día.

days.title: La vida cívica y cómo se organiza una sociedad
days.objective: Describe, in general terms, how civic participation works in a society: voting, contacting local administration, rights and duties, without referring to any real institution.
days.paretoFocus: Civic vocabulary appears in B1 reading about public life, and this lesson recycles impersonal se and present-subjunctive value judgements in a genuinely new topic, without claiming to prepare any citizenship exam.
drills: List four generic civic vocabulary words: el gobierno, el voto, los derechos, los deberes.
Write a sentence with se vota or se elige.
Describe, in Spanish, one way you might get involved in your neighbourhood.

items: What is impersonal se used for?
Name one right and one duty a resident might generally have.
What preposition follows participar?

activities.title: La vida cívica
activities.intro: This lesson uses only generic civic vocabulary (government, town hall, elections, rights, duties) and recycles impersonal se and value-judgement subjunctive. It names no real institution, quotes no legal text and does not prepare any citizenship exam.

items.hr: En unas elecciones, se vota para elegir a quienes van a gobernar.

items.note: generic vocabulary

activities.title: Participar en la sociedad
activities.intro: Practise impersonal se and value-judgement subjunctive with generic civic vocabulary.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Es importante que la gente ___ en la vida de su barrio.'

days.title: La igualdad y las cuestiones sociales
days.objective: Discuss equality and social issues, expressing judgements about fairness using the subjunctive.
days.paretoFocus: Social issues are a common opinion-essay theme on the B1 exam, and reacting to unfairness recycles value-judgement subjunctive with new, more abstract vocabulary.
drills: Write two sentences with es injusto que and es justo que.
Describe one social issue you care about, in Spanish.
Practise lo que with a value judgement.

items: What structure does es injusto que require?
What does 'lo que' refer to?
Name a discourse connector meaning 'however'.

activities.title: Igualdad y sociedad
activities.intro: Social issues recycle value-judgement subjunctive, lo que and discourse connectors, all taught earlier, with more abstract vocabulary.

items.hr: Es injusto que dos personas con el mismo trabajo cobren distinto sueldo.
items.en: It's unfair for two people with the same job to earn different pay.
items.note: value judgement plus subjunctive

items.hr: Lo que más me preocupa es la desigualdad entre barrios de la misma ciudad.

items.note: lo que

items.hr: Cada vez se habla más de la igualdad de oportunidades.
items.en: People talk more and more about equality of opportunity.
items.note: impersonal se, cada vez más

items.hr: Sin embargo, todavía queda mucho camino por recorrer.
items.en: However, there is still a long way to go.
items.note: discourse connector sin embargo

items.hr: Es fundamental que todos tengan acceso a la misma educación.
items.en: It's fundamental that everyone has access to the same education.
items.note: value judgement plus subjunctive

activities.title: Hablar de igualdad

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Es injusto que dos personas con el mismo trabajo ___ distinto sueldo.'

activities.title: Hablando de igualdad

lines.speaker: Partner

lines.speaker: Me

lines.en: Exactly, that's where everything starts.

days.title: La cultura: libros, cine y música
days.objective: Talk about books, film and music using invented cultural figures and works, giving opinions about them.
days.paretoFocus: Culture is a rich B1 opinion topic, and reviewing a book, film or song recycles relative clauses and opinion verbs over content that must stay entirely invented.
drills: Invent a one-sentence description of a book, using a relative clause.
Write an opinion about an invented film using creo que or no creo que.
Describe an invented song in two sentences.

items: How do you introduce an opinion you doubt, with the subjunctive?
What does a relative clause with an indicative verb tell you about its antecedent?
Name a connector for adding an extra point.

activities.title: Libros, cine y música
activities.intro: Meet three entirely invented cultural figures: the novelist Beatriz Solano, the film director Rodrigo Nieva and the singer Marta Solís. Use them to recycle relative clauses and opinion verbs.

items.hr: Beatriz Solano es la autora que escribió 'El mapa de las ausencias'.

items.note: no creo que plus subjunctive

activities.title: Opiniones sobre cultura

days.title: Fiestas y tradiciones en España
days.objective: Describe festivals and traditions in Spain using real geography and generic customs, without naming real people or organisations.
days.paretoFocus: Festival description is a classic B1 reading and speaking topic and recycles impersonal se and habitual time clauses over genuinely regional content.
drills: Describe one festival tradition using se plus a verb.
Write a sentence about when a festival happens with cuando.
List three words related to local festivals.

items: How does impersonal se work in describing a custom?
What structure introduces a habitual time clause with cuando?
Name one word for a traditional local celebration.

activities.title: Fiestas españolas
activities.intro: Festivals recycle impersonal se and the habitual cuando plus present indicative, both taught earlier, over real Spanish geography and generic customs.

items.hr: En muchos pueblos de España se celebran fiestas patronales en verano.
items.en: In many Spanish villages, patron saint festivals are celebrated in summer.
items.note: passive se

items.hr: Cuando llega la primavera, en algunas regiones se preparan hogueras y desfiles.
items.en: When spring arrives, in some regions bonfires and parades are prepared.
items.note: cuando plus present indicative, habitual

items.hr: En las fiestas de mi pueblo se suele comer al aire libre con toda la familia.
items.en: At my village's festivals, people usually eat outdoors with the whole family.
items.note: soler periphrasis

items.hr: Cada región de España tiene sus propias tradiciones y su propio calendario festivo.
items.en: Every region of Spain has its own traditions and its own festival calendar.
items.note: vocabulary

items.hr: Durante estas fiestas, los vecinos se disfrazan y participan en el desfile.
items.en: During these festivals, neighbours dress up and take part in the parade.
items.note: reflexive verb, generic

activities.title: Costumbres y fiestas
activities.intro: Practise impersonal se and habitual cuando in the context of Spanish festivals.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'En muchos pueblos ___ fiestas patronales en verano.'
questions.explanation: passive se agrees in the plural with fiestas.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué es 'un desfile'?

questions.answer: un grupo de personas que caminan juntas en una celebración
questions.explanation: un desfile is a parade.

questions.prompt: Cuando llega la primavera, en algunas regiones se ___ (preparar) hogueras.
questions.explanation: cuando plus present indicative for a habitual event.

questions.explanation: soler plus infinitive expresses a habit.

questions.explanation: simple present indicative stating a general fact.

activities.title: Fiestas del pueblo
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk about local festivals, exercising impersonal se and habitual cuando.

days.title: El español en el mundo
days.objective: Understand the main lexical and grammatical differences between peninsular and American Spanish, and state clearly what this course teaches and why.
days.paretoFocus: Every DELE B1 listening and reading text may come from any Spanish-speaking country, so recognising these pairs without judging either as wrong is essential exam and real-world skill.
drills: Write three contrastive pairs from memory, peninsular and American.
Say one sentence with vosotros and its ustedes equivalent.
Explain, in Spanish, why this course teaches the peninsular form for production.

items: Which pronoun does Spain use for informal plural 'you', and which does America use for both formal and informal?
Name three lexical pairs: coche/carro, and two more.
What perfect tense does Spain use for 'today', and what does most of America use instead?

activities.title: Variedades del español
activities.intro: Neither the peninsular nor the American form is ever wrong; they are different, equally correct varieties. This course teaches the peninsular form for production, because that is the exam's own rule, but every variety must be understood.

items.hr: En España se dice 'coche' y 'conducir'; en gran parte de América, 'carro' y 'manejar'.
items.en: In Spain people say 'coche' and 'conducir'; in much of America, 'carro' and 'manejar'.
items.note: neither form is wrong, both are correct Spanish

items.hr: En España usamos 'el ordenador' y 'el móvil'; en América, 'la computadora' y 'el celular'.
items.en: In Spain we use 'el ordenador' and 'el móvil'; in America, 'la computadora' and 'el celular'.
items.note: lexical variety

items.hr: Una 'patata' en España es una 'papa' en la mayoría de América; un 'zumo' allí es un 'jugo'.
items.en: A 'patata' in Spain is a 'papa' in most of America; a 'zumo' there is a 'jugo'.
items.note: lexical variety

items.hr: En España decimos 'vosotros coméis'; en América, siempre 'ustedes comen'.
items.en: In Spain we say 'vosotros coméis'; in America, always 'ustedes comen'.
items.note: grammatical variety, four second persons against three

items.hr: Hoy he comido en casa, decimos en España; hoy comí en casa, dice gran parte de América.
items.en: 'Hoy he comido en casa' is what we say in Spain; 'hoy comí en casa' is what much of America says.
items.note: the peninsular perfect against the American preference for the indefinido

activities.title: Peninsular o americano
activities.intro: Practise recognising peninsular and American forms as equally valid pairs.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma peninsular para el vehículo que en gran parte de América se llama 'el carro'?
questions.explanation: el coche is the Spanish peninsular term for the car.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué palabra usa gran parte de América para lo que en España se llama 'el coche'?
questions.explanation: el carro is the common American term for the car.

questions.prompt: Nombra el aparato que usas para trabajar y navegar por internet (cualquier variedad del español).
questions.explanation: Both ordenador (Spain) and computadora (much of America) are correct; either is accepted.

questions.prompt: Nombra el aparato que llevas en el bolsillo para llamar y navegar (cualquier variedad del español).
questions.explanation: Both móvil (Spain) and celular (much of America) are correct; either is accepted.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'A patata in Spain is a papa in most of America.'
questions.explanation: a simple present-tense statement pairing the two forms.

activities.title: Las variedades del español
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend just got back from visiting family in Latin America and picked up some new words there; work out together which ones are simply the other side of the Atlantic saying the same thing.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Es verdad que en América dicen 'carro' en vez de 'coche'?
lines.en: Is it true that in America they say 'carro' instead of 'coche'?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, y también 'manejar' en vez de 'conducir'. Ninguna forma es incorrecta, son variedades distintas.
lines.en: Yes, and also 'manejar' instead of 'conducir'. Neither form is incorrect, they're different varieties.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y qué pasa con 'ordenador' y 'móvil'?
lines.en: And what about 'ordenador' and 'móvil'?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En América se dice 'computadora' y 'celular'; aquí en España usamos 'ordenador' y 'móvil'.
lines.en: In America they say 'computadora' and 'celular'; here in Spain we use 'ordenador' and 'móvil'.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Este curso enseña las dos formas para hablar?
lines.en: Does this course teach both forms for speaking?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Enseña la forma peninsular para producir, pero tú tienes que entender todas las variedades.
lines.en: It teaches the peninsular form for production, but you have to understand every variety.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tiene sentido. ¿Y con 'vosotros'?
lines.en: That makes sense. And with 'vosotros'?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En España decimos 'vosotros coméis'; en América siempre dicen 'ustedes comen', y las dos son correctas.
lines.en: In Spain we say 'vosotros coméis'; in America they always say 'ustedes comen', and both are correct.

days.title: Describir una fotografía
days.objective: Describe a photograph in detail, describing people, setting and possible situations, using ser and estar together with location language.
days.paretoFocus: Describing an image aloud is one of this course's speaking-task formats, and it forces natural use of ser/estar and location language together.
drills: Describe an imagined photo of a street scene in three sentences.
Practise one sentence with están plus a gerund for an ongoing action in a photo.
Guess, in Spanish, what might happen next in an invented photo.

items: How do you say what's happening right now in a photo, using estar?
What's the difference between ser and estar with an adjective like 'aburrido'?
Name two location expressions, such as al fondo or en primer plano.

activities.title: Describir una foto
activities.intro: Describing a photograph recycles estar plus gerundio and the ser/estar contrast, both taught earlier, in a new speaking-task format: describe what you see and guess at the situation.

items.hr: En primer plano se ve a una mujer que está leyendo un periódico.
items.en: In the foreground you can see a woman who is reading a newspaper.
items.note: impersonal se, estar plus gerundio

items.hr: Al fondo de la imagen hay varios edificios altos.
items.en: In the background of the image there are several tall buildings.
items.note: location vocabulary

items.hr: Parece que están celebrando algo, quizá un cumpleaños.
items.en: It looks like they're celebrating something, maybe a birthday.
items.note: estar plus gerundio, plus quizá

items.hr: La chica de la izquierda está contenta, mientras que el chico de la derecha parece aburrido.
items.en: The girl on the left is happy, while the boy on the right looks bored.
items.note: estar plus adjective for the state she is in right now

items.hr: Es probable que la fotografía sea de verano, por la ropa que llevan.
