items.en: The photo is probably from summer, judging by the clothes they're wearing.
items.note: probability plus present subjunctive

activities.title: Lo que se ve en la foto
activities.intro: Practise estar plus gerundio and ser/estar in the context of describing a photograph.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'En primer plano se ve a una mujer que ___ leyendo un periódico.'
questions.explanation: estar plus gerundio for an action in progress.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'al fondo de la imagen'?
options: en la parte de atrás de la foto
en el centro de la foto
questions.answer: en la parte de atrás de la foto
questions.explanation: al fondo means in the background.

questions.prompt: La chica de la izquierda ___ (estar) contenta.
questions.explanation: estar for the emotional state she is in, what she IS would take ser.

questions.prompt: El chico de la derecha ___ (parecer) un poco aburrido.
questions.explanation: parecer plus adjective, a guess about appearance.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'In the background of the image there are several tall buildings.'
questions.explanation: hay for existence, plus location language.

activities.title: Describiendo una foto
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Describe an imagined photograph, exercising estar plus gerundio and ser/estar.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Puedes describirme esta foto?
lines.en: Can you describe this photo to me?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro. En primer plano se ve a una mujer que está leyendo un periódico.
lines.en: Sure. In the foreground you can see a woman who is reading a newspaper.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y qué hay al fondo?
lines.en: And what's in the background?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Al fondo de la imagen hay varios edificios altos, parece una ciudad grande.
lines.en: In the background of the image there are several tall buildings, it looks like a big city.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Hay más gente en la foto?
lines.en: Are there more people in the photo?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, un grupo que parece que está celebrando algo, quizá un cumpleaños.
lines.en: Yes, a group that looks like it's celebrating something, maybe a birthday.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo se ven las personas?
lines.en: How do the people look?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: La chica de la izquierda está contenta, mientras que el chico de la derecha parece aburrido.
lines.en: The girl on the left is happy, while the boy on the right looks bored.

days.title: Dar una breve presentación preparada
days.objective: Give a short prepared presentation on a familiar topic, structuring it clearly with discourse connectors.
days.paretoFocus: A structured short talk is one of this course's speaking-task formats, and organising it explicitly recycles discourse connectors in a genuinely productive skill.
drills: Plan a one-minute talk about a hobby, with an intro, two points and a conclusion.
Write three connectors you'd use to structure a talk.
Practise saying 'en primer lugar... por último' aloud.

items: Name a connector for starting a list of points.
What phrase signals you're finishing a talk?
How do you say 'on the one hand... on the other hand'?

activities.title: Estructurar una presentación
activities.intro: A prepared talk recycles discourse connectors, taught earlier, now used to build a whole structured mini-speech from opening to close.

items.hr: En primer lugar, me gustaría hablar de por qué elegí este tema.
items.en: First of all, I'd like to talk about why I chose this topic.
items.note: opening connector

items.hr: Por un lado, es un tema que me interesa desde hace años; por otro lado, es muy actual.
items.en: On the one hand, it's a topic I've been interested in for years; on the other hand, it's very current.
items.note: por un lado, por otro lado

items.hr: Además, quiero dar un par de ejemplos concretos.
items.en: Besides, I want to give a couple of concrete examples.
items.note: connector además

items.hr: En resumen, creo que este tema merece más atención de la que recibe.
items.en: In summary, I think this topic deserves more attention than it gets.
items.note: connector en resumen

items.hr: Por último, me gustaría agradecer vuestra atención.
items.en: Finally, I'd like to thank you all for your attention.
items.note: closing connector, vosotros possessive

activities.title: Organizar un discurso
activities.intro: Practise the discourse connectors that structure a short prepared talk.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué conector usarías para empezar una presentación?
questions.explanation: En primer lugar opens a structured talk.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué conector se usa para cerrar una presentación?
questions.explanation: Por último signals the closing point.

questions.prompt: ___ un lado, es un tema que me interesa desde hace años.
questions.explanation: por un lado begins a two-part contrast.

questions.prompt: En resumen, creo que este tema merece más ___ de la que recibe.
questions.explanation: vocabulary: atención, attention.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Finally, I'd like to thank you all for your attention.'
questions.explanation: me gustaría plus infinitive, a polite closing.

activities.title: Preparando el discurso
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Plan a short presentation aloud, exercising the structuring connectors.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo vas a empezar tu presentación?
lines.en: How are you going to start your presentation?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En primer lugar, me gustaría hablar de por qué elegí este tema.
lines.en: First of all, I'd like to talk about why I chose this topic.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y después qué harás?
lines.en: And what will you do after that?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Por un lado, hablaré de mi experiencia; por otro lado, daré datos generales.
lines.en: On the one hand, I'll talk about my experience; on the other hand, I'll give general data.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buena estructura. ¿Vas a dar ejemplos?
lines.en: Good structure. Are you going to give examples?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, además quiero dar un par de ejemplos concretos.
lines.en: Yes, besides I want to give a couple of concrete examples.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cómo la vas a terminar?
lines.en: And how are you going to end it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En resumen, diré que el tema merece más atención, y por último agradeceré vuestra atención.
lines.en: In summary, I'll say the topic deserves more attention, and finally I'll thank you all for your attention.

days.title: Conversar sobre tu propia presentación
days.objective: Answer follow-up questions about your own presentation naturally, clarifying and expanding on points.
days.paretoFocus: Handling unscripted follow-up questions is the second speaking-task format in this course, and it recycles the pluscuamperfecto and clarifying phrases under real conversational pressure.
drills: Prepare two follow-up questions someone might ask about your last talk.
Practise answering with 'lo que quería decir es que...'.
Write one clarifying sentence starting with 'en otras palabras'.

items: What does the pluscuamperfecto express, an event before which other past moment?
What phrase helps you clarify or rephrase a point?
Name a way to ask for more detail politely.

activities.title: Responder preguntas
activities.intro: Answering follow-up questions recycles the pluscuamperfecto and conditional politeness, both taught earlier, in a new conversational format.

items.hr: Lo que quería decir es que el tema me afecta directamente.
items.en: What I meant to say is that the topic affects me directly.
items.note: clarifying phrase

items.hr: En otras palabras, creo que el problema es más grave de lo que parece.
items.en: In other words, I think the problem is more serious than it seems.
items.note: clarifying connector

items.hr: ¿Podrías explicar un poco más ese punto?
items.en: Could you explain that point a bit more?
items.note: conditional politeness

items.hr: Buena pregunta, no se me había ocurrido pensarlo desde ese punto de vista.
items.en: Good question, it hadn't occurred to me to think of it from that point of view.
items.note: pluscuamperfecto

items.hr: Me alegra que te haga pensar en ello de otra forma.
items.en: I'm glad it makes you think about it differently.
items.note: emotion plus subjunctive

activities.title: Aclarar y ampliar
activities.intro: Practise the pluscuamperfecto and clarifying phrases in a conversational follow-up.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'No se me ___ ocurrido pensarlo así.'
questions.explanation: pluscuamperfecto for a thought that had not occurred before now.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'en otras palabras'?
questions.explanation: en otras palabras means 'put another way'.

questions.prompt: ¿___ explicar un poco más ese punto?
questions.explanation: conditional simple for a polite request.

questions.prompt: Me alegra que te ___ (hacer) pensar en ello de otra forma.
questions.explanation: me alegra que triggers the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'What I meant to say is that the topic affects me directly.'
questions.explanation: lo que quería decir, a clarifying phrase with the imperfecto.

activities.title: Preguntas sobre mi presentación
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Someone in the audience wants more detail on what you just presented; rephrase your point a different way and back it up with an example.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Por qué elegiste ese tema en concreto?
lines.en: Why did you choose that particular topic?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo que quería decir es que el tema me afecta directamente.
lines.en: What I meant to say is that the topic affects me directly.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Podrías explicar un poco más ese punto?
lines.en: Could you explain that point a bit more?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro. En otras palabras, creo que el problema es más grave de lo que parece.
lines.en: Sure. In other words, I think the problem is more serious than it seems.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Qué interesante, no se me había ocurrido pensarlo desde ese punto de vista.
lines.en: How interesting, it hadn't occurred to me to think of it from that point of view.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me alegra que te haga pensar en ello de otra forma.
lines.en: I'm glad it makes you think about it differently.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Tienes algún ejemplo más para ilustrarlo?
lines.en: Do you have another example to illustrate it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, puedo darte uno muy concreto si quieres.
lines.en: Yes, I can give you a very specific one if you like.

days.title: Situaciones simuladas: quejarse, negociar, pedir un favor
days.objective: Handle simulated situations, complaining, negotiating and asking a favour, using polite conditional forms and subjunctive requests.
days.paretoFocus: This is the fourth speaking-task format in this course, and it forces natural combination of conditional politeness and subjunctive requests under social pressure.
drills: Write a polite complaint using querría or me gustaría.
Practise negotiating a solution with 'lo que podríamos hacer es...'.
Ask a favour politely using ¿te importaría...?

items: What's a polite way to make a request, using querría instead of a blunter form?
How do you ask a favour using te importaría?
Name a phrase for proposing a compromise.

activities.title: Quejarse y negociar
activities.intro: Bluntness that sounds normal in English can land as rude in Spanish: swapping quiero for querría, or a flat imperative for a question with te importaría, is what turns a demand into something a stranger actually wants to help with.

items.hr: Querría hablar con el encargado sobre un problema con mi pedido.
items.en: I would like to speak with the person in charge about a problem with my order.
items.note: querría for a polite request

items.hr: ¿Le importaría cambiarme la mesa? Hay mucho ruido aquí.
items.en: Would you mind changing my table? There's a lot of noise here.
items.note: importaría plus infinitive

items.hr: Lo que podríamos hacer es dividir la diferencia entre los dos.
items.en: What we could do is split the difference between the two of us.
items.note: negotiating phrase

items.hr: Necesito que me devuelvan el dinero, el producto llegó defectuoso.
items.en: I need them to give me my money back, the product arrived defective.
items.note: necesitar que plus subjunctive

items.hr: ¿Te importaría ayudarme con esto? Te lo agradecería mucho.
items.en: Would you mind helping me with this? I'd really appreciate it.
items.note: conditional politeness

activities.title: Pedir con educación
activities.intro: Practise polite conditional requests and subjunctive requests in complaint and favour situations.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta y educada de pedir algo?
options: Necesito hablar con el encargado ahora.
Quiero hablar con el encargado ya.
questions.explanation: querría softens the request politely.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa '¿le importaría...?'
options: una forma educada de pedir algo
questions.answer: una forma educada de pedir algo
questions.explanation: le importaría is a polite way to ask something.

questions.prompt: Necesito que me ___ (devolver, ellos) el dinero.
questions.explanation: necesitar que triggers the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: ¿Te ___ (importar) ayudarme con esto?
questions.explanation: conditional simple for a polite favour.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'What we could do is split the difference between the two of us.'
questions.explanation: podríamos, conditional simple, proposes a compromise.

activities.title: Una reclamación
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Handle a complaint and negotiate a solution, exercising polite conditional requests.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buenas tardes, ¿en qué puedo ayudarle?
lines.en: Good afternoon, how can I help you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Querría hablar con el encargado sobre un problema con mi pedido.
lines.en: I would like to speak with the person in charge about a problem with my order.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Claro, cuénteme qué ha pasado.
lines.en: Of course, tell me what happened.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: El producto llegó defectuoso, necesito que me devuelvan el dinero.
lines.en: The product arrived defective, I need them to give me my money back.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Entiendo. Lo que podríamos hacer es cambiarle el producto por otro.
lines.en: I understand. What we could do is exchange the product for another one.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Preferiría el dinero, si no le importa.
lines.en: I would prefer the money, if you don't mind.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: De acuerdo, ¿le importaría esperar cinco minutos mientras lo gestiono?
lines.en: All right, would you mind waiting five minutes while I sort it out?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ningún problema, se lo agradezco mucho.
lines.en: No problem, I really appreciate it.

days.title: Expresar y defender una opinión
days.objective: Express and defend a personal opinion clearly, contrasting it with an opposing view.
days.paretoFocus: Defending an opinion under mild challenge is a core B1 speaking and writing skill, and it recycles the indicative/subjunctive contrast after opinion verbs.
drills: Write your opinion on a topic using en mi opinión or desde mi punto de vista.
Practise contradicting politely with no creo que.
Give one reason to support your opinion using ya que.

items: What structure follows no creo que?
What structure follows creo que?
Name a connector meaning 'since' or 'because', used to justify an opinion.

activities.title: Defender una opinión
activities.intro: Defending an opinion recycles the indicative/subjunctive contrast after opinion verbs and the concessive aunque, both taught earlier, in a new persuasive context.

items.hr: En mi opinión, deberíamos invertir más en educación pública.
items.en: In my opinion, we should invest more in public education.
items.note: conditional for advice

items.hr: Creo que tiene razón en parte, aunque no estoy del todo de acuerdo.
items.en: I think they're partly right, although I don't fully agree.
items.note: aunque plus indicative, a known fact

items.hr: No creo que exista una solución fácil para este problema.
items.en: I don't think there's an easy solution to this problem.
items.note: no creo que plus subjunctive

items.hr: Defiendo mi postura ya que la he pensado mucho.
items.en: I defend my position since I've thought about it a lot.
items.note: ya que, causal

items.hr: Desde mi punto de vista, el debate merece más tiempo del que se le da.
items.en: From my point of view, the debate deserves more time than it's given.
items.note: comparative structure

activities.title: Opinar con argumentos
activities.intro: Practise the indicative/subjunctive contrast after opinion verbs.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'No creo que ___ una solución fácil.'
questions.explanation: no creo que triggers the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué significa 'defender una postura'?
questions.explanation: defender una postura means to uphold and justify an opinion.

questions.prompt: ___ mi opinión, deberíamos invertir más en educación.
questions.explanation: en mi opinión introduces a personal view.

questions.prompt: Defiendo mi postura ___ la he pensado mucho.
questions.explanation: ya que gives the reason for a position.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I think they're partly right, although I don't fully agree.'
questions.explanation: aunque plus indicative concedes a known fact.

activities.title: Un debate amistoso
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Defend an opinion in a friendly debate, exercising the indicative/subjunctive contrast.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué opinas sobre invertir más en educación pública?
lines.en: What do you think about investing more in public education?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En mi opinión, deberíamos invertir mucho más de lo que se invierte ahora.
lines.en: In my opinion, we should invest a lot more than is invested now.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo no estoy tan seguro, hay otras prioridades.
lines.en: I'm not so sure, there are other priorities.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Creo que tienes razón en parte, aunque no estoy del todo de acuerdo.
lines.en: I think you're partly right, although I don't fully agree.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Por qué defiendes tanto esa postura?
lines.en: Why do you defend that position so much?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: La defiendo ya que la he pensado mucho y he leído bastante sobre el tema.
lines.en: I defend it since I've thought about it a lot and read quite a bit on the topic.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Respeto tu opinión, aunque yo veo el problema de otra forma.
lines.en: I respect your opinion, although I see the problem differently.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Desde mi punto de vista, el debate merece más tiempo del que se le da.
lines.en: From my point of view, the debate deserves more time than it's given.

days.title: Estar de acuerdo y en desacuerdo
days.objective: Agree and disagree politely in conversation, softening disagreement appropriately.
days.paretoFocus: Polite disagreement is essential to natural conversation, and it recycles the concessive aunque and the subjunctive of doubt in a genuinely social skill.
drills: Write a polite disagreement using no estoy muy seguro de que.
Practise agreeing enthusiastically with tienes toda la razón.
Soften a disagreement with aunque plus indicative.

items: How do you soften disagreement politely in Spanish?
What structure follows no estoy seguro de que?
Name a phrase for strong agreement.

activities.title: Acuerdo y desacuerdo
activities.intro: Agreeing and disagreeing politely recycles the pluscuamperfecto, the subjunctive of doubt and the concessive aunque, all taught earlier, in a social context.

items.hr: Tienes toda la razón, no se me había ocurrido pensarlo así.
items.en: You're completely right, it hadn't occurred to me to think of it that way.
items.note: pluscuamperfecto

items.hr: No estoy muy seguro de que eso sea del todo cierto.
items.en: I'm not very sure that's entirely true.
items.note: doubt plus subjunctive

items.hr: Entiendo tu punto, aunque yo lo veo de otra manera.
items.en: I understand your point, although I see it differently.
items.note: aunque plus indicative

items.hr: Estoy totalmente de acuerdo contigo en ese aspecto.
items.en: I completely agree with you on that point.
items.note: agreement phrase

items.hr: Puede que tengas parte de razón, pero no toda.
items.en: You might be partly right, but not entirely.
items.note: puede que plus subjunctive

activities.title: Suavizar el desacuerdo
activities.intro: Practise softened disagreement and the subjunctive of doubt.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'No estoy muy seguro de que eso ___ del todo cierto.'
questions.explanation: no estoy seguro de que triggers the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase expresa acuerdo total?
questions.explanation: expresses full agreement.

questions.prompt: Entiendo tu punto, ___ yo lo veo de otra manera.
questions.explanation: aunque plus indicative softens a disagreement.

questions.prompt: No se me ___ (ocurrir) pensarlo así.
questions.explanation: pluscuamperfecto for a thought that had not occurred before.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'You might be partly right, but not entirely.'
questions.explanation: puede que triggers the subjunctive tengas.

activities.title: De acuerdo, en parte
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Agree and disagree politely, exercising the concessive aunque and the subjunctive of doubt.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Creo que deberíamos cambiar de plan para el viaje.
lines.en: I think we should change the plan for the trip.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tienes toda la razón, no se me había ocurrido pensarlo así.
lines.en: You're completely right, it hadn't occurred to me to think of it that way.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Aunque también podríamos quedarnos con el plan original.
lines.en: Although we could also keep the original plan.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No estoy muy seguro de que eso sea la mejor opción, la verdad.
lines.en: I'm not very sure that's the best option, honestly.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Entiendo tu punto, aunque yo lo veo de otra manera.
lines.en: I understand your point, although I see it differently.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Puede que tengas parte de razón, pero no toda.
lines.en: You might be partly right, but not entirely.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bueno, busquemos un término medio entonces.
lines.en: Well, let's find a middle ground then.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Estoy totalmente de acuerdo contigo en eso.
lines.en: I completely agree with you on that.

days.title: Hacer, aceptar y rechazar sugerencias
days.objective: Make, accept and refuse suggestions politely, using the subjunctive after suggestion verbs.
days.paretoFocus: Suggesting and responding to suggestions is a frequent conversation prompt, and it recycles the subjunctive after sugerir and proponer alongside politeness periphrases.
drills: Write a suggestion using sugiero que or propongo que.
Practise refusing a suggestion politely.
Accept a suggestion enthusiastically using me parece genial.

items: What structure follows sugerir que?
Name a polite way to refuse a suggestion.
What phrase would you use to accept a suggestion enthusiastically?

activities.title: Sugerencias y respuestas
activities.intro: Making and responding to suggestions recycles the subjunctive after verbs like sugerir and proponer, taught earlier, in a fully conversational context.

items.hr: Sugiero que quedemos el sábado en vez del viernes.
items.en: I suggest we meet on Saturday instead of Friday.
items.note: sugerir que plus subjunctive

items.hr: Propongo que hagamos la reunión por videollamada.
items.en: I propose we have the meeting by video call.
items.note: proponer que plus subjunctive

items.hr: Me parece genial esa idea, cuenta conmigo.
items.en: That idea sounds great to me, count me in.
items.note: accepting a suggestion

items.hr: Prefiero no hacerlo así, si no te importa.
items.en: I'd rather not do it that way, if you don't mind.
items.note: polite refusal

items.hr: ¿Qué te parece si probamos otra opción?
items.en: What do you think if we try another option?
items.note: suggestion structure

activities.title: Proponer y responder
activities.intro: Match each prompt with the mood-correct reply, whether that means proposing, accepting or turning something down.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Sugiero que ___ el sábado en vez del viernes.'
questions.explanation: sugerir que triggers the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase rechaza una sugerencia educadamente?
options: Prefiero no hacerlo así, si no te importa.
questions.answer: Prefiero no hacerlo así, si no te importa.
questions.explanation: prefiero no... is a polite refusal.

questions.prompt: Propongo que ___ (hacer, nosotros) la reunión por videollamada.
questions.explanation: proponer que triggers the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué te parece ___ probamos otra opción?
questions.explanation: qué te parece si introduces a suggestion.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'That idea sounds great to me, count me in.'
questions.explanation: parecer plus adjective, an enthusiastic acceptance.

activities.title: Quedando para el sábado
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Make and respond to suggestions, exercising the subjunctive after verbs of suggestion.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sugiero que quedemos el sábado en vez del viernes.
lines.en: I suggest we meet on Saturday instead of Friday.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me parece genial esa idea, cuenta conmigo.
lines.en: That idea sounds great to me, count me in.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Y propongo que hagamos la reunión anterior por videollamada.
lines.en: And I propose we have the earlier meeting by video call.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Prefiero no hacerlo así, si no te importa, prefiero vernos en persona.
lines.en: I'd rather not do it that way, if you don't mind, I'd rather meet in person.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Vale, sin problema. ¿Qué te parece si quedamos en el centro?
lines.en: Okay, no problem. What do you think if we meet downtown?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfecto, me viene muy bien esa zona.
lines.en: Perfect, that area works very well for me.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Genial, entonces quedamos así.
lines.en: Great, then it's settled.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Trato hecho, nos vemos el sábado.
lines.en: Deal, see you on Saturday.

days.title: Hipotetizar dentro del límite B1
days.objective: Hypothesise and speculate within the B1 grammar ceiling, using puede que, a lo mejor, seguramente and quizá, and know that the counterfactual conditional is beyond this course.
days.paretoFocus: Speculating naturally is a constant conversational need, and doing it correctly at B1 means using these adverbs with the right mood, never the pattern that belongs to a later level.
drills: Write three guesses about the future using seguramente, a lo mejor and quizá.
Practise puede que plus present subjunctive with a guess about a friend.
Say, in your own words, what kind of hypothesis this course does not teach yet.

items: Pick two of today's hedging words and explain why one takes the subjunctive and the other doesn't.
What mood follows a lo mejor and seguramente?
What structure does this course use for a real condition with si?

activities.title: Hablar de posibilidades
activities.intro: Four small hedging words split into two camps: some pull the following verb into the subjunctive, others leave it in the indicative. None of them reach for the past-subjunctive-plus-conditional combination native speakers use for pure fantasy, since that pairing sits beyond this course's B1 ceiling.

items.hr: Puede que llueva mañana, así que lleva paraguas por si acaso.
items.en: It might rain tomorrow, so bring an umbrella just in case.
items.note: puede que plus present subjunctive

items.hr: A lo mejor no viene a la cena, últimamente está muy ocupado.
items.en: Maybe he won't come to dinner, he's been very busy lately.
items.note: a lo mejor plus present indicative

items.hr: Seguramente llegaremos tarde con este tráfico.
items.en: We'll surely arrive late with this traffic.
items.note: seguramente plus future indicative

items.hr: Quizá tengas razón, aunque yo lo veo distinto.
items.en: Maybe you're right, although I see it differently.
items.note: quizá plus present subjunctive

items.hr: Quizá no sea buena idea salir tan tarde con este tiempo.
items.en: Maybe it's not a good idea to go out so late in this weather.
items.note: quizá plus present subjunctive

activities.title: Puede que, a lo mejor, quizá
activities.intro: Practise the mood each hedging adverb takes: subjunctive after puede que and quizá, indicative after a lo mejor and seguramente.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es correcta? 'Puede que ___ mañana, así que lleva paraguas.'
questions.explanation: puede que always takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué expresión se usa con el indicativo, no con el subjuntivo?
questions.explanation: a lo mejor is always followed by the indicative.

questions.prompt: Seguramente ___ (llegar, nosotros) tarde con este tráfico.
questions.explanation: seguramente plus future indicative.

questions.prompt: Quizá ___ (tener, tú) razón, aunque yo lo veo distinto.
questions.explanation: quizá plus present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Maybe he won't come to dinner, he's been very busy lately.'
questions.explanation: a lo mejor takes the present indicative viene.

activities.title: Especulando sobre el día
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Weather, a friend's plans and the evening traffic are all up in the air; hedge your bets on each one without committing to anything you can't back up.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Crees que va a llover mañana?
lines.en: Do you think it's going to rain tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Puede que llueva, así que lleva paraguas por si acaso.
lines.en: It might rain, so bring an umbrella just in case.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y crees que vendrá Marcos a la cena?
lines.en: And do you think Marcos will come to dinner?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A lo mejor no viene, últimamente está muy ocupado.
lines.en: Maybe he won't come, he's been very busy lately.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Seguramente llegaremos tarde con este tráfico, por cierto.
lines.en: We'll surely arrive late with this traffic, by the way.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Quizá tengas razón, deberíamos salir ya.
lines.en: Maybe you're right, we should leave now.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Es verdad que este curso no enseña el condicional para imaginar situaciones que no son reales?
lines.en: Is it true that this course doesn't teach the conditional for imagining unreal situations?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Así es, ese condicional existe en español real, pero queda para un nivel posterior.
lines.en: That's right, that conditional exists in real Spanish, but it's for a later level.

days.title: La respuesta informal: correo o foro
days.objective: Write a 100-to-120-word informal email or forum reply that answers every point in a short message, using the right greeting and sign-off.
days.paretoFocus: This is DELE B1 writing task 1 exactly, and examiners score length and point-coverage separately from grammar, so a learner who nails the shape banks marks before a single verb is checked.
drills: Read a two-line message asking about your holiday plans and jot down every point it raises.
Time yourself drafting the full reply within the 100-to-120-word range, then check nothing on your list got left out.
Circle your greeting and your sign-off and check they match the informal register.

items: Recall how to report what someone told you using the past tense shift.
Say a sentence using por lo tanto to link two ideas.
Explain when donde functions as a relative pronoun.

activities.title: El correo informal
activities.intro: DELE B1 writing task 1 asks you to reply to a short input text (a note, an advert, a message) in 100 to 120 words, answering every point it raises. An informal reply opens with a greeting, works through what was asked, asks a question back, and closes with a short sign-off.

items.hr: ¡Hola Diego! ¡Qué alegría tener noticias tuyas!
items.en: Hi Diego! How lovely to hear from you!
items.note: an all-purpose informal opening

items.hr: Me preguntas por mis planes para las vacaciones, así que te cuento.
items.en: You ask me about my holiday plans, so let me tell you.
items.note: signals you are about to answer the point raised

items.hr: Por cierto, ¿vosotros vais a venir a la fiesta?
items.en: By the way, are you all coming to the party?
items.note: vosotros is the everyday peninsular plural you, alongside tú, usted and ustedes

items.hr: Bueno, te dejo, que se me hace tarde. ¡Un abrazo!
items.en: Well, I will leave it there, it is getting late. Hugs!
items.note: a natural informal closing before the sign-off

items.hr: Escribo unas ciento diez palabras, ni menos de cien ni más de ciento veinte.
items.en: I am writing about a hundred and ten words, no fewer than a hundred and no more than a hundred and twenty.
items.note: a self-check worth saying to yourself before you submit

activities.title: Escribir un correo informal
activities.intro: Practise the conventions of an informal reply.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es un saludo informal apropiado para empezar un correo a un amigo?
questions.explanation: The other three openings are formal and would be wrong in a message to a friend.

questions.prompt: En la tarea 1 del DELE B1, ¿cuántas palabras debe tener la respuesta?
questions.explanation: 100 to 120 words is the exact range for writing task 1.

questions.prompt: Bueno, te ___, que se me hace tarde. ¡Un abrazo! (despedirse de alguien de forma informal)
questions.explanation: te dejo is the standard informal way to signal you are about to sign off.

questions.prompt: Le pregunté ___ vivía, porque no me acordaba de la dirección.
questions.explanation: dónde keeps its accent in an indirect question, just as in a direct one.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'By the way, are you all coming to the party?'
questions.explanation: por cierto introduces the afterthought, and vosotros is the peninsular plural you.

activities.title: Preparando la respuesta
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A friend messages about weekend plans; agree on what points to cover in your 100-to-120-word reply.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Oye, ¿leíste el mensaje de Elena? Nos pregunta por el fin de semana.
lines.en: Hey, did you read Elena's message? She's asking us about the weekend.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, quiere saber si vamos a la excursión y qué tiempo va a hacer.
lines.en: Yes, she wants to know if we're going on the trip and what the weather will be like.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Entonces tienes que contestar a esos dos puntos, y no te olvides del saludo.
lines.en: So you have to answer those two points, and don't forget the greeting.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, empiezo con '¡Hola Elena!' y luego le cuento lo del tiempo.
lines.en: Of course, I'll start with 'Hi Elena!' and then tell her about the weather.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Y acuérdate de hacerle una pregunta a ella también, eso también lo piden.
lines.en: And remember to ask her a question too, that's required as well.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, le pregunto si prefiere salir temprano o tarde.
lines.en: Okay, I'll ask her whether she prefers to leave early or late.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perfecto. Y cuenta las palabras antes de enviarlo, que sean como ciento diez.
lines.en: Perfect. And count the words before sending it, make it around a hundred and ten.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Hecho. Lo reviso y lo mando ahora mismo.
lines.en: Done. I'll check it over and send it right now.

days.title: La carta formal de solicitud
days.objective: Write a formal email or letter making a request, using the correct opening, closing and polite forms of address.
days.paretoFocus: Requests to institutions, landlords and employers are a recurring real-life need, and the formal register is exactly what marks a letter as competent rather than rude.
drills: Write three sentences using ¿podría...?, me gustaría and querría.
Draft a five-line formal email requesting information about something.
Underline the formal opening and closing phrases in your draft.

items: Recall how to give a courteous request with the conditional, not with an off-syllabus form.
Say a sentence using an indirect object pronoun combined with a direct one.
Explain when a relative clause needs the subjunctive instead of the indicative.

activities.title: La carta formal
activities.intro: Every word a stranger reads has to sound like it came from someone who respects them: the greeting names a role rather than a person you know, tú and vosotros disappear entirely in favour of usted and ustedes, and a request turns into a question instead of a command.

items.hr: Estimado señor García:
items.en: Dear Mr. García,
items.note: formal opening with surname and colon

items.hr: Le escribo para solicitar información sobre el curso de verano.
items.en: I am writing to request information about the summer course.
items.note: standard formal opening line for a request

items.hr: ¿Podría indicarme el plazo de inscripción?
items.en: Could you tell me the enrolment deadline?
items.note: podría, the polite conditional, is the courteous request form taught in this course

items.hr: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
items.en: I look forward to your reply.
items.note: fixed formal closing phrase before the sign-off

items.hr: Atentamente,
items.en: Yours sincerely,
items.note: formal sign-off, paired with a full name below it

activities.title: Escribir una solicitud formal
activities.intro: Practise the conventions of a formal request.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es un saludo formal correcto para una carta a una empresa?
questions.explanation: The other three openings are too informal for a letter to a company.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué forma es la petición cortés correcta en este curso?
options: Enviarme información, por favor, ya mismo.
questions.explanation: podría is the courteous conditional taught for polite requests; the other options are too abrupt for a formal letter.

questions.prompt: Le escribo para ___ información sobre el piso que anuncian.
questions.explanation: solicitar is the formal verb for making a request in writing.

questions.prompt: Es importante que ___ (usted, enviar) los documentos antes del viernes.
questions.explanation: a value judgement, es importante que, requires the present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I look forward to your reply.'
questions.explanation: quedar a la espera de is the fixed formal phrase for awaiting a reply.

activities.title: Redactando el correo formal
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Draft a formal email to a landlord requesting a repair.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ya le escribiste al casero sobre la calefacción?
lines.en: Did you already write to the landlord about the heating?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Todavía no, pero voy a redactar un correo formal esta tarde.
lines.en: Not yet, but I'm going to draft a formal email this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Empieza con 'Estimado señor Pla' y explica el problema claramente.
lines.en: Start with 'Dear Mr. Pla' and explain the problem clearly.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, le voy a decir que la calefacción no funciona desde el lunes.
lines.en: Yes, I'm going to tell him the heating hasn't worked since Monday.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Y pregúntale cortésmente cuándo puede mandar a alguien a arreglarla.
lines.en: And politely ask him when he can send someone to fix it.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Claro, le escribo: '¿Podría enviar a un técnico esta semana?'
lines.en: Of course, I'll write: 'Could you send a technician this week?'

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Muy bien. Termina con 'Quedo a la espera de su respuesta' y firma.
lines.en: Very good. Finish with 'I look forward to your reply' and sign it.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Perfecto, así lo hago. Atentamente, y mi nombre.
lines.en: Perfect, that's what I'll do. Sincerely, and my name.

days.title: La carta de reclamación
days.objective: Write a formal letter of complaint that states the problem, gives evidence and states what resolution you expect.
days.paretoFocus: Complaint letters follow a predictable shape, fact then problem then a request for a remedy, that once automatic works for landlords, shops, airlines and any formal dispute.
drills: List three facts a complaint letter should state clearly.
Write a short paragraph describing a faulty product using the indefinido.
Add one sentence stating what remedy you expect.

items: Recall the difference between the indefinido and the imperfecto in a short story.
Say a sentence using en caso de que with the present subjunctive.
Explain how passive se changes the verb's agreement.

activities.title: La reclamación
activities.intro: A complaint letter states the fact plainly, describes the problem, and closes by saying what you expect to happen next. It stays formal even when the writer is frustrated.

items.hr: Me pongo en contacto con ustedes para expresar mi disconformidad con...
items.en: I am contacting you to express my dissatisfaction with...
items.note: formal opening for a complaint

items.hr: El pasado martes compré un producto que llegó defectuoso.
items.en: Last Tuesday I bought a product that arrived faulty.
items.note: states the fact using the indefinido

items.hr: Espero que solucionen el problema cuanto antes.
items.en: I hope you will resolve the problem as soon as possible.
items.note: espero que plus present subjunctive, a hope expression already known

items.hr: En caso de que no reciba respuesta, tomaré otras medidas.
items.en: If I do not receive a reply, I will take further action.
items.note: en caso de que plus present subjunctive, within the B1 ceiling

items.hr: Sin otro particular, les saluda atentamente,
items.en: Without further matters to raise, yours sincerely,
items.note: fixed formal closing formula for a complaint

activities.title: Escribir una reclamación
activities.intro: Practise the conventions of a formal complaint.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué expresión abre una carta de reclamación de forma adecuada?
options: Me pongo en contacto con ustedes para expresar mi disconformidad con...
¡Qué rollo, esto no hay quien lo aguante!
questions.answer: Me pongo en contacto con ustedes para expresar mi disconformidad con...
questions.explanation: The other three options are too informal for a formal complaint.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta después de 'en caso de que'?
questions.explanation: en caso de que always takes the present subjunctive at this level.

questions.prompt: El pasado martes ___ (comprar, yo) un producto que llegó defectuoso.
questions.explanation: a single completed action in the past takes the indefinido.

questions.prompt: En esta tienda no ___ (devolver, se) el dinero, solo se cambia el producto.
questions.explanation: passive se agrees with dinero, singular, so the verb stays singular too.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I hope you will resolve the problem as soon as possible.'
questions.explanation: espero que triggers the present subjunctive, solucionen.

activities.title: Redactando la queja
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Draft a complaint letter to an online shop about a broken delivery.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo va la reclamación que ibas a mandar a la tienda online?
lines.en: How's the complaint you were going to send to the online shop coming along?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: La estoy escribiendo. Empiezo explicando que el paquete llegó roto.
lines.en: I'm writing it. I'm starting by explaining that the package arrived broken.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bien, y no olvides poner la fecha exacta de la compra.
lines.en: Good, and don't forget to include the exact date of purchase.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ya la puse: el pasado martes. Ahora explico el problema con detalle.
lines.en: I've already put it: last Tuesday. Now I'm explaining the problem in detail.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y qué solución vas a pedir, el reembolso o un producto nuevo?
lines.en: And what remedy are you going to ask for, a refund or a new product?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Voy a pedir que me cambien el producto por uno en buen estado.
lines.en: I'm going to ask them to replace the product with one in good condition.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buena idea. Termina diciendo que esperas una respuesta pronto.
lines.en: Good idea. Finish by saying you expect a reply soon.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, y cierro con 'sin otro particular, les saluda atentamente'.
lines.en: Yes, and I'll close with 'without further matters to raise, yours sincerely'.

days.title: La redacción de opinión
days.objective: Write a 130-to-150-word composition that reacts to a short news item with description or narration plus a clearly stated personal opinion.
days.paretoFocus: This is DELE B1 writing task 2, where the candidate picks one of two prompts, and the length plus a genuine opinion are exactly what separates a pass from a fail.
drills: Pick a short invented news item and note two facts from it.
Draft the full composition within the 130-to-150-word window, spending roughly half on the news and half on your reaction.
Count your words and check you used at least one discourse connector.

items: Recall three discourse connectors used to structure an argument.
Say a sentence contrasting an advantage and a disadvantage of something.
Explain when acabar de is used instead of a simple past tense.

activities.title: La redacción de opinión
activities.intro: Task 2 hands you two prompts side by side and expects exactly one response, not a blend of both: open by relaying what the item said, then pivot into what you personally think of it.

items.hr: En la tarea 2 se ofrecen dos opciones y solo hay que elegir una.
items.en: In task 2, two options are offered and you only need to choose one.
items.note: fact about the exam format

items.hr: Según la noticia, el ayuntamiento va a construir un carril bici nuevo.
items.en: According to the news item, the town council is going to build a new bike lane.
items.note: describing the news item, first paragraph

items.hr: En mi opinión, esta medida es positiva porque reduce el tráfico.
items.en: In my opinion, this measure is positive because it reduces traffic.
items.note: opinion plus reason, second paragraph

items.hr: Por un lado tiene ventajas, pero por otro lado también genera algún problema.
items.en: On the one hand it has advantages, but on the other hand it also creates some problem.
items.note: reusing the por un lado / por otro connector

items.hr: Esta redacción debe tener entre ciento treinta y ciento cincuenta palabras.
items.en: This composition must have between a hundred and thirty and a hundred and fifty words.
items.note: the length rule stated explicitly

activities.title: Practicar la redacción de opinión
activities.intro: Practise the shape and the length rule for writing task 2.

questions.prompt: En la tarea 2 del DELE B1, ¿cuántas palabras debe tener la redacción?
questions.explanation: 130 to 150 words is the exact range for writing task 2.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuántas opciones se ofrecen en la tarea 2, y cuántas hay que desarrollar?
options: Dos opciones, se elige y desarrolla solo una
Tres opciones, hay que desarrollar las tres
Dos opciones, hay que mezclar las dos
questions.answer: Dos opciones, se elige y desarrolla solo una
questions.explanation: The candidate chooses one of the two options offered and develops only that one.

questions.prompt: ___ la noticia, el ayuntamiento va a construir un carril bici nuevo.
questions.explanation: según introduces the source of the information.

questions.prompt: Acabo ___ leer la noticia sobre el carril bici nuevo.
questions.explanation: acabar de plus infinitive expresses something just completed.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'In my opinion, this measure is positive.'
questions.explanation: en mi opinión is the standard opener for a personal view.

activities.title: Eligiendo la opción
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Decide which of two writing-task-2 prompts to develop and how to structure it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué opción vas a elegir para la redacción, la del carril bici o la otra?
lines.en: Which option are you going to choose for the composition, the bike lane one or the other?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Voy a elegir la del carril bici, tengo más que decir sobre eso.
lines.en: I'm going to choose the bike lane one, I have more to say about it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Bien. Primero cuenta la noticia y luego da tu opinión, ¿no?
lines.en: Good. First you tell the news item and then give your opinion, right?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exacto, primero explico lo que dice la noticia y después opino.
lines.en: Exactly, first I explain what the news item says and then I give my opinion.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cuál es tu opinión, a favor o en contra?
lines.en: And what's your opinion, for or against?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A favor, aunque también menciono algún inconveniente para ser objetivo.
lines.en: In favour, although I also mention some drawback to be objective.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buena estrategia. No olvides las ciento treinta a ciento cincuenta palabras.
lines.en: Good strategy. Don't forget the hundred and thirty to hundred and fifty words.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo sé, ya las estoy contando mientras escribo.
lines.en: I know, I'm already counting them as I write.

days.title: El diario y la anécdota personal
days.objective: Write a diary entry or narrate a personal anecdote using the past tenses together to distinguish background from main events.
days.paretoFocus: A diary entry recycles the whole past system in a register B1 writing task 2 sometimes asks for directly, turning grammar already learned into a genre worth exam marks.
drills: Write four lines of a diary entry mixing indefinido and imperfecto.
Add one sentence using the pluscuamperfecto for something that happened earlier.
Close the entry with a sentence about tomorrow using the present subjunctive.

items: Recall the four past tenses and what each one is for.
Say a sentence reporting what someone told you yesterday.
Explain why aunque can take either the indicative or the subjunctive.

activities.title: Un día cualquiera
activities.intro: A diary entry or anecdote narrates events with the indefinido, describes the background with the imperfecto, and reaches further back with the pluscuamperfecto when needed, all in one short text.

items.hr: Querido diario: hoy ha sido un día raro.
items.en: Dear diary: today has been a strange day.
items.note: classic diary opening, perfecto for a day still open

items.hr: Cuando salí de casa, llovía muchísimo.
items.en: When I left home, it was raining a lot.
items.note: indefinido for the main event, imperfecto for the background

items.hr: No me lo podía creer: había perdido las llaves otra vez.
items.en: I couldn't believe it: I had lost my keys again.
items.note: pluscuamperfecto for the event before the event

items.hr: Al final todo salió bien, aunque el día empezó fatal.
items.en: In the end everything turned out fine, even though the day started terribly.
items.note: aunque with the indicative for a known fact

items.hr: Mañana espero que sea un día más tranquilo.
items.en: Tomorrow I hope it will be a calmer day.
items.note: espero que plus present subjunctive to close the entry

activities.title: Narrar en pasado
activities.intro: Practise choosing the right past tense for background, main events and earlier events.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué tiempo se usa normalmente para el fondo de una anécdota, la descripción de la situación?
questions.explanation: The imperfecto sets the scene: what was happening around the main event.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué tiempo expresa lo que había pasado antes del evento principal?
questions.explanation: The pluscuamperfecto, había plus participle, reaches back to an earlier point in the past.

questions.prompt: Cuando ___ (salir, yo) de casa, llovía muchísimo.
questions.explanation: the main completed event takes the indefinido.

questions.prompt: Me dijo que ___ (estar) muy cansado después del viaje.
questions.explanation: reported speech in the past shifts the present into the imperfecto.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I couldn't believe it.'
questions.explanation: no me lo podía creer is the fixed everyday phrase for disbelief.

activities.title: Un día raro
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Tell a friend about an anecdote you wrote in your diary last week.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Escribes un diario? Cuéntame algo que te pasó la semana pasada.
lines.en: Do you keep a diary? Tell me something that happened to you last week.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, escribo casi todos los días. La semana pasada perdí el autobús.
lines.en: Yes, I write almost every day. Last week I missed the bus.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y qué hiciste? ¿Llegaste tarde al trabajo?
lines.en: And what did you do? Did you get to work late?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Llegué media hora tarde, y encima había olvidado el paraguas en casa.
lines.en: I arrived half an hour late, and on top of that I had left my umbrella at home.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¡Vaya día! ¿Cómo empezaba tu entrada del diario sobre eso?
lines.en: What a day! How did your diary entry about that begin?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Empezaba así: 'Querido diario, hoy ha sido un día raro'.
lines.en: It began like this: 'Dear diary, today has been a strange day'.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Me gusta ese estilo. ¿Y cómo terminó todo al final?
lines.en: I like that style. And how did everything turn out in the end?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Al final todo salió bien, aunque el día empezó fatal.
lines.en: In the end everything turned out fine, even though the day started terribly.

days.title: La biografía
days.objective: Write a short biography of an invented person, sequencing life events with the past tenses and dates.
days.paretoFocus: Biography is one of the DELE B1 reading input genres and a natural writing task 2 option, so producing one fluently pays off on both papers.
drills: Invent a person and note three life events with dates.
Write five sentences narrating their life using at least three past tenses.
Add one sentence about what they still do today.

items: Recall how to combine indefinido and pluscuamperfecto to order two past events.
Say a sentence using desde entonces.
Explain the agreement rule for a past participle used as an adjective.

activities.title: La vida de Lucía Ferreiro
activities.intro: A biography sequences a life with dates and the indefinido for single events, the imperfecto for habits, and the pluscuamperfecto for an even earlier achievement. This lesson invents its subject entirely.

items.hr: Lucía Ferreiro nació en Vigo en mil novecientos setenta y ocho.
items.en: Lucía Ferreiro was born in Vigo in nineteen seventy-eight.
items.note: nació, indefinido for a single completed event

items.hr: De joven, pintaba todos los fines de semana en el puerto.
items.en: As a young woman, she used to paint every weekend at the harbour.
items.note: imperfecto for a habitual past

items.hr: En dos mil tres se trasladó a Bilbao, donde vive desde entonces.
items.en: In two thousand three she moved to Bilbao, where she has lived ever since.
items.note: se trasladó, indefinido, plus donde as a relative

items.hr: Para cuando cumplió treinta años, ya había expuesto en varias galerías.
items.en: By the time she turned thirty, she had already exhibited in several galleries.
items.note: pluscuamperfecto for the earlier achievement

items.hr: Hoy sigue pintando y da clases a jóvenes artistas.
items.en: Today she still paints and teaches young artists.
items.note: seguir plus gerundio, a periphrasis reused from an earlier lesson

activities.title: Escribir una biografía
activities.intro: Practise sequencing an invented life with the right tenses.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué tiempo se usa para dar la fecha exacta de nacimiento de alguien?
questions.explanation: A single dated event, like being born, takes the indefinido.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estas frases es propia de una biografía?
options: Nació en Vigo en 1978 y se trasladó a Bilbao en 2003.
¡Qué rollo, no me cuentes su vida!
Oye, ¿tú sabes dónde nació esa tía?
Nacer aquí, vivir allí, qué más da.
questions.answer: Nació en Vigo en 1978 y se trasladó a Bilbao en 2003.
questions.explanation: The other options are too colloquial for the neutral register of a biography.

questions.prompt: Lucía ___ (nacer) en Vigo en mil novecientos setenta y ocho.
questions.explanation: nacer describes a single completed event, so it takes the indefinido.

questions.prompt: Lucía ___ (llevar) pintando más de veinte años.
questions.explanation: llevar plus gerundio expresses how long an ongoing activity has lasted.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Today she still paints and teaches young artists.'
questions.explanation: seguir plus gerundio expresses an action that continues.

activities.title: Sobre la pintora inventada
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Discuss the invented biography you wrote about a painter.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Has leído la biografía que escribiste sobre esa pintora inventada?
lines.en: Have you read the biography you wrote about that invented painter?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, se llama Lucía Ferreiro y nació en Vigo en 1978.
lines.en: Yes, her name is Lucía Ferreiro and she was born in Vigo in 1978.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y qué hacía de joven, antes de ser conocida?
lines.en: And what did she do as a young woman, before she was well known?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Pintaba todos los fines de semana en el puerto de su ciudad.
lines.en: She used to paint every weekend at her city's harbour.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuándo se trasladó a Bilbao?
lines.en: When did she move to Bilbao?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: En 2003, y desde entonces vive allí y sigue pintando.
lines.en: In 2003, and she's lived there ever since and still paints.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Ya había expuesto en galerías antes de cumplir treinta años?
lines.en: Had she already exhibited in galleries before turning thirty?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, para cuando cumplió treinta ya había expuesto en varias.
lines.en: Yes, by the time she turned thirty she had already exhibited in several.

days.title: La reseña breve
days.objective: Write a short review of a book, film or restaurant giving a brief description and a clear recommendation.
days.paretoFocus: Reviews are compact and formulaic, what it is, what's good or bad, would you recommend it, making them a fast, low-risk genre to have ready for either writing task.
drills: Pick an invented book, film or restaurant.
Write three sentences: what it is, what's good, what's bad.
Close with a recommendation and a rating.

items: Recall a sentence using lo mejor or lo peor.
Say a sentence with a relative clause introduced by a quien.
Explain when a relative clause after an indefinite antecedent needs the subjunctive.

activities.title: Una reseña breve
activities.intro: A short review states what the thing is, weighs its best and worst points, and closes with a clear recommendation and often a rating.

items.hr: Se trata de una novela ambientada en un pueblo de montaña.
items.en: It is a novel set in a mountain village.
items.note: se trata de, the standard way to introduce what something is about

items.hr: Lo mejor es el ritmo de la historia; lo peor, algunos personajes secundarios.
items.en: The best thing is the pace of the story; the worst, some secondary characters.
items.note: lo mejor / lo peor, neuter lo plus adjective

items.hr: En general, recomiendo esta novela a quien le guste el misterio.
items.en: Overall, I recommend this novel to anyone who likes mystery.
items.note: a quien le guste, subjunctive after an indefinite antecedent

items.hr: Le doy cuatro estrellas sobre cinco.
items.en: I give it four stars out of five.
items.note: a fixed formula for rating something

items.hr: En resumen, merece la pena.
items.en: In short, it's worth it.
items.note: en resumen, a discourse connector reused from an earlier lesson

activities.title: Escribir una reseña
activities.intro: Practise the shape of a short review.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué expresión sirve para presentar de qué trata algo?
questions.explanation: se trata de is the standard way to introduce the subject of a review.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué estructura necesita 'a quien le guste el misterio' porque el antecedente no es concreto?
questions.explanation: an unspecified, indefinite person, quien, takes the subjunctive in the relative clause.

questions.prompt: Lo mejor es el ritmo; ___ peor, algunos personajes secundarios.
questions.explanation: lo peor mirrors lo mejor, the neuter article plus adjective.

questions.prompt: En resumen, esta película ___ (merecer) la pena.
questions.explanation: merecer la pena is the fixed phrase for being worth it.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I recommend this novel to anyone who likes mystery.'
questions.explanation: quien plus the subjunctive guste covers any unspecified reader.

activities.title: Comentando una novela
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Recommend or not recommend a book you've just finished.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tal la novela que estabas leyendo? ¿La recomiendas?
lines.en: How was the novel you were reading? Do you recommend it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Se trata de una historia ambientada en un pueblo de montaña, y sí, la recomiendo.
lines.en: It's a story set in a mountain village, and yes, I recommend it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué es lo mejor y lo peor?
lines.en: What's the best and worst thing about it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Lo mejor es el ritmo; lo peor, algún personaje secundario un poco plano.
lines.en: The best thing is the pace; the worst, some secondary character that's a bit flat.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuántas estrellas le das?
lines.en: How many stars do you give it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Le doy cuatro estrellas sobre cinco.
lines.en: I give it four stars out of five.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Se la recomendarías a cualquiera?
lines.en: Would you recommend it to just anyone?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Se la recomiendo a quien le guste el misterio. En resumen, merece la pena.
lines.en: I recommend it to anyone who likes mystery. In short, it's worth it.

days.title: La cohesión en el texto escrito
days.objective: Organise a written text into clear paragraphs, use pronouns and synonyms to avoid repeating the same noun, and link ideas with connectors.
days.paretoFocus: Cohesion is graded directly on both DELE B1 writing tasks, and a text that repeats the same noun five times reads as lower level even when the grammar in it is correct.
drills: Take a paragraph you wrote earlier and circle every repeated noun.
Rewrite it replacing at least two repetitions with a pronoun or synonym.
Split it into two paragraphs by topic.

items: Say one pronoun and one synonym you could use in place of a noun you've already introduced.
Say a sentence using sin embargo to contrast two ideas.
Explain what del que refers back to in a sentence.

activities.title: Cohesión: párrafos, referencia y conectores
activities.intro: A cohesive text groups one idea per paragraph, replaces repeated nouns with pronouns or synonyms, and links ideas with connectors instead of stacking short unconnected sentences.

items.hr: Mi hermano trabaja en un hospital. Él llegó tarde ayer.
items.en: My brother works at a hospital. He arrived late yesterday.
items.note: using él instead of repeating 'mi hermano'

items.hr: Compré una novela; el libro me costó quince euros.
items.en: I bought a novel; the book cost me fifteen euros.
items.note: 'el libro' as a synonym so 'novela' isn't repeated

items.hr: Primero, llegamos tarde. Además, perdimos las entradas.
items.en: First, we arrived late. What's more, we lost the tickets.
items.note: primero and además organise events in sequence

items.hr: Este problema, del que ya hablamos antes, sigue sin resolverse.
items.en: This problem, which we already talked about before, is still unresolved.
items.note: del que refers back without repeating 'el problema'

items.hr: Un párrafo, una idea: cambia de párrafo cuando cambies de tema.
items.en: One paragraph, one idea: start a new paragraph when you change subject.
items.note: the basic paragraphing rule for a B1 composition

activities.title: Practicar la cohesión
activities.intro: Practise avoiding repetition and linking ideas clearly.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estas frases evita mejor la repetición?
options: Compré una novela; el libro me costó quince euros.
Compré una novela; la novela me costó quince euros; la novela era interesante.
Vi una película; la película trataba de una película.
Fui a la tienda; en la tienda había una tienda cerrada.
questions.answer: Compré una novela; el libro me costó quince euros.
questions.explanation: the other options repeat the same noun needlessly.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué conector añade una idea a la anterior?
questions.explanation: además adds a further point; the others contrast or explain.

questions.prompt: Mi hermano trabaja en un hospital. ___ llegó tarde ayer. (pronombre, no repetir 'mi hermano')
questions.explanation: él replaces the noun already introduced in the first sentence.

questions.prompt: Este problema, ___ ya hablamos antes, sigue sin resolverse.
questions.explanation: del que combines the preposition de with the relative que to refer back to el problema.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Start a new paragraph when you change subject.'
questions.explanation: cuando plus the subjunctive cambies gives a general instruction about a future moment.

activities.title: Revisando el borrador
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Get feedback on a draft that repeats a noun too often and fix it.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: He leído tu redacción, pero repites 'el problema' cinco veces.
lines.en: I've read your composition, but you repeat 'the problem' five times.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tienes razón, puedo usar 'este asunto' o simplemente 'él' a veces.
lines.en: You're right, I can use 'this matter' or simply 'it' sometimes.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Además, todo está en un solo párrafo enorme.
lines.en: Also, it's all in one huge paragraph.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Voy a dividirlo: un párrafo para la descripción y otro para mi opinión.
lines.en: I'm going to split it: one paragraph for the description and another for my opinion.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buena idea. ¿Y usas algún conector para unir las ideas?
lines.en: Good idea. And do you use any connector to link the ideas?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, uso 'además' y 'sin embargo' para conectar los párrafos.
lines.en: Yes, I use 'also' and 'however' to connect the paragraphs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perfecto, así queda mucho más cohesionado.
lines.en: Perfect, that makes it much more cohesive.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Gracias, ahora lo reviso y lo corrijo entero.
lines.en: Thanks, now I'll review and correct the whole thing.

days.title: Lectura, tarea 1: relacionar enunciados con textos
days.objective: Apply the matching strategy for DELE B1 reading task 1: scan ten short texts of 40 to 60 words and match each of six people's statements to the text that answers it.
days.paretoFocus: Task 1 is worth six of the thirty reading items, and a fast keyword-scanning strategy on short texts wins time for the longer tasks later in the seventy-minute paper.
drills: Read five short invented notices and match each to one statement.
Time yourself and note how long the matching took.
Identify the key word that led you to each match.

items: Recall the difference between por and para in one example each.
Say a sentence using se to describe something happening without naming who does it.
Explain how to eliminate an obviously wrong option quickly.

activities.title: Textos breves y enunciados
activities.intro: The paper always offers more texts than there are people, so some texts match nobody and part of the skill is leaving them unused without second-guessing yourself. Work outward from the people: take one statement, fix on the single thing it asks for, then hunt for the text that supplies exactly that and discard the near misses.

items.hr: La tarea uno presenta a seis personas y nueve textos breves de cuarenta a sesenta palabras; sobran tres textos.
items.en: Task one presents six people and nine short texts of forty to sixty words; three texts are left over.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Primero lee los enunciados, después busca las palabras clave en cada texto.
items.en: First read the statements, then look for the key words in each text.
items.note: the scanning strategy

items.hr: Los textos suelen ser anuncios, mensajes personales o avisos.
items.en: The texts are usually adverts, personal messages or notices.
items.note: genre range in task 1

items.hr: No hace falta entender cada palabra, solo lo suficiente para relacionar.
items.en: You don't need to understand every word, just enough to match.
items.note: strategic reassurance

items.hr: Descarta primero las opciones claramente incorrectas.
items.en: Rule out the clearly wrong options first.
items.note: process-of-elimination strategy

activities.title: Estrategia de la tarea 1
activities.intro: Practise the reading task 1 strategy and format.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuántas palabras tiene cada texto de la tarea uno de lectura?
questions.explanation: reading task 1 texts are the shortest in the paper, 40 to 60 words each.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la mejor estrategia para empezar la tarea uno?
options: Leer primero los enunciados y luego buscar palabras clave
Leer los seis textos palabra por palabra sin mirar los enunciados
Adivinar las respuestas sin leer nada
questions.answer: Leer primero los enunciados y luego buscar palabras clave
questions.explanation: knowing what you're looking for before you scan saves time.

questions.prompt: Los textos de la tarea uno suelen ser anuncios, mensajes personales o ___.
questions.explanation: avisos, notices, complete the usual genre range for task 1.

questions.prompt: En este anuncio ___ (buscar, se) compañero de piso.
questions.explanation: se busca is the impersonal se used in adverts and notices.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Rule out the clearly wrong options first.'
questions.explanation: descarta gives the instruction, and the adverb claramente modifies incorrectas.

activities.title: Practicando la tarea 1
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk through your approach to reading task 1 before the exam.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo enfocas la tarea uno de lectura en el examen?
lines.en: How do you approach reading task one in the exam?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Leo los seis enunciados primero, antes de mirar los textos.
lines.en: I read the six statements first, before looking at the texts.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y luego qué haces?
lines.en: And then what do you do?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Busco palabras clave en los textos breves para relacionar a cada persona con el suyo.
lines.en: I look for key words in the short texts to match each person to theirs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te preocupa no entender alguna palabra?
lines.en: Are you worried about not understanding some word?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, no hace falta entender todo, solo lo suficiente para emparejar.
lines.en: No, you don't need to understand everything, just enough to match.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuánto tiempo le dedicas a esta tarea?
lines.en: How much time do you spend on this task?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Poco, porque los textos son cortos, de cuarenta a sesenta palabras.
lines.en: Not much, because the texts are short, forty to sixty words.

days.title: Lectura, tarea 2: el texto informativo largo
days.objective: Handle a single 400-to-450-word informative text with three-option multiple choice by reading for the general idea before checking each option against the text.
days.paretoFocus: This task rewards a global first read over word-by-word translation, and the strategy transfers directly to task 2 of the listening paper.
drills: Skim a long invented text once without stopping.
Answer three questions about it, checking the exact text for each.
Note which option resembled the text without matching it exactly.

items: Recall a sentence using por lo tanto to draw a conclusion.
Say a sentence describing a habitual past action with the imperfecto.
Explain why reading a whole text once before answering saves time.

activities.title: El texto informativo largo
activities.intro: One passage carries the full weight of this task, so skimming for the gist before hunting for answers protects you from getting lost in unfamiliar vocabulary. Regional spelling or word choice may show up here, since input is drawn from every variety of Spanish, but it never changes what a question is actually asking.

items.hr: La tarea dos es un solo texto informativo de cuatrocientas a cuatrocientas cincuenta palabras.
items.en: Task two is a single informative text of four hundred to four hundred fifty words.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Cada pregunta tiene tres opciones, y solo una es correcta.
items.en: Each question has three options, and only one is correct.
items.note: format of the task 2 questions

items.hr: Lee el texto entero una vez para entender la idea general.
items.en: Read the whole text once to understand the general idea.
items.note: strategy

items.hr: Después, busca en el texto la parte que corresponde a cada pregunta.
items.en: Then, look in the text for the part that matches each question.
items.note: second-pass strategy

items.hr: Dos opciones suelen parecerse mucho al texto sin decir exactamente lo mismo.
items.en: Two options usually resemble the text closely without saying exactly the same thing.
items.note: warning about distractors

activities.title: Estrategia de la tarea 2
activities.intro: Practise the reading task 2 strategy and format.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuántas opciones tiene cada pregunta en la tarea dos?
questions.explanation: each question in task 2 offers exactly three options, of which one is correct.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la mejor estrategia para empezar un texto largo como el de la tarea dos?
options: Leerlo entero una vez para captar la idea general
Buscar la respuesta antes de leer el texto
questions.answer: Leerlo entero una vez para captar la idea general
questions.explanation: a global first read orients you before you hunt for specific answers.

questions.prompt: El texto de la tarea dos tiene entre cuatrocientas y cuatrocientas ___ palabras.
questions.explanation: the range is 400 to 450 words.

questions.prompt: El texto es largo; ___, conviene leerlo con calma.
questions.explanation: por lo tanto draws a conclusion from the previous statement.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Read the whole text once to understand the general idea.'
questions.explanation: para entender introduces the purpose of the first read.

activities.title: Practicando la tarea 2
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk through your approach to the long informative text.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: La tarea dos siempre me da miedo, el texto es larguísimo.
lines.en: Task two always scares me, the text is really long.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A mí también, pero ayuda leerlo entero primero sin pararte en cada palabra.
lines.en: Me too, but it helps to read it all first without stopping at every word.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y después?
lines.en: And then?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Después busco en el texto la parte que corresponde a cada pregunta.
lines.en: Then I look in the text for the part that matches each question.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Las opciones suelen ser parecidas?
lines.en: Are the options usually similar?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, dos opciones se parecen mucho al texto sin decir lo mismo exactamente.
lines.en: Yes, two options resemble the text closely without saying exactly the same thing.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo distingues la correcta entonces?
lines.en: So how do you tell which is correct?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vuelvo al texto y comparo cada opción con la frase exacta.
lines.en: I go back to the text and compare each option with the exact sentence.

days.title: Lectura, tarea 3: información en tres textos
days.objective: Locate specific information spread across three 100-to-120-word texts and match it to the right one.
days.paretoFocus: This task tests scanning across multiple sources at once, a skill needed whenever a real search turns up several short listings that must be compared.
drills: Read three short invented texts on the same topic.
Decide which text answers each of three questions.
Underline the detail that confirms each match.

items: Recall how a relative clause narrows down which piece of information is meant.
Say a sentence using antes de que with the subjunctive.
Explain the difference between an anecdote and a biography as text types.

activities.title: Información en tres textos
activities.intro: Task three spreads specific information across three texts and asks you to find where each detail lives. Underline what each question is looking for before you read.

items.hr: La tarea tres presenta tres textos de cien a ciento veinte palabras cada uno.
items.en: Task three presents three texts of a hundred to a hundred twenty words each.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Los textos pueden ser anécdotas, biografías, ofertas de trabajo o guías de viaje.
items.en: The texts can be anecdotes, biographies, job adverts or travel guides.
items.note: genre range

items.hr: Cada pregunta corresponde a uno de los tres textos, nunca a los tres a la vez.
items.en: Each question corresponds to one of the three texts, never to all three at once.
items.note: format clarification

items.hr: Subraya el nombre o el dato que busca cada pregunta antes de leer.
items.en: Underline the name or the detail each question is looking for before reading.
items.note: strategy

items.hr: Compara los tres textos solo cuando dos parezcan encajar con la misma pregunta.
items.en: Compare the three texts only when two seem to fit the same question.
items.note: refinement strategy

activities.title: Estrategia de la tarea 3
activities.intro: Practise the reading task 3 strategy and format.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuántos textos hay en la tarea tres de lectura?
questions.explanation: task three always presents exactly three texts.

questions.prompt: ¿A cuántos textos corresponde cada pregunta de la tarea tres?
options: A los tres a la vez
questions.explanation: every question matches exactly one of the three texts.

questions.prompt: Cada texto de la tarea tres tiene entre cien y ciento ___ palabras.
questions.explanation: the range is 100 to 120 words per text.
