questions.prompt: Busco al candidato que ___ (tener) experiencia en ventas.
questions.explanation: an unspecified, still-to-be-found candidate takes the subjunctive in the relative clause.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Underline the detail each question is looking for before reading.'
questions.explanation: antes de leer places the underlining step before you start reading the texts.

activities.title: Practicando la tarea 3
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk through your approach to matching information across three texts.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: En la tarea tres hay tres textos, ¿verdad? Se me mezclan un poco.
lines.en: In task three there are three texts, right? They get a bit mixed up for me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, por eso subrayo el dato que busca cada pregunta antes de leer nada.
lines.en: Yes, that's why I underline the detail each question is looking for before reading anything.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y si dos textos parecen encajar con la misma pregunta?
lines.en: And if two texts seem to fit the same question?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Entonces los comparo con más cuidado, solo en ese caso.
lines.en: Then I compare them more carefully, only in that case.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tipo de textos suelen aparecer?
lines.en: What kind of texts usually appear?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Anécdotas, biografías, ofertas de trabajo o guías de viaje.
lines.en: Anecdotes, biographies, job adverts or travel guides.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cada pregunta corresponde a un solo texto?
lines.en: Does each question correspond to a single text?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, nunca a los tres a la vez, eso ya lo sé por experiencia.
lines.en: Yes, never all three at once, I already know that from experience.

days.title: Lectura, tarea 4: reconstruir el texto
days.objective: Reconstruct a text by fitting short removed statements back into the gaps, using cohesion clues like connectors and pronoun reference.
days.paretoFocus: This task directly rewards the cohesion skills already practised, so recognising a connector or a pronoun that only fits one gap is the fastest route to full marks.
drills: Read a short text with one sentence removed.
Choose which of three candidate sentences fits the gap.
Explain your choice using a connector or a pronoun clue.

items: Recall three discourse connectors that link two sentences.
Say a sentence where a pronoun refers back to something mentioned earlier.
Explain why paragraphing matters for a written text.

activities.title: Reconstruir el texto
activities.intro: Task four removes six fragments from a text and offers eight candidates to fill the gaps. Connectors and pronouns at the start of a fragment are the clues that reveal where each one belongs.

items.hr: La tarea cuatro quita seis fragmentos de un texto y ofrece ocho para completar los huecos.
items.en: Task four removes six fragments from a text and offers eight to fill the gaps.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Fíjate en los conectores al principio de cada fragmento: además, sin embargo, por eso.
items.en: Look at the connectors at the start of each fragment: also, however, therefore.
items.note: strategy

items.hr: Un pronombre como 'esto' o 'ella' solo encaja si el hueco anterior lo explica.
items.en: A pronoun like 'this' or 'she' only fits if the previous gap explains it.
items.note: reference-tracking strategy

items.hr: Lee el texto entero primero, sin los fragmentos, para entender el hilo general.
items.en: Read the whole text first, without the fragments, to understand the general thread.
items.note: strategy

items.hr: Sobran siempre dos fragmentos que no encajan en ningún hueco.
items.en: There are always two fragments left over that don't fit any gap.
items.note: exam-format warning

activities.title: Estrategia de la tarea 4
activities.intro: Practise the reading task 4 strategy and format.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué hay que hacer en la tarea cuatro de lectura?
options: Devolver fragmentos quitados a su lugar en el texto
Elegir la opción correcta de un menú desplegable
Relacionar enunciados con seis textos breves
Contestar preguntas sobre un solo texto largo
questions.answer: Devolver fragmentos quitados a su lugar en el texto
questions.explanation: task four is specifically about restoring removed fragments to their gaps.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué pista ayuda más a encajar un fragmento en su hueco?
options: Los conectores y los pronombres de referencia
El número de palabras del fragmento
questions.answer: Los conectores y los pronombres de referencia
questions.explanation: connectors and pronouns reveal how a fragment links to what comes before or after.

questions.prompt: Siempre ___ (sobrar) dos fragmentos que no encajan en ningún hueco.
questions.explanation: sobrar agrees with the plural dos fragmentos: two fragments are always left unused.

questions.prompt: ___, el texto quedó mucho más claro después de reorganizarlo.
questions.explanation: en resumen closes an explanation with a summary.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Read the whole text first, without the fragments.'
questions.explanation: primero orders this step before working on the gaps.

activities.title: Practicando la tarea 4
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk through your approach to reconstructing a gapped text.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: La tarea cuatro me cuesta, no sé por dónde empezar.
lines.en: Task four is hard for me, I don't know where to start.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Yo primero leo el texto entero sin los fragmentos, para pillar el hilo.
lines.en: I first read the whole text without the fragments, to get the thread.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y después cómo decides dónde va cada fragmento?
lines.en: And then how do you decide where each fragment goes?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Miro los conectores al principio: además, sin embargo, por eso.
lines.en: I look at the connectors at the start: also, however, therefore.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y los pronombres también ayudan?
lines.en: Do pronouns help too?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, si un fragmento empieza con 'ella' busco a quién se refiere antes.
lines.en: Yes, if a fragment starts with 'she' I look for who it refers to earlier.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Sobra siempre algún fragmento?
lines.en: Is there always a fragment left over?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, dan ocho fragmentos para seis huecos, así que siempre sobran dos; no te obsesiones con usarlos todos.
lines.en: Yes, they give you eight fragments for six gaps, so two are always left over; don't obsess over using them all.

days.title: Lectura, tarea 5: el texto con huecos
days.objective: Complete a cloze text by choosing the option that fits grammatically and in meaning at each of the gaps.
days.paretoFocus: The cloze tests grammar in context rather than isolated rules, so reading a full sentence around each gap is faster and safer than reading the gap alone.
drills: Read a short cloze text with three gaps.
Choose the best option for each gap from three choices.
Reread the completed text aloud to check it sounds natural.

items: Recall the rule for choosing between ser and estar with an adjective that changes meaning.
Say a sentence using aunque with the indicative for a known fact.
Explain why reading a full sentence is safer than reading only the gap.

activities.title: El texto con huecos
activities.intro: Task five is a cloze: a text with several gaps and three options for each one. Some gaps test a grammar word, others test vocabulary, and both are best solved by reading the whole sentence around the gap.

items.hr: La tarea cinco es un texto con varios huecos y tres opciones para cada uno.
items.en: Task five is a text with several gaps and three options for each one.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Algunos huecos piden una palabra gramatical: una preposición, un pronombre, un conector.
items.en: Some gaps ask for a grammar word: a preposition, a pronoun, a connector.
items.note: gap type 1

items.hr: Otros huecos piden el vocabulario que mejor encaja en el significado.
items.en: Other gaps ask for the vocabulary that best fits the meaning.
items.note: gap type 2

items.hr: Lee la frase completa, no solo el hueco, antes de elegir.
items.en: Read the whole sentence, not just the gap, before choosing.
items.note: strategy

items.hr: Si dudas entre dos opciones, elige la que suena más natural en el contexto.
items.en: If you're unsure between two options, choose the one that sounds most natural in context.
items.note: tiebreaker strategy

activities.title: Estrategia de la tarea 5
activities.intro: Practise the reading task 5 strategy and format.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuántas opciones hay para cada hueco en la tarea cinco?
questions.explanation: every gap in the cloze offers exactly three options.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué tipo de palabra puede pedir un hueco de la tarea cinco?
options: Una preposición, un pronombre o un conector
questions.answer: Una preposición, un pronombre o un conector
questions.explanation: grammar-word gaps in the cloze can test any of these categories.

questions.prompt: Antes de elegir, lee la frase ___, no solo el hueco.
questions.explanation: reading the whole sentence gives you the context the gap alone cannot.

questions.prompt: Este ejercicio es ___ practicar la gramática en contexto.
questions.explanation: para introduces the purpose of the exercise.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Choose the option that sounds most natural in context.'
questions.explanation: que suena más natural introduces the relative clause describing the right option.

activities.title: Practicando la tarea 5
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk through your approach to the cloze text.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué tal se te da la tarea cinco, la de los huecos?
lines.en: How are you doing with task five, the gap-fill one?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bien, aunque algunos huecos piden vocabulario y ahí dudo más.
lines.en: Well, although some gaps ask for vocabulary and I hesitate more there.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Lees la frase entera o solo miras el hueco?
lines.en: Do you read the whole sentence or just look at the gap?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Siempre la frase entera, si no, es fácil confundirse.
lines.en: Always the whole sentence, otherwise it's easy to get confused.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y si dudas entre dos opciones?
lines.en: And if you're unsure between two options?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Elijo la que suena más natural en el contexto.
lines.en: I choose the one that sounds most natural in context.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Hay muchos huecos de gramática pura, como preposiciones?
lines.en: Are there many purely grammatical gaps, like prepositions?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, varios, y esos suelen ser los más rápidos de resolver.
lines.en: Yes, several, and those tend to be the quickest to solve.

days.title: Auditiva, tareas 1 y 4: monólogos y conversaciones breves
days.objective: Apply listening strategies for task 1 (six short monologues) and task 4 (six informal exchanges on one theme) by reading the options before the audio starts.
days.paretoFocus: Both tasks give you the questions before you hear anything, so pre-reading them is free preparation time that most candidates waste.
drills: Read six short invented statements before imagining the audio.
Predict what kind of text will answer each one.
Note who is speaking in an informal exchange you imagine.

items: Recall the future of probability and what it expresses.
Say a sentence reporting a question someone asked you.
Explain why pre-reading the options before listening saves time.

activities.title: Monólogos y conversaciones breves
activities.intro: These two listening tasks share one trait that rewards preparation: the printed questions sit in front of you well before the recording begins, so whatever those extra seconds buy you is time the audio itself won't hand back.

items.hr: La tarea uno de auditiva son seis monólogos breves, de cuarenta a sesenta palabras cada uno.
items.en: Listening task one is six short monologues, forty to sixty words each.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: La tarea cuatro son seis intercambios informales sobre un mismo tema, de cincuenta a setenta palabras.
items.en: Task four is six informal exchanges on the same theme, fifty to seventy words.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Lee las opciones antes de que empiece el audio, mientras puedes.
items.en: Read the options before the audio starts, while you can.
items.note: strategy

items.hr: En la tarea cuatro, fíjate en quién dice cada frase, no solo en el tema.
items.en: In task four, pay attention to who says each line, not just the topic.
items.note: strategy specific to task 4

items.hr: Cada monólogo o intercambio se escucha dos veces.
items.en: Each monologue or exchange is heard twice.
items.note: exam-format fact, true of every recording in the listening paper; answer on the first hearing and check on the second

activities.title: Estrategia de las tareas 1 y 4
activities.intro: Practise the listening strategy for the short recorded texts.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuántos monólogos hay en la tarea uno de auditiva?
questions.explanation: listening task one always contains six short monologues.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué tienen en común los seis intercambios de la tarea cuatro?
questions.explanation: task four's six exchanges share one theme with different speakers.

questions.prompt: Los monólogos de la tarea uno duran de cuarenta a ___ palabras.
questions.explanation: the range is 40 to 60 words per monologue.

questions.prompt: No sé quién habla, ___ (ser, futuro) un cliente del hotel.
questions.explanation: the future here expresses probability about the present, not a real future event.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Each monologue is heard twice.'
questions.explanation: se escucha, passive se, plus dos veces states the repetition fact.

activities.title: Practicando las tareas 1 y 4
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk through your approach to the short listening tasks.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué haces mientras esperas a que empiece el audio de la tarea uno?
lines.en: What do you do while you wait for the task one audio to start?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Leo las opciones rápido, así ya sé qué buscar cuando empiece.
lines.en: I read the options quickly, so I already know what to listen for when it starts.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y en la tarea cuatro, con los intercambios informales?
lines.en: And in task four, with the informal exchanges?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ahí me fijo en quién dice cada frase, porque hay varias voces sobre el mismo tema.
lines.en: There I pay attention to who says each line, because there are several voices on the same theme.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Se repite el audio en algún momento?
lines.en: Does the audio repeat at any point?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, cada audio se escucha dos veces, pero conviene responder ya en la primera escucha.
lines.en: Yes, each audio is heard twice, but it's best to answer on the first listen already.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te da tiempo a tomar notas?
lines.en: Do you have time to take notes?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Un poco, apunto solo una palabra clave por opción.
lines.en: A little, I only jot down one key word per option.

days.title: Auditiva, tarea 2: el monólogo largo
days.objective: Follow a single 400-to-450-word sustained personal monologue and answer three-option questions about it in order.
days.paretoFocus: The questions in task 2 follow the order of the monologue, so tracking your place as you listen is the single most effective technique.
drills: Outline a five-point personal story in the order you'd tell it.
Write three questions in the order they'd appear about that story.
Practise answering them in that same order.

items: Recall the pluscuamperfecto and what it expresses relative to another past event.
Say a sentence using mientras to describe two simultaneous actions.
Explain why tracking the question order helps during a long listening text.

activities.title: El monólogo largo
activities.intro: Task two is a single sustained personal monologue, 400 to 450 words, played twice. Because the questions follow the order of the information in the audio, tracking your place as you listen is the key skill.

items.hr: La tarea dos es un monólogo personal de cuatrocientas a cuatrocientas cincuenta palabras.
items.en: Task two is a personal monologue of four hundred to four hundred fifty words.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Las preguntas siguen el mismo orden que la información en el audio.
items.en: The questions follow the same order as the information in the audio.
items.note: strategy

items.hr: Mientras escuchas, ve tachando mentalmente la pregunta que ya has contestado.
items.en: As you listen, mentally cross off the question you've already answered.
items.note: strategy

items.hr: Si te pierdes un momento, sigue escuchando: la siguiente pregunta llegará pronto.
items.en: If you lose track for a moment, keep listening: the next question will come soon.
items.note: reassurance strategy

items.hr: El monólogo se reproduce dos veces.
items.en: The monologue is played twice.
items.note: exam-format fact; every recording in the listening paper plays twice

activities.title: Estrategia de la tarea 2
activities.intro: Practise the listening task 2 strategy and format.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuántas veces se reproduce el monólogo de la tarea dos?
questions.explanation: like every recording in the listening paper, the long monologue is played twice.

questions.prompt: ¿En qué orden aparecen las preguntas respecto al audio?
options: En el mismo orden que la información del audio
questions.answer: En el mismo orden que la información del audio
questions.explanation: the questions track the monologue in the order the speaker gives the information.

questions.prompt: El monólogo de la tarea dos tiene de cuatrocientas a cuatrocientas ___ palabras.
questions.explanation: the range is 400 to 450 words.

questions.prompt: El hablante contó que ya ___ (viajar, pluscuamperfecto) a varios países antes de mudarse.
questions.explanation: the pluscuamperfecto marks an event completed before another past event, the move.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The monologue is played twice.'
questions.explanation: se reproduce, passive se, plus dos veces states the format fact.

activities.title: Practicando la tarea 2
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk through your approach to the long personal monologue.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: La tarea dos es la que más me cuesta, es un monólogo larguísimo.
lines.en: Task two is the one I struggle with most, it's a really long monologue.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A mí me ayuda saber que las preguntas siguen el mismo orden que el audio.
lines.en: It helps me to know that the questions follow the same order as the audio.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y si te pierdes en algún momento?
lines.en: And if you lose track at some point?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sigo escuchando, la siguiente pregunta llega pronto de todas formas.
lines.en: I keep listening, the next question comes soon anyway.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Se escucha una sola vez, o la repiten?
lines.en: Is it heard only once, or do they repeat it?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Se reproduce dos veces, como todos los audios de la prueba, y eso ayuda bastante.
lines.en: It's played twice, like every recording in the paper, and that helps quite a lot.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Tomas notas mientras escuchas?
lines.en: Do you take notes while listening?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, voy tachando mentalmente cada pregunta que ya he contestado.
lines.en: Yes, I mentally cross off each question I've already answered.

days.title: Auditiva, tarea 3: el informativo de seis noticias
days.objective: Follow a news programme carrying six separate items in 350 to 400 words total, keeping each item's topic separate from the next.
days.paretoFocus: The six items change topic quickly with almost no pause, so the real skill is resetting attention fast rather than understanding any single item deeply.
drills: List six invented headlines for a short news programme.
Write one sentence per headline, under seventy words each.
Practise moving from one headline to the next without pausing.

items: Recall an impersonal expression using se or dicen que.
Say a sentence describing a change using ponerse or volverse.
Explain why it helps to let go of a difficult item quickly in a fast-changing recording.

activities.title: El informativo de seis noticias
activities.intro: Task three is a short radio or TV news programme made of six separate items. Because DELE B1 draws on every variety of Spanish, the presenter's accent or a news item's origin may be Latin American rather than peninsular, labelled where it matters; the task itself works the same way regardless.

items.hr: La tarea tres es un informativo de radio o televisión con seis noticias.
items.en: Task three is a radio or TV news programme with six news items.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: En total, el informativo tiene entre trescientas cincuenta y cuatrocientas palabras.
items.en: In total, the programme has between three hundred fifty and four hundred words.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Cada noticia cambia de tema, así que hay que soltar la anterior rápido.
items.en: Each news item changes topic, so you have to let go of the previous one quickly.
items.note: strategy

items.hr: El presentador suele anunciar el tema al principio de cada noticia.
items.en: The presenter usually announces the topic at the start of each item.
items.note: strategy, listen for the opening line

items.hr: No te quedes pensando en una noticia difícil: la siguiente ya ha empezado.
items.en: Don't dwell on a difficult item: the next one has already started.
items.note: pacing warning

activities.title: Estrategia de la tarea 3
activities.intro: Practise the listening task 3 strategy and format.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuántas noticias tiene el informativo de la tarea tres?
questions.explanation: the news programme in task three always carries six items.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es el mayor peligro al escuchar la tarea tres?
options: Quedarse pensando en una noticia y perderse la siguiente
Que el informativo dure demasiado poco
questions.answer: Quedarse pensando en una noticia y perderse la siguiente
questions.explanation: dwelling on one item risks missing the start of the next, since they follow quickly.

questions.prompt: El informativo completo tiene entre trescientas cincuenta y ___ palabras.
questions.explanation: the total length is 350 to 400 words.

questions.prompt: ___ dice que va a llover este fin de semana en el norte.
questions.explanation: se dice que is the impersonal way to report what people say.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The presenter usually announces the topic at the start of each item.'
questions.explanation: soler plus infinitive expresses what usually happens.

activities.title: Practicando la tarea 3
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk through your approach to the fast-moving news programme.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cómo llevas la tarea tres, la del informativo?
lines.en: How are you doing with task three, the news one?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Regular, con seis noticias seguidas es fácil perderse.
lines.en: So-so, with six news items in a row it's easy to lose track.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué haces cuando una noticia te resulta difícil?
lines.en: What do you do when a news item is difficult for you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Intento no quedarme pensando en ella, porque la siguiente ya ha empezado.
lines.en: I try not to dwell on it, because the next one has already started.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te ayuda algo para saber cuándo cambia el tema?
lines.en: Does anything help you know when the topic changes?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, el presentador suele anunciar el tema al principio de cada noticia.
lines.en: Yes, the presenter usually announces the topic at the start of each item.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Cuánto dura en total el informativo?
lines.en: How long does the programme last in total?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Entre trescientas cincuenta y cuatrocientas palabras en total, así que no es tan largo.
lines.en: Between three hundred fifty and four hundred words in total, so it's not that long.

days.title: Auditiva, tarea 5: la conversación entre dos personas
days.objective: Follow a conversation between two people, distinguishing each speaker's opinion and identifying where they agree and disagree.
days.paretoFocus: This task tests tracking two viewpoints at once, and confusing who said what is the single most common way candidates lose points here.
drills: Write a short two-person conversation where they disagree on one point.
Label each line A or B by speaker.
Write one question that could only be answered by re-reading who said what.

items: Recall a verb that takes a fixed preposition, like depender de or contar con.
Say a sentence expressing agreement or disagreement with an opinion.
Explain why one option might describe only one speaker's opinion rather than both.

activities.title: La conversación entre dos personas
activities.intro: Two voices sharing one recording means two things to track at once: whose turn it is to speak, and whether what they just said lines up with or pushes back on what came before. One of those voices may carry a Latin American accent or turn of phrase, since DELE B1 material draws on every variety of Spanish; that's never a sign anything is wrong.

items.hr: La tarea cinco es una conversación entre dos personas sobre un mismo tema.
items.en: Task five is a conversation between two people on the same topic.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Identifica pronto quién es cada voz: por el tono, o porque el audio los presenta.
items.en: Identify each voice early: by the tone, or because the audio introduces them.
items.note: strategy

items.hr: Presta atención a en qué están de acuerdo y en qué no.
items.en: Pay attention to what they agree on and what they don't.
items.note: strategy

items.hr: Una opción puede describir la opinión de uno, no la de los dos.
items.en: One option may describe one person's opinion, not both.
items.note: warning about distractors

items.hr: Anota con una letra, A o B, de quién es cada idea mientras escuchas.
items.en: Note down with a letter, A or B, whose idea each one is as you listen.
items.note: note-taking strategy

activities.title: Estrategia de la tarea 5
activities.intro: Practise the listening task 5 strategy and format.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuántas personas hablan en la tarea cinco de auditiva?
questions.explanation: task five always presents a conversation between exactly two people.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué hay que identificar con cuidado en esta tarea?
options: El número de palabras del audio
questions.explanation: the main risk is attributing an opinion to the wrong speaker.

questions.prompt: Una opción puede describir la opinión de ___ persona, no la de las dos.
questions.explanation: a distractor often isolates only one speaker's view.

questions.prompt: Los dos hablantes no ___ (estar) de acuerdo con la propuesta.
questions.explanation: estar de acuerdo con is the fixed expression for agreeing with something.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Pay attention to what they agree on and what they don't.'
questions.explanation: presta atención a introduces the two things to track, marked by en qué.

activities.title: Practicando la tarea 5
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Talk through your approach to a two-speaker conversation.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: En la tarea cinco, ¿te cuesta distinguir a los dos hablantes?
lines.en: In task five, do you find it hard to tell the two speakers apart?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Al principio sí, pero intento identificar el tono de cada voz enseguida.
lines.en: At first yes, but I try to identify each voice's tone right away.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y cómo sabes en qué están de acuerdo?
lines.en: And how do you know what they agree on?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Voy anotando con una letra, A o B, de quién es cada idea.
lines.en: I note down with a letter, A or B, whose idea each one is.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Alguna vez una opción describe solo la opinión de uno?
lines.en: Does an option ever describe only one person's opinion?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, por eso hay que tener cuidado y no asumir que es de los dos.
lines.en: Yes, that's why you have to be careful and not assume it's both of theirs.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Es la última tarea del examen de auditiva?
lines.en: Is it the last task in the listening exam?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, y después ya solo quedan las pruebas escritas y orales.
lines.en: Yes, and after that only the written and oral papers remain.

days.title: En condiciones de examen
days.objective: State the timing of each DELE B1 prueba from memory and explain the grouped pass rule accurately: at least 30 of 50 points in each of two groups.
days.paretoFocus: Misunderstanding the pass rule leads to the wrong revision priorities, and this is the single fact about the exam most worth getting exactly right before test day.
drills: Time yourself reading a text for exactly seventy minutes worth of practice pacing.
State the pass rule out loud in your own words.
Identify which of your four skills is currently your weakest.

items: Recall the conditional used for giving advice.
Say a sentence explaining a plan using pensar plus infinitive.
Explain why a modular section-by-section pass rule would be different from a grouped one.

activities.title: Tiempos y regla de aprobado
activities.intro: Four separate scores don't stand alone here: they're bundled two at a time, and a strong score in one paper can rescue a weak one in its own bundle, but nothing crosses over to rescue the other bundle. Knowing which paper sits in which bundle changes how you'd actually spend a limited number of revision hours.

items.hr: Comprensión de lectura dura setenta minutos, con cinco tareas y treinta ítems.
items.en: Reading comprehension lasts seventy minutes, with five tasks and thirty items.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Comprensión auditiva dura cuarenta minutos, con cinco tareas y treinta ítems.
items.en: Listening comprehension lasts forty minutes, with five tasks and thirty items.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Expresión e interacción escritas dura sesenta minutos, con dos tareas.
items.en: Written expression and interaction lasts sixty minutes, with two tasks.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: Expresión e interacción orales dura quince minutos, más otros quince de preparación, con cuatro tareas.
items.en: Oral expression and interaction lasts fifteen minutes, plus another fifteen of preparation, with four tasks.
items.note: exam fact

items.hr: El grupo uno es lectura más escritura; el grupo dos, auditiva más orales; hace falta treinta de cincuenta en cada uno.
items.en: Group one is reading plus writing; group two, listening plus speaking; you need thirty out of fifty in each one.
items.note: the pass rule stated precisely

activities.title: La regla de aprobado
activities.intro: Practise the exam timings and the grouped pass rule.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuánto dura la prueba de comprensión de lectura en el DELE B1?
questions.explanation: reading comprehension is the longest prueba, at seventy minutes.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estas frases describe correctamente la regla de aprobado?
options: Hace falta al menos treinta de cincuenta puntos en cada uno de los dos grupos.
Hace falta un sesenta por ciento de media entre las cuatro pruebas.
Hace falta aprobar cada prueba por separado con un mínimo del sesenta por ciento.
Basta con superar el sesenta por ciento en total, sin importar cómo se reparta.
questions.answer: Hace falta al menos treinta de cincuenta puntos en cada uno de los dos grupos.
questions.explanation: the rule is grouped and per-group, not a global average and not a per-section floor.

questions.prompt: El grupo uno junta la comprensión de lectura con la expresión ___.
questions.explanation: grupo 1 pairs reading comprehension with written expression.

questions.prompt: Yo en tu lugar, ___ (repasar, condicional) primero el grupo que tienes más flojo.
questions.explanation: the conditional simple is used to give advice, yo en tu lugar plus the conditional.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'You need thirty out of fifty points in each group.'
questions.explanation: hace falta introduces the requirement, treinta de cincuenta the threshold.

activities.title: Repasando las reglas del examen
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Explain the exam timings and the grouped pass rule to a study partner.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Sabes cuánto dura cada prueba del examen B1?
lines.en: Do you know how long each B1 exam paper lasts?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, lectura son setenta minutos y auditiva, cuarenta.
lines.en: Yes, reading is seventy minutes and listening, forty.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y las pruebas escritas y orales?
lines.en: And the written and oral papers?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Escritas, sesenta minutos; orales, quince más quince de preparación.
lines.en: Written, sixty minutes; oral, fifteen plus fifteen of preparation.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Entonces basta con sacar un sesenta por ciento de media entre todo?
lines.en: So is it enough to get sixty percent on average across everything?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, eso es un error común. Hay dos grupos, y hay que sacar treinta de cincuenta en cada uno.
lines.en: No, that's a common mistake. There are two groups, and you need thirty out of fifty in each one.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: O sea que si voy fatal en auditiva, no lo salva la lectura.
lines.en: So if I do terribly in listening, reading doesn't save it.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exacto, la oral sí puede salvar a la auditiva dentro del mismo grupo, pero un grupo entero flojo no lo salva el otro.
lines.en: Exactly, speaking can save listening within the same group, but a whole weak group isn't saved by the other.

days.title: Indicativo o subjuntivo: el procedimiento completo
days.objective: Decide between the indicative and the present subjunctive in noun, adjective and adverbial clauses using one consistent procedure.
days.paretoFocus: This is the single decision that governs the largest grammar system in the course, and having one procedure instead of a list of exceptions is what makes it usable in real time.
drills: Write one example each of a noun, adjective and adverbial clause needing the subjunctive.
Say the one-question test you use to decide indicative or subjunctive.
Check each example against that test.

items: Recall an example of the present subjunctive after a wish.
Say a sentence with a relative clause whose antecedent may not exist.
Explain why cuando plus subjunctive is required for a future time clause.

activities.title: Una sola pregunta, tres tipos de oración
activities.intro: Three grammar chapters that looked unrelated when you learned them apart turn out to hinge on the exact same question, whether what's being described is settled fact or still up in the air. Nothing new gets introduced here, just the single thread that was tying those chapters together all along.

items.hr: En una oración sustantiva, el subjuntivo aparece cuando hay dos sujetos y el verbo principal expresa voluntad, duda o sentimiento.
items.en: In a noun clause, the subjunctive appears when there are two subjects and the main verb expresses will, doubt or feeling.
items.note: rule for noun clauses

items.hr: En una oración de relativo, el subjuntivo aparece cuando el antecedente no existe o no es concreto: 'busco un piso que tenga terraza'.
items.en: In a relative clause, the subjunctive appears when the antecedent doesn't exist or isn't specific.
items.note: rule for adjective clauses

items.hr: En una oración adverbial, el subjuntivo aparece con lo aún no realizado: 'cuando llegues', 'para que puedas', 'aunque llueva' si es una concesión hipotética.
items.en: In an adverbial clause, the subjunctive appears with what is not yet realised.
items.note: rule for adverbial clauses

items.hr: La pregunta útil siempre es la misma: ¿el hecho ya es real y conocido, o todavía no?
items.en: The useful question is always the same: is the fact already real and known, or not yet?
items.note: the unifying decision procedure

items.hr: Creo que llueve frente a no creo que llueva; aunque llueve frente a aunque llueva.
items.en: I think it's raining versus I don't think it's raining; even though it's raining versus even if it rains.
items.note: a minimal pair across two categories at once

activities.title: Aplicar el procedimiento
activities.intro: Run each sentence through the one-question test before picking a mood, no matter which of the three clause types it turns out to be.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué pregunta ayuda a decidir entre indicativo y subjuntivo en cualquier tipo de oración?
options: ¿El hecho ya es real y conocido, o todavía no?
questions.answer: ¿El hecho ya es real y conocido, o todavía no?
questions.explanation: this single question applies across noun, adjective and adverbial clauses alike.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estas frases usa correctamente el subjuntivo en una oración de relativo?
options: Busco un piso que tenga terraza.
Tengo un piso que tenga terraza.
Busco el piso que tiene terraza y no lo encuentro.
Vivo en un piso que tenga terraza.
questions.answer: Busco un piso que tenga terraza.
questions.explanation: only an antecedent that may not exist, an unfound flat, takes the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Aunque ___ (llover, hecho conocido), salimos a pasear de todas formas.
questions.explanation: a known, observed fact after aunque takes the indicative.

questions.prompt: Aunque ___ (llover, concesión hipotética) mañana, saldremos igual.
questions.explanation: an unknown future possibility after aunque takes the present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'It is important that you arrive on time.'
questions.explanation: A value judgement in the main clause puts the subordinate clause in the present subjunctive, and the two clauses have different subjects, so que is required rather than an infinitive.

activities.title: El procedimiento en la práctica
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Explain the one-question test for indicative versus subjunctive to a classmate.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Todavía me lío con el indicativo y el subjuntivo a veces.
lines.en: I still get confused with the indicative and the subjunctive sometimes.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A mí me ayuda una sola pregunta: ¿el hecho ya es real, o todavía no?
lines.en: One single question helps me: is the fact already real, or not yet?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y eso vale para los tres tipos de oración?
lines.en: And does that work for all three types of clause?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, para las sustantivas, las de relativo y las adverbiales, siempre la misma lógica.
lines.en: Yes, for noun, relative and adverbial clauses, always the same logic.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ponme un ejemplo con 'aunque'.
lines.en: Give me an example with 'aunque'.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Aunque llueve, si ya lo sé; aunque llueva, si no lo sé todavía.
lines.en: Even though it's raining, if I already know it; even if it rains, if I don't know yet.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Ah, ¿y con un piso que busco pero no existe todavía?
lines.en: Ah, and with a flat I'm looking for but that doesn't exist yet?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Exacto: busco un piso que tenga terraza, porque no sé si existe ese piso.
lines.en: Exactly: I'm looking for a flat that has a terrace, because I don't know if that flat exists.

days.title: Vocabulario y registro: repaso final
days.objective: Choose the right register, formal or informal, for a given situation and recall high-value B1 vocabulary across the course's themes.
days.paretoFocus: Register mismatches read as more foreign than a grammar mistake, so this is a cheap, high-impact final check.
drills: List five informal words and their formal equivalents.
Write one sentence in each register about the same topic.
Compare the two and note what changed besides the vocabulary.

items: Recall a formal opening and its informal equivalent.
Say a sentence using a diminutive appropriately.
Explain why register matters as much as grammar in a formal letter.

activities.title: Registro formal e informal
activities.intro: The same idea can be said in an informal or a formal register, and choosing the wrong one for the situation is a common, avoidable mistake. Before writing, decide who you are addressing and what they expect.

items.hr: 'Currar' es informal para trabajar; en un correo formal se dice simplemente 'trabajar'.
items.en: 'Currar' is informal for 'to work'; in a formal email you just say 'trabajar'.
items.note: register pair

items.hr: 'Un montón de' es informal para 'mucho'; en un texto formal se prefiere 'numerosos' o 'una gran cantidad de'.
items.en: 'Un montón de' is informal for 'a lot of'; in a formal text 'numerosos' or 'a great quantity of' is preferred.
items.note: register pair

items.hr: El vocabulario de trámites (solicitud, plazo, contrato, requisito) aparece en textos formales y laborales.
items.en: Paperwork vocabulary (application, deadline, contract, requirement) appears in formal and work texts.
items.note: thematic vocabulary recall

items.hr: El vocabulario de opinión (a mi parecer, desde mi punto de vista, no cabe duda de que) sirve para redacciones y conversaciones.
items.en: Opinion vocabulary (in my view, from my point of view, there's no doubt that) is useful for compositions and conversations.
items.note: functional vocabulary

items.hr: Antes de escribir, pregúntate: ¿a quién le escribo, y qué registro espera de mí?
items.en: Before writing, ask yourself: who am I writing to, and what register do they expect from me?
items.note: the consolidating strategy

activities.title: Elegir el registro adecuado
activities.intro: Practise recognising and choosing formal and informal vocabulary.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estas palabras es informal?
questions.explanation: currar is the everyday informal word for trabajar.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué expresión es más adecuada para una redacción formal de opinión?
questions.explanation: the other options are too colloquial for a formal composition.

questions.prompt: En un correo formal, en vez de 'un montón de gente', se dice 'una gran ___ de gente'.
questions.explanation: una gran cantidad de is the formal equivalent of un montón de.

questions.prompt: Con los años, aquel barrio ___ (convertirse) en una zona muy cara.
questions.explanation: convertirse en describes a completed change, so it takes the indefinido here.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Before writing, ask yourself who you're writing to.'
questions.explanation: antes de plus the infinitive introduces the step before the main action.

activities.title: Corrigiendo el registro
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Fix a draft that mixed up formal and informal register.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Le escribiste 'tío' al director del centro en el correo, ¿en serio?
lines.en: You wrote 'dude' to the centre director in the email, seriously?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Uy, no, eso fue un borrador informal, ahora lo cambio al registro formal.
lines.en: Oh no, that was an informal draft, I'll change it to the formal register now.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué vocabulario usas normalmente para un texto formal?
lines.en: What vocabulary do you normally use for a formal text?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Palabras como solicitud, plazo o requisito, nada de 'currar' ni 'un montón de'.
lines.en: Words like application, deadline or requirement, nothing like 'currar' or 'un montón de'.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y para dar tu opinión en una redacción?
lines.en: And to give your opinion in a composition?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Uso 'desde mi punto de vista' o 'no cabe duda de que', en vez de 'yo qué sé'.
lines.en: I use 'from my point of view' or 'there's no doubt that', instead of 'I don't know, whatever'.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Buena estrategia. ¿Siempre te preguntas el registro antes de escribir?
lines.en: Good strategy. Do you always ask yourself about the register before writing?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, siempre pienso a quién le escribo y qué espera de mí.
lines.en: Yes, I always think about who I'm writing to and what they expect from me.

days.title: El B1 en miniatura: cierre del curso
days.objective: Summarise everything the course now allows the learner to do at B1 and prepare for the B1 quiz and the B1 mock exam.
days.paretoFocus: A clear sense of what you can now do is what turns a long course into confidence on exam day, and previewing the mock's shape removes the biggest source of exam-day surprise.
drills: Write a two-sentence summary of what you can now do in Spanish.
List the two writing tasks and their exact word counts from memory.
State the pass rule in one sentence, without saying '60 percent overall.'

items: Recall how to write both DELE B1 writing tasks to the correct length.
Say a sentence using the present subjunctive after a value judgement.
Explain the grouped pass rule in your own words.

activities.title: Lo que ya sabes hacer
activities.intro: Every rule from here back to day one adds up to this single moment: a level-appropriate list of what used to be unreachable and now isn't, right before that list gets tested for real.

items.hr: Ahora sabes formar y usar el futuro, el condicional y el pluscuamperfecto sin dudar.
items.en: You can now form and use the future, the conditional and the pluperfect without hesitating.
items.note: recap

items.hr: Sabes cuándo usar el subjuntivo presente: con deseo, duda, valoración, y en cláusulas de tiempo, finalidad y concesión.
items.en: You know when to use the present subjunctive: with wish, doubt, value judgement, and in time, purpose and concession clauses.
items.note: recap

items.hr: Sabes narrar una vida entera combinando los cuatro tiempos del pasado y contar lo que alguien dijo con el cambio de tiempo verbal.
items.en: You can narrate a whole life combining the four past tenses and report what someone said with the tense shift.
items.note: recap

items.hr: Sabes escribir un correo informal de cien a ciento veinte palabras y una redacción de opinión de ciento treinta a ciento cincuenta.
items.en: You can write an informal email of a hundred to a hundred twenty words and an opinion composition of a hundred thirty to a hundred fifty.
items.note: recap

items.hr: El siguiente paso es el cuestionario de B1 y después el examen simulado completo.
items.en: The next step is the B1 quiz and then the full mock exam.
items.note: what's next

activities.title: Cierre del curso
activities.intro: Consolidate what the course covered and what to do next.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué examen prepara este curso como meta final?
options: Un examen de acceso a la universidad
questions.explanation: the course's finish line is the DELE B1.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estos NO es parte de lo que ya sabes hacer en B1?
options: Un tiempo verbal del nivel siguiente, fuera de este curso
Usar el subjuntivo presente en cláusulas de deseo y duda
Narrar una vida combinando los cuatro tiempos del pasado
Escribir una redacción de opinión de ciento treinta a ciento cincuenta palabras
questions.answer: Un tiempo verbal del nivel siguiente, fuera de este curso
questions.explanation: the course stops at the present subjunctive; a tense reserved for the next level was never taught here.

questions.prompt: El correo informal de la tarea uno tiene de cien a ciento ___ palabras.
questions.explanation: the range for writing task 1 is 100 to 120 words.

questions.prompt: Es importante que ___ (repasar, tú) todo antes del examen simulado.
questions.explanation: a value judgement, es importante que, requires the present subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'The next step is the B1 quiz and then the full mock exam.'
questions.explanation: el siguiente paso es introduces what comes right after this lesson.

activities.title: Antes del examen simulado
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Reflect with a classmate on everything learned before the final quiz and mock exam.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Te das cuenta de todo lo que has aprendido desde el principio del curso?
lines.en: Do you realise everything you've learned since the start of the course?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, la verdad, ahora manejo el futuro, el condicional y todo el subjuntivo presente.
lines.en: Yes, honestly, now I handle the future, the conditional and the whole present subjunctive.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Y te sientes preparado para el examen?
lines.en: And do you feel ready for the exam?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Bastante, sé narrar en pasado, escribir los dos textos con la longitud exacta y entender todas las tareas de cada prueba.
lines.en: Quite ready, I can narrate in the past, write both texts to the exact length and understand all the tasks in each paper.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué te falta hacer ahora?
lines.en: What do you still need to do now?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: El cuestionario de B1 primero, para repasar, y después el examen simulado completo.
lines.en: The B1 quiz first, to review, and then the full mock exam.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Nervioso?
lines.en: Nervous?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Un poco, pero sé exactamente qué esperar en cada prueba, así que estoy tranquilo.
lines.en: A little, but I know exactly what to expect in each paper, so I'm calm.
